title: 個體經濟學 Microeconomics
description:
This course is the first part of a two-semester sequence in intermediate microeconomics, taught in English. The fall semester covers Consumer Theory in depth and introduces the Foundations of Producer Theory. We study how consumers and firms make optimal choices under constraints and how markets aggregate these decisions into equilibrium.
Two analytical pillars—optimization and equilibrium—organize our approach. Comfort with differential calculus, linear functions, and elementary algebra is expected.
objectives:
By the end of the course, students should be able to:
1. Analyze consumer choice using optimization tools (preferences, utility functions, demand derivation, and Slutsky equation).
2. Model intertemporal choice, buying and selling with endowments, and decision-making under uncertainty.
3. Measure consumer surplus, welfare changes, and partial market equilibrium dynamics.
4. Analyze firm behavior and foundations of producer theory (technology, production functions, cost minimization, and cost curves).
5. Apply multivariable calculus to solve structured microeconomic models.
grading:
1. Problem Sets (20%):
- Frequency: 6 problem sets assigned throughout the semester.
- Content: Calculus-based analytical derivations and microeconomic modeling problems.
2. Midterm Examination (40%):
- Format: In-class, written examination (Week 8).
- Scope: Covers material from Weeks 1 through 7 (Consumer Theory, Optimization, Slutsky Equation, Endowments, and Intertemporal Choice).
3. Final Examination (40%):
- Format: In-class, written examination (Week 16).
- Scope: Comprehensive, with a primary focus on Weeks 9 through 15 (Choice Under Uncertainty, Welfare Analysis, Market Demand, and Producer Theory).
prerequisite: [ 經濟學(全學年)(修習且及格)]
weeklyText:
Week 1
Course Topic: Introduction & Mathematical Foundations
Content & Readings: Course overview, mathematical appendix, constrained optimization, and the Lagrange multiplier method. Reading: Varian Ch. 1 & Math Appendix.
Homework: None.
Week 2
Course Topic: Budget Constraint & Consumer Preferences
Content & Readings: Budget line, shifts, trade–offs; preference axioms, indifference curves, and Marginal Rate of Substitution (MRS). Reading: Varian Ch. 2–3.
Homework: Problem Set 1 Assigned.
Week 3
Course Topic: Utility Theory & Utility Maximization (UMP)
Content & Readings: Utility representation, monotonic transformations, solving the Utility Maximization Problem (UMP) via Lagrange. Reading: Varian Ch. 4–5.
Homework: Problem Set 1 Due | Problem Set 2 Assigned.
Week 4
Course Topic: Demand Functions & Revealed Preference
Content & Readings: Deriving Marshallian demand, income/price expansion paths, Engel curves, and Weak Axiom of Revealed Preference (WARP). Reading: Varian Ch. 5–7.
Homework: Problem Set 2 Due.
Week 5
Course Topic: Slutsky Equation & Comparative Statics
Content & Readings: Decomposing price changes into substitution and income effects, Slutsky vs. Hicksian decomposition, Giffen goods. Reading: Varian Ch. 8.
Homework: Problem Set 3 Assigned.
Week 6
Course Topic: Endowments & Labor Supply
Content & Readings: Endowment budget constraints, net vs. gross demand, price changes with endowments, labor supply choice. Reading: Varian Ch. 9.
Homework: None.
Week 7
Course Topic: Intertemporal Choice & Present Value
Content & Readings: Two-period consumption choice, interest rates, present value calculations, inflation, borrowing and lending. Reading: Varian Ch. 10.
Homework: Problem Set 3 Due (Midterm Review).
Week 8
Course Topic: Midterm Examination
Content & Readings: In-Class Midterm Exam (Covers Weeks 1–7 material).
Homework: None.
Week 9
Course Topic: Choice Under Uncertainty
Content & Readings: Contingent consumption, expected utility theory (vNM), risk aversion, risk neutrality, insurance markets. Reading: Varian Ch. 12.
Homework: Problem Set 4 Assigned.
Week 10
Course Topic: Consumer Welfare (CV/EV) & Market Demand
Content & Readings: Measuring welfare changes, Compensating Variation (CV), Equivalent Variation (EV), aggregating individual demand to market demand. Reading: Varian Ch. 14–15.
Homework: Problem Set 4 Due | Problem Set 5 Assigned.
Week 11
Course Topic: Partial Market Equilibrium
Content & Readings: Market equilibrium, producer surplus, deadweight loss, tax incidence, and welfare evaluation. Reading: Varian Ch. 16.
Homework: Problem Set 5 Due.
Week 12
Course Topic: Producer Theory: Technology & Production Functions
Content & Readings: Inputs, technology constraints, marginal product, Technical Rate of Substitution (TRS), returns to scale. Reading: Varian Ch. 19.
Homework: Problem Set 6 Assigned.
Week 13
Course Topic: Producer Theory: Profit Maximization & Factor Demands
Content & Readings: Short-run vs. long-run profit maximization, iso-profit lines, factor demand derivation, profit functions. Reading: Varian Ch. 20.
Homework: None.
Week 14
Course Topic: Producer Theory: Cost Minimization Problem (CMP)
Content & Readings: Solving the Cost Minimization Problem (CMP), conditional factor demand, returns to scale and cost functions. Reading: Varian Ch. 21.
Homework: Problem Set 6 Due.
Week 15
Course Topic: Producer Theory: Short-Run & Long-Run Cost Curves
Content & Readings: Average cost, marginal cost, short-run vs. long-run cost curve relationships, envelope theorem applications. Reading: Varian Ch. 22.
Homework: None (Final Exam Review).
Week 16
Course Topic: Final Examination
Content & Readings: In-Class Final Exam (Comprehensive, with focus on Weeks 9––15).
Homework: None.

title: 個體經濟學 Microeconomics
description: This is a one-year course, with 3-credit per semester, required for students majoring in Economics. This course is designed to introduce to undergraduate students the concepts, theories, and applications of Microeconomics.
objectives:
Through this course, the attempt is made to build in students basic analytical skills that, jointly with skills learned from macroeconomics, will enable them to understand and cope with real-world economic issues. As such, students are encouraged to apply theory to practice and also to reason on the basis of sound Economics theories. Students will organize small groups to read and report, as a team, academic journal papers which demonstrate how microeconomic theories and analytical frameworks are applied to real-world issues.
In addition to the knowledge of Microeconomics theories, the participants will gain experience in doing academic literature reviews and writing-up that summarizes key points and insights of the reviewed academic literature.
In the Fall semester, we will focus on the concepts of optimization and consumer theory from Microeconomics perspectives, while production and cost theories will be introduced in the Spring semester.
A. Lectures:
Fall semester:
Part 0: Introduction to Microeconomics: covering Ch. 1.
Part I: Utility-Maximizing Choice: Consumers, workers, and savers theories: covering Chapters 2 to 10.
Spring semester:
Part II: Profit-Maximizing Choice: Producers (or “Firms”), covering Ch. 11-13.
Part III: Competitive Markets and the “invisible hand”, covering Ch. 14-16.
Part IV: Distortions of the “invisible hand” in Competitive Markets, covering Ch. 18-21.
Part V: Distortions of the “invisible hand” from strategic Decisions, covering Ch. 23-25.
B. Group projects:
Journal papers on consumer-related topics (Fall semester); producer and factor market-related topics (Spring semester).

(1) Final exam: 30%
(2) Homework (through the digital companion platform): 30%

(4) Written report of the group project: 20%

title: 經濟學 Economics
description:
Principle of Economics is a year-long course (3 credits for each semester) that provides an introduction to basic economic principles and methods of economic analysis. The goal of the course is to equip students with basic economic concepts and techniques to apply to daily economic activities and related policy implications.
In the first semester, we concentrate on Microeconomics, the study focuses on the optimizing behavior of individual consumers and firms and the coordination of these individual decisions through markets, including the evaluation of market outcomes. Topics include the theory of the consumer, the theory of the firm, perfect competition, monopoly, monopsony,and oligopoly, markets with asymmetric information, and externalities and public goods.
In the second semester, we concentrate on Macroeconomics, the study of the economy as a whole. Topics include the theory of the determination of national income, employment, prices, and interest rates; related issues of economic growth, fluctuations, and inflation; monetary and fiscal policy; exchange rate and international trade.

title: 經濟學 Economics
description:
Economics is a year-long course spanning both microeconomics and macroeconomics. The first (Fall) semester is devoted primarily to microeconomics. It examines the behaviour of demand and supply, the several concepts of elasticity, consumer choice, the costs of production, the productive behaviour of firms, pricing strategy, and the structure of perfectly competitive markets.
A recitation (practicum) session is also scheduled on Monday at noon (10:10 AM – 12:00 PM). In the first hour (10:10–11:00 AM) the teaching assistant reviews basic concepts through worked problems; in the second (11:00 AM – 12:00 PM) the assistant responds to students' questions. The recitation meets, on average, once every two weeks. Participation and performance there are assessed separately by the teaching assistant and count toward the final grade, and attendance is recorded; students who are unable to attend the recitation are advised to enrol in another section.
The midterm and final examinations are held on 10/30 and 12/18 respectively, during the regular class session (Friday, 10:10 AM – 12:00 PM) in the usual classroom. Students who, for any reason whatsoever, cannot sit the examinations at these scheduled times should not enrol in this course: no make-up examination will be offered under any circumstances.
objectives:
The course works through economic theory using the core analytical framework of the discipline, complemented throughout by practical application, so that students can bring the basic concepts of economics to bear on everyday life.
Students should come to understand the reasoning that underlies economic decisions and to grasp the nature of economic phenomena and the way they change — and so to become economically literate individuals who can follow an economic argument, interpret what they observe, and make sound economic decisions of their own.
grading:
1. The course grade reflects attendance, coursework, and examination performance. The weighting is: midterm examination 30%; final examination 30%; and regular assignments together with in-class performance 40%.
2. Recitation participation and performance are graded separately by the teaching assistant and folded into the final grade; attendance at the recitation is recorded. Students unable to attend should enrol in another section.
3. Article 32 of the University's academic regulations provides that, absent a legitimate reason reported and approved in advance, no make-up examination will be granted for any assessment. An unexcused absence from an examination is recorded as a score of zero.
4. Students who cannot sit the midterm and final examinations on 10/30 and 12/18 (10:10 AM – 12:00 PM) should not enrol in this course.
5. Examination rules: bring your student ID card for verification; calculators and dictionaries of any kind are prohibited; answer in pen (ballpoint).
6. Cheating is strictly forbidden. Any instance substantiated by report or by the teaching assistant's inspection will be dealt with under University regulations.
7. This course does not involve the use of AI.

title: 經濟學 Economics
description:
經濟學是一門研究在資源有限的情況下,個人、廠商與政府如何做出選擇,以及這些選擇如何影響資源配置的社會科學。本課程將介紹經濟學中的個體經濟學,探討個別市場中的經濟行為及其運作。
個體經濟學關注消費者與廠商等市場參與者如何做出決策、市場在自由運作下會產生什麼樣的結果,以及這些結果對整體社會是否是好的。本課程也將介紹經濟學家如何判斷一個市場結果對整體社會是否是好的。此外,我們也將探討政府是否有介入市場的必要,以及政府干預可能帶來的效果與影響。
objectives:
課程目標
本課程旨在介紹個體經濟學的基本理論架構與核心概念,幫助學生理解市場機制的運作方式、個體經濟行為的決策邏輯,以及市場可能出現的效率問題。課程同時介紹經濟分析的基本工具,並運用這些工具分析現實世界中的經濟政策與公共議題,培養學生以經濟學視角分析問題的能力。
學習成效
完成本課程後,學生應能夠:
理解個體經濟學的基本概念與核心理論,包括需求與供給、市場均衡、消費者選擇、廠商行為、外部性及公共財等重要議題。
解釋市場機制在資源配置中的角色,以及自由市場運作下可能產生的市場失靈及其原因。
分析政府針對市場失靈所採行的各項政策工具,並評估不同政策措施對效率與的影響。
應用個體經濟學的理論與分析方法,針對現實經濟現象及公共政策進行基本的分析與批判性思考。

title: 經濟學 Economics
description: This is an introductory course in the principles of economic behaviors and decisions, as well as the analytical methods for studying economic issues.
objectives: This course contains two parts: microeconomics and macroeconomics. In microeconomics, this course focuses on the behaviors of consumers and firms, including the topics of market structure, factor market, income distribution, market failure and government intervention, public choice, among others. In macroeconomics, this course offers a fundamental framework in analyzing macroeconomic issues and policies, focusing mainly on the measurement of GDP, inflation and unemployment, aggregate demand and supply, monetary policy, and fiscal policy. This course aims to develop for the freshman students the basic knowledge in economics, and lay the foundation for their further studies in other related fields in economics.
grading:
GRADING:
There are four graded assignments during the semester with the following weights.
Class Participation: 10%
Problem Sets: 10%
Quiz #1: 10%
Quiz #2: 10%
Midterm: 30%.
Any request of absence for the midterm must be submitted in writing before 9:00am on the exam day, except for medical emergencies.
Final: 30%. Any request of absence must be filed according to university rules.
Grading disputes may arise. With the exception of arithmetic errors, and in order to avoid problems associated with self-selection, disputes involving points scored on individual questions will NOT be considered. However, if you wish, the entire assignment will be re-graded. This re-grading may result in either a higher or lower number of points being scored.
Requests for re-grading must be submitted in writing to the instructor within one week of the assignment first being returned.
PROBLEM SETS
There are problem sets basically every two weeks. Problem sets MUST be word-processed although you may do graphs and equations by hand. Problem sets MUST have your name (last name first) and SID number in the upper right-hand corner. Problem sets are due at the beginning of class on the assignment due date. Faxed or e-mailed problem sets will NOT be accepted; late problem sets will NOT be accepted. If you want to turn your problem sets in early, you can make arrangements with me or the TA.
Although you may work on problem sets with your classmates, the written answers which you hand in are expected to be your own effort. In general, you should use study groups to figure out how to solve a problem, to make sure you have made your calculations correctly, and to discuss the answers to questions that ask you to summarize or draw conclusions from the exercise. On your own, you should write up your answers, making sure you understand yourself how to solve the problem step-by-step, and answering non-quantitative questions in your own words.
Solving the problem sets in this way is important not only for the sake of academic integrity but because the primary value of the problem sets is not in counting toward your course grade but in building your own understanding and ability to solve problems. Using the Internet and/or “test banks” deserve special mention. The general principle governing collaborative work is that it is truly collaborative: namely, it is work shared by a group of people, all of whom are learning from the experience. Copying from someone, looking for answers or hints on the Internet, or looking at problem set or exam solutions from previous semesters are not collaborative. There is a difference between being interested in an issue raised by a problem set and using the Internet to learn more about it, and searching the Internet to figure out how to solve the problem.

description:
Designed as an introduction to economics for first-year students, this course explores the foundational principles of microeconomics. The course starts with the economist’s most essential analytical framework: the model of supply and demand. Then, throughout the semester, we will apply this tool to a diverse range of microeconomic topics, including welfare analysis, public finance, firm behavior, industrial organization, labor markets, and economic inequality. While a basic understanding of calculus is beneficial, it is not a prerequisite; mathematical concepts will be reviewed in class as needed.
This is the first of a two-course sequence; macroeconomics will be covered in the following semester.
TA sessions (Mandatory): Friday 12pm-1pm.
Lectures will be given in English only.
objectives: This course aims to familiarize students with the way economists think. The tools learned in the course will help students understand and analyze economic issues clearly. Ultimately, these skills will allow students to critically engage with the business and financial articles and debate current events, which is a fundamental competency for future leaders in the field of international business.

title: 財政學 Public Finance
description:
(This syllabus is required by the school administrators; the class will proceed based on the syllabus and announcement published on the course web page.)
Public finance is a field of economics mainly concerned with government (or other collective organizations') activities and the associated economic effects. The understanding of government activities and the associated economic effects helps in the design and administration of public policies. The field is often divided into questions of what the government should do or are doing (expenditure side), and questions of how to pay for those activities (revenue side).
- On the expenditure side, one may classify government expenditures into three main types. Government purchases of goods and services for current use are classed as government consumption. Government purchases of goods and services intended to create future benefits---such as infrastructure investment or research spending---are classed as government investment. Government expenditures that are not purchases of goods and services, and instead just represent transfers of money---such as social security payments---are called transfer payments. The associated effects of various government expenditures on economic incentives and on the distribution of income, wealth, and/or consumption are the focus of expenditure-side studies.
- On the revenue side, government financing can be achieved by taxes, debts (government borrowing), asset sales, earnings made by public enterprises, seigniorage, and/or other means. How a government chooses to finance its activities must have effects on the distribution of income, wealth, and/or consumption, and on the efficiency of markets. The main theme of this course on the revenue side is taxation. The issue of how taxes affect income and wealth distribution is the focus of tax incidence studies; the issue of how taxes affect efficiency performance is the focus of efficient taxation studies. In addition, revenue side studies also analyze the effects of various types of taxes and types of borrowing as well as administrative concerns, such as tax evasion and enforcement.
In addition to the term "public finance", a broader term—public economics—and a narrower term—government finance—are also used often. As a late comer, the public choice school to public finance becomes somewhat popular from the 80's. It seeks to explain how self-interested voters, politicians, and bureaucrats actually operate, rather than how they should operate.
objectives: The purpose of this course is to provide you with a theoretical framework in the discipline of public finance. My objectives are to stimulate thinking based on the framework, and to prepare you for continuing your pursuit in the field of public finance.

∙ Exams (75%): There will be one mid-term exam and one final exam. The mid-term exam counts for 35% of your final score, and the final exam counts for 40%. Be notice that the preparation of each midterm and final exam requires a tremendous amount of time and effort from the instructor and teaching assistants. Furthermore, to maintain grading fairness and objective evaluation for the entire class, this course does not offer makeup exams or accommodate individual absences by creating separate test papers. All enrolled students are strictly required to attend both exams to avoid any negative impact on their final semester grades.

title: 財政學 Public Finance
description:
This course is the first of a two-course sequence in Public Finance. The field of public finance studies how governments make decisions in response to market failures, distributional concerns, and social objectives, as well as the resulting economic effects. The first semester focuses on the expenditure side.
The curriculum is structured around four core thematic pillars:
Foundations of Welfare Economics (Weeks 1 and 2): We start the course by reviewing some core concepts learned from Basic Economics with Calculus as our tool. We extend them in meaningful ways that will be helpful to understand the role of the government (or state) and social choice.
Market Failures and Government Mitigation (Weeks 3 through 6): We then explore ways the private market can fail to reach an “optimum” (i.e., Pareto efficiency), and how the government can mitigate these inefficiencies using public policies.
Political Economy and Policy Implementation (Weeks 7 through 11): We investigate the structural hurdles the government may run into when implementing policies. Specifically, how does the government elicit preferences from the public as well as determine the value for goods provided?
Social Insurance and Redistribution (Weeks 12 through 15): We finish up this course by discussing different national (or social) insurance programs, including health care and social security. We will compare programs from Taiwan and the United States.
Note: it is strongly encouraged for students to have taken the Calculus sequence before enrolling in this course. This course is conducted entirely in English. All lectures, course materials, assignments, exams, and presentations will be strictly in English.
objectives:
After this course, a typical student should be able to ...
Select and apply the appropriate tools of economic analysis,
Explain the inefficiencies of a private market and how government intervention can mitigate these issues,
Discuss the role of voting and implications for social welfare,
Evaluate a social project that has future costs and benefits,
Compare different social programs in Taiwan and the United States,
Appraise different types of “equity” and deduce their implications.
grading:
This course is graded out of 500 points with the following rubric:
Concept Checks: 40 points
Homework Inspection: 60 points
Review Quizzes: 75 points each (150 points total)
Final Exam: 250 points
Your semester grade will be determined by the proportion out of 500 points you earn throughout the course.

title: 政治學 Political science
description: 本課程以一學期授課。大致依照政治學的研究範圍與方法、相關基本概念、政府運作、非政府(市民社會)運作、重要政策、國際關係等順序,用兩個學期對政治學做一鳥瞰式全覽。其中政府運作、非政府(市民社會)運作、重要政策三大部分,將各以數次進度詳細說明。
objectives: 本課程擬以最新的事例和理論學說,介紹政治方面的問題與爭議,提供初學者對政治問題的辨識與初步分析能力。尤其對政治學的研究範圍與方法、政府運作、非政府(市民社會)運作、國家經濟、社會政策之決策過程等範疇,具有基本概念且能建立其中相互關連之概念連結。其中政府運作、非政府(市民社會)運作、重要政策三大部分,將與時事連結期能使學理與生活密切同步化理解;進而建構學生以理論分析當前政治問題之初步能力。
grading:
平時成績占30%,期中考試占20%、期末考試占50%
。平時上課若遲到或無故曠課,會嚴重影響成績—很嚴重、非常嚴重。

title: 國際關係 International Relations
description: This course introduces students to the basic premises and theoretical concepts in the field of International Relations. The main goal of this course is to assist students from different backgrounds to understand the major theoretical debates and empirical issues in the study of relations among states and other relevant actors in the international system. This can increase their interest in global issues, and prepare those who are interested in pursuing related-career paths.
objectives:
The main objective of this course is to get students closer to the understanding of International Relations, from different theoretical perspectives, as well as in relevant sub-areas of study. From the introduction of mainstream theories and the alternative theoretical approaches from recent decades, to important themes such as conflict, war, institutions, security, development, environmentalism, among others, students will be able to better comprehend the diversity of opinions and explanations behind those issues.
Throughout the semester, students are required to read the indicated chapters from the main course book, as well as trying to read the recommended supplementary materials. Each session will consist of three hours. For the first couple of hours, the instructor will provide a lecture on the main ideas and concepts for the selected topic of the day. The third hour will be devoted to interactive activities, occassionally combined with a team-based presentation prepared by students on specific study cases. It is expected that through these activities, students can also improve their critical thinking, oral and writing presentation skills.
grading:
This course is a required course for students at the Diplomacy Department, and student's attendance and participation are vital elements to its passing. Preparation and discussion are therefore highly encouraged. The composition of evaluation is as follows:
Midterm Exam: 20%
Final Exam: 30%
Team-based presentation: 20%
Depending on the number of students enrolled in this course, the instructor will ask them to form teams and each one will be making a presentation throughout the semester. Each team will be selecting a study case to be presented, after previous consultation with the instructor. The team presentations will take place between Week 5 and Week 15. The number of teams and their members will be defined in the first weeks of the semester, depending on the total number of students enrolled in this course. Also, depending on the number of members per team, the average length recommended for each presentation will be determined.
After its definition and selection of the topic, the team should read all the required and supplementary materials for that session, and connect its contents to the case they will present. The team can use audiovisual materials, such as PowerPoint, Canva or Prezi files during the presentation; and if time allows it, some interactive activities at the end of it, to engage the audience.
The score of the presentation will consist in: organization and coordination of the team members (20pts.); content and coherence of the presentation (40pts.); performance of team members during the presentation and time management (40pts.).
Attendance and Participation: 30%
Attendance and punctuality are a key element in the course, as well as constant participation by students. Discussion will be relevant, particularly during the last hour of each session.
weeklyText:
Weekly time of in-classroom sessions: 3 hours
Expected weekly time of study and preparation prior to the class: 1-2 hours
Week 1 (9/8): Course overview and introduction / What is International Relations and World Politics?
Shannon L. Blanton and Charles W. Kegley, World Politics: Trend & Transformation, 17th Edition (Boston, MA: Cengage Learning, 2021), Chapter 1. [Hereafter: World Politics].
* Kenneth Waltz, Theory of International Politics (New York: McGraw-Hill, 1979), Chapter 1.
Week 2 (9/15): Mainstream Theories in International Relations: Realism and Liberalism
Blanton and Kegley, World Politics, Chapter 2.
*David A. Lake, “Theory is Dead, Long Live Theory: The End of the Great Debates and the Rise of Eclecticism in International Relations,” European Journal of International Relations 19 (2013), pp. 567-587.
*John Mearsheimer, “E. H. Carr vs. Idealism: The Battle Rages On,” International Relations, Vol. 19, No. 2 (2005), pp. 139-152.
Week 3 (9/22): Other Theories: Constructivism, Marxism and Feminism
Blanton and Kegley, World Politics, Chapter 2.
* Emanuel Adler, “Constructivism in International Relations: Sources, Contributions, and Debates,” in Handbook, pp. 112-145.
Week 4 (9/29): Foreign Policy and Explanation of International Decision Making
Blanton and Kegley, World Politics, Chapter 3.
* Duncan Snidal, “Rational Choice and International Relations,” in Walter Carlsnaes, Thomas Risse, and Beth Simmons, eds., Handbook of International Relations, 2nd. edition pp. 85-111 (London: SAGE, 2012). [Hereafter: Handbook].
Week 5 (10/6): Great Powers, Hegemony, and Rivalries
Blanton and Kegley, World Politics, Chapter 4.
* David Lake, “Great Power Hierarchies and Strategies in Twenty-First Century World Politics,” in Handbook, pp. 555-577.
Week 6 (10/13): Emerging Powers and the Global South
Blanton and Kegley, World Politics, Chapter 5.
* Richard Ned Lebow and Benjamin Valentino, “Lost in Transition: A Critical Analysis of Power Transition Theory,” International Relations, Vol. 23, No. 3 (2009), pp. 389-410.
Week 7 (10/20): Increasing Relevance of Non-state Actors
Blanton and Kegley, World Politics, Chapter 6.
* Marianna Charountaki, “Conceptualising Non-State Actors in International Relations,” in Marianna Charountaki and D. Irrera, eds., Mapping Non-State Actors in International Relations. Non-State Actors in International Relations, pp.1-16 (Cham: Springer, 2022).
Week 8 (10/27): Midterm Exam
Week 9 (11/3): The concept of War and its Threats
Blanton and Kegley, World Politics, Chapter 7.
* Brian Efird, Jacek Kugler and Gaspare Genna, “From War to Integration: A Generalized Power Transition Dynamic,” International Interactions, Vol. 29, No. 4 (2003), pp. 293-313.
Week 10 (11/10): The Quest for Security, Power, and Alliances
Blanton and Kegley, World Politics, Chapter 8.
* Jeffrey Taliaferro, “Security Seeking under Anarchy: Defensive Realism Revisited,” International Security, Vol. 25, No. 3 (2000/01), pp. 128-161.
Week 11 (11/17): The Maintenance of Peace, International Law, and Collective Security
Blanton and Kegley, World Politics, Chapter 9.
* John Ikenberry, “Liberal Internationalism 3.0: America and the Dilemmas of Liberal World Order,” Perspectives on Politics, Vol. 7, No. 1 (2009), pp. 71-87.
* Sebastian Rosato, "The Flawed Logic of Democratic Peace Theory," American Political Science Review, Vol. 97, No. 4 (2003), pp. 585-602.
Week 12 (11/24): Economic Globalization and International Finances
Blanton and Kegley, World Politics, Chapter 10.
* Jonathan Kirshner, “The Economic Sins of Modern IR Theory and the Classical Realist Alternative,” World Politics, Vol. 67, No. 1 (2015), pp. 155-183.
Week 13 (12/1): Economic Development and International Trade
Blanton and Kegley, World Politics, Chapter 11.
* Jana Honke and Markus Lederer, “Development and International Relations,” in Handbook, pp. 775-800.
Week 14 (12/8): Demographic and Cultural Transformations and their impact on IR
Blanton and Kegley, World Politics, Chapter 12.
* Monica Duffy Toft, “Religion and International Relations Theory,” in Handbook, pp. 673-691.
* Gallya Lahav and Sandra Lavenex, “International Migration,” in Handbook, pp. 746-774.
Week 15 (12/15): Political Change and Human Rights in IR
Blanton and Kegley, World Politics, Chapter 13.
* Thomas Risse, “Transnational Actors and World Politics,” in Handbook, pp. 426-452.
Week 16 (12/22): Final Exam

title: 社會學 Sociology
description:
主題與目的
本課程為一學年之課程。在兩學期的課程學習中,我們將透過社會學基礎理論及概念的學習,來討論人類社會的各種型態及特質,以及了解存在於我們生活周遭的各種社會現象。
本課程規劃為兩階段的學習。在上學期的課程中,除了介紹社會學此學門的特性、發展背景與常用的研究方法之外,學習主題將偏重於微視社會學的範疇。我們將透過不同主題的介紹,以了解個人、人際、團體、組織等等的發展與關連。本學期教授的單元,將包括自我發展與社會化、團體與組織、偏差與犯罪、社會控制、性別、家庭與婚姻、文化與媒體、消費等等。在下學期的課程中,我們除接續上學期的學習脈絡外,將著重於鉅視社會學的範疇,探討各種較為宏觀的社會學現象與理論。其中的主題將包括教育、宗教、社會階層與社會流動、族群、人口、都市化與社區發展、經濟與工作、政治制度與國家發展、社會運動、全球的不平等與社會變遷等等。
課程型態介紹
本課程包括正課與實習/討論課,其中正課上課時間為3節課(08:10-11:00),主要是由授課老師以演講(lectures)方式講授社會學相關理論概念與分析社會現象,並依教學需要以討論及影音媒體輔助教學。實習/討論課則提供同學們更多互動學習的機會。實習/討論課時間為一節課(11:10-12:00),主要是以互動式的分享及討論(discussion sessions)方式進行。助教將會配合教學進度,帶領同學對正課內容進行延伸性討論,協助導讀期中報告閱讀文本,輔導小組研究的執行,以期能強化同學們對於理論概念的理解,培養社會學思考與研究能力,增進知識在生活經驗上的連結與應用。
本課程使用Moodle數位學習平台搭配課堂教學。同學們可在平台上瀏覽並下載各單元投影檔內容以及各單元之補充參考資料,上傳作業與報告,提問課程相關問題,進行線上討論等。由於課程平台並非每日維護,同學若需緊急聯繫授課師或助教,為求溝通時效,仍建議以電郵為主。同學在討論課的參與及表現將由助教評分,並將列入本課程平時成績計算。
objectives: 全課程目標在於培養學生對於社會學的基本認識,對社會的關懷與理解,以及對社會現象與生活經驗的觀察與分析能力。。
grading:
修課成績之決定因素:
課堂表現:23%
此項目包括你整學期的課堂參與及學習表現(含正課與討論課之出席與表現)。
報告:32%
報告共有三篇,其中包括二篇個人短篇閱讀報告及一篇小組學習報告。每篇報告必須以電腦打字,規定字型大小規格為12,版面之邊界設定不得小於2.5公分。期中報告必須於繳交日當天早上8:00前上傳至教學網頁「作業繳交區」,繳交時間以作業上傳時間為依據,過繳交日上午8:00即算遲繳。
期中報告紙本請以訂書針簡單裝訂(勿置入文件夾中或加上塑膠製封面),於繳交日當天的討論課將報告紙本交與你討論課的助教。期末報告與組員互評表只需上傳,不需繳交紙本。
報告可提早繳交。遲交作業將予以扣分,處理方式為每遲交一天扣一級分(如B→B-,B-→C+),過早上8點(期中報告)或下午5點(期末報告)算次一天。
個人期中閱讀報告:11%(5.5% × 2)
參與本課程學習的同學需於本學期針對必讀教材中四篇英文短文中,分別於期中考前(指學期前半部)及期末考前(指學期後半部)各擇一篇撰寫個人短篇閱讀報告,報告中請簡述文章大意,並針對每篇文章末後的思考問題提出你的回應。篇幅原則上不要超過2頁(約1500字),繳交日期請參考教學行程。
小組期末學習報告:20%
參與本課程學習的同學於本學期需針對學習內容,以約4-5人為一組,繳交一篇小組書面報告。報告題目與形式可自訂,但其主題需與本課程在這一學期所教授的內容有關,且在報告中可囊括多項課程主題領域進行綜合式的探討。各小組同學可於助教所開放的討論諮詢時間與助教約定時間討論小組報告之題目、準備方向、以及報告進行中的各項問題。其他相關事項會於學期中在課堂內及教學網站中公佈。小組報告請於期末考當週週五(12/25)下午5:00前,至數位教學平台之作業繳交區完成線上繳交,不需繳交紙本。
各小組需於期中考前繳交1頁A4的簡要研究計畫書給所屬助教(繳交日為第6週上課日),該作業將佔期末報告10%的成績(學期成績2%)。各小組並請於第6-8週間與助教約時間討論小組研究計畫。與助教約討論的時間為週間(不含放假日)0900-2100(討論最晚需於2100結束),若需更改時間必須於48小時前通知助教,逾期不受理。若約定討論時間no show,則該組放棄與助教討論的機會,無法另行約時間討論。會議討論出席與表現亦將計入討論課平時成績考量。
小組組員互評表:1%

title: 初級會計學(一) Fundamental Accounting (I)
description:
Please do not contact the Professor and TA for override. Thank you!
This is the first course in a two-semester Introductory Level Financial Accounting sequence. This course is designed to enhance students’ understanding of the financial reporting processes. The focus of the course is on fundamental accounting concepts and principles. The course shows students how a firm's economic transactions are prepared and reported in the financial statements and related disclosures. The course aims to provide students with basic skills to prepare, read, and use financial statements. This course also aims to further prepare students for more advanced financial accounting courses as well as to help students become both sophisticated preparers and users of financial accounting information.
objectives:
This course is designed to provide you with an in-depth understanding of the subject covered by the materials - fundamental financial accounting. The nature of this course is demanding and challenging. It is time-consuming for a college freshman to master the subject while trying to get used to the newly-started college life in the same time. To succeed, you need to put serious efforts outside of class. Come to each class prepared.
The course materials are presented through a mix of pre-recorded class lectures, assigned readings and problems. You should maximize your understanding of the materials by watching class lectures. To be successful, you are expected to actively involve in the course by asking questions via email and review the assigned readings and attempt all homework problems after the class.
grading:
Exams 60%
Homework, Quizzes, and Participation 40%

title: 初級會計學(一) Fundamental Accounting (I)
description:
115學年度本課程,已超過原先設定選課人數,無法加簽。請勿寄信詢問是否加簽,教師不會回覆任何加簽詢問之mail。
This course is designed to introduce students to the assumptions, principles, and practice of financial accounting. The course content consists of a mix of descriptive material, financial accounting rules, and the application of these rules to various business situations. Topics include a detailed discussion of the accounting cycle, accounting for assets, liabilities, and shareholders’ equity, and financial statement analysis. The course is part of the foundation for all advanced business school classes, and as such is of great importance for building a successful business career.
grading:
Book chapters are assigned each week. Reading each chapter and doing the problems will help you understand the material. I will assume you have read each chapter PRIOR to discussion question and explanation. I am very happy to help any student to learn the material. But before you discuss a question with me, I expect that you do your part of the bargain. That is, you are to read the text, work the problems before hand, and discuss concepts and problems with classmates first. Then you are more than welcome to ask questions anytime! Written Material and your colleagues are valuable resources that are instrumental in any career!!!!
Examinations must be taken at the scheduled time. No makeup exam is allowed unless you are involved in an emergency under certain circumstances. If it happens to you, official affidavits and your written petition must be presented to the instructor in order to file for an official decision and record.
Appropriate classroom behavior is expected at all times, including respect for the instructor and peers. PLEASE make every effort to be in the classroom at the official start time. If circumstances prevent on-time arrival, be considerate of your peers by entering with minimal disruption. Cell phones in the classroom should be turn off during class time!
The course is comprised of lectures and tutorials. Attendance at lectures and tutorials is compulsory. Students learn from lectures, class discussion, tutorials, and homework exercises, and by preparing other material. Personal study is supplemented by help which is readily available from the instructor and subject tutor. Examinations are part of the learning process. To this end the lecturer and tutor conduct tests in classes.

title: 初級會計學(一) Fundamental Accounting (I)
description: This course is designed to provide a basic understanding of financial accounting and covers various financial accounting topics, including basic accounting theory, accounting principles, procedures to record business transactions, measurements of assets and liabilities and preparations for financial statements. More importantly, students will learn how accounting information assists financial statement users in facilitating their decision making.
objectives: Accounting is the language of business, facilitating communication of the financial aspects of business. This module provides an introduction to the financial accounting branch of accounting. The activities and events of a business entity are summarized by the financial accounting process into published financial statements to be used by external users such as investors and creditors. Such users would need to understand both the financial accounting process and its outputs in order to make investing or lending decisions. Therefore, students will learn how to prepare simple financial statements and also learn how to read, understand and use published financial statements for decision-making. Published financial statements of listed companies will be used as examples.

This course is the first course in a two-semester sequence of Introductory Level Financial Accounting. This course is designed to enhance students' understanding of the financial reporting processes. The focus of the course is on fundamental accounting concepts and principles. The course shows students how the economic transactions of a firm are prepared and reported in the financial statements and related disclosures. The objective of the course is to provide students with basic skills to prepare, read, and use financial statements. This course also aims to further prepare students for more advanced financial accounting courses as well as to help students become both sophisticated preparers and users of financial accounting information.

This course is designed to introduce students to the assumptions, principles, and practice of financial accounting. The course content consists of a mix of descriptive material, financial accounting rules, and the application of these rules to various business situations. Topics include a detailed discussion of the accounting cycle, accounting for assets, liabilities, and shareholders’ equity, and financial statement analysis. The course is part of the foundation for all advanced business school classes, and as such is of great importance for building a successful business career.

title: 初級會計學(一) Fundamental Accounting (I)
description: This course is designed to provide a basic understanding of financial accounting and covers various financial accounting topics, including basic accounting theory, accounting principles, procedures to record business transactions, measurements of assets and liabilities and preparations for financial statements. More importantly, students will learn how accounting information assists financial statement users in facilitating their decision making.
objectives: Accounting is the language of business, facilitating communication of the financial aspects of business. This module provides an introduction to the financial accounting branch of accounting. The activities and events of a business entity are summarized by the financial accounting process into published financial statements to be used by external users such as investors and creditors. Such users would need to understand both the financial accounting process and its outputs in order to make investing or lending decisions. Therefore, students will learn how to prepare simple financial statements and also learn how to read, understand and use published financial statements for decision-making. Published financial statements of listed companies will be used as examples.
grading:

title: 初級會計學(二) Fundamental Accounting (II)
description: This course is the second part of a two-semester sequence in Introductory Financial Accounting. It deepens students' understanding of financial reporting processes, emphasizing core accounting concepts and principles. The course explores how a firm’s economic transactions are recorded and reflected in financial statements and related disclosures. The primary goal is to equip students with the foundational skills to prepare, interpret, and utilize financial statements effectively. Additionally, this course prepares students for advanced financial accounting studies and aims to develop their proficiency as both preparers and users of financial accounting information.
objectives:
This course is designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of fundamental financial accounting. The subject matter is rigorous and demanding, requiring significant effort, especially for college freshmen adapting to their new academic environment. Success in this course will depend on your dedication and commitment outside of structured learning activities. It is essential to stay consistent and come prepared to engage with the course material.
The course content is delivered through video lectures, assigned readings, and problem-solving exercises. To maximize your understanding, you should watch all assigned videos attentively, review the related readings thoroughly, and complete all homework problems. Active engagement with the material—such as taking notes, reflecting on the concepts, and attempting to solve problems independently—will be crucial for your success in this course.

description:
請注意:本班級不加簽擋修單,若會計學(一)、(二)未全部及格者,老師強烈建議修過會計學(一)、(二)再修習中級會計學。教學經驗上,學生同時修習會計學(一)、(二)和本班中級會計學者,結果都是學期成績不及格,甚至初會、中會二者同時不及格,會增加同學成績單上不好的紀錄。(若系統選課選上或班級灌檔選上的同學,建議請在開學前自行自系統退課,以便利可以改選修其他課程或其他班級中級會計學。)
本課程介紹中級會計學(一)重要主題之會計處理,包括財務報導與會計準則、財務報表、收入認列、現金及應收帳款、存貨、不動產、廠房及設備、無形資產,及其他新發展之國際財務報導準則。
學習態度及上課表現影響考試分數及學期成績,也是學生未來職場成功的關鍵因素,四大會計師事務所的合夥會計師都建議教學應更著重學生平時的學習態度及上課表現之考核分數。本班級對於學習態度及上課表現要求請參見「學習的規範」,上課第二週需填寫座位表,以利後續上課表現之考核成績。
課程大綱若修改,以本課程數位學習網的最終版本內容及上課發放之課程大綱說明為準。
objectives:
學習目標包括:
1.了解財務會計體系之原理及原則。
2.了解國際會計準則基礎的會計處理及財務報導原則。
3.了解財務報導與企業經營及決策之關係。
4.應用資料處理工具軟體分析財務報表資料。
5.學習應用會計專業資訊分析能力及展現團隊合作精神。
grading:
1.上課及平時成績 20%
2.期中考試(二次) 40%
3.期末考試 25%
4.學期專題報告 15%
成績公正性的規範:維持成績公正性是學校重要的原則,上課及平時成績著重同學的上課表現,考試成績著重考試公平性之維持,如因事、病假(不包括公假)需補考期中考或期末考者,需依學校規定程序事先辦理請假,並需在一週內完成補考,且該次成績須乘以0.85。學期專題報告成績著重報告的創意、內容完整性、團隊合作及應用多元媒體表達能力之呈現。
學習態度及上課表現的規範:維持良好的教室上課環境是老師與學生共同的責任,也是尊重其他同學學習權利的表現,包括缺席、遲到、看手機、睡覺、吃東西等都可能影響到老師的上課及其他同學的聽講,也會影響學期總成績。上課準時認真聽講及回答老師問題者,平時成績及學期成績將予以加分,最高加至滿分100分。
請假規範:請假皆須依學校規定辦理,且不接受事後請假。
第二次上課將會請同學填寫座位表,以便利紀錄同學出席及上課表現成績。
上課遲到、缺席及學習態度不佳的同學,考試成績及學期總分將不會給予任何加分。
學期專題報告製作說明:同學以6位為一組完成指定之專題報告,並在12/26以前將報告交給助教及上傳檔案至政大Moodle教學平台。

title: 中級會計學(一) Intermediate Accounting (I)
description:
*開學第一堂正課務必出席,以確認課程要求與內容細節(與114學年度有極大差異)。
*課程內容、進度及評量規定如有必要將進行調整,請以第一周正課時所發放之授課大綱為基準。
*本課程以會計學(一)、(二)之觀念與會計處理能力為基礎。若尚未修畢或尚未通過會計學(一)、(二)之學生,原則上「不」建議修習本課程(不簽檔修單)。依過往教學經驗,初級會計學基礎未完備者,通常會面臨較高的學習負荷;若同時修習初級會計學與中級會計學,高度很有可能增加兩門課程學習成果均不理想之風險。經選課系統或系所灌檔取得修課資格者,仍應自行審慎評估其先備能力、可投入時間及整體修課負荷。
==============
*本課程加簽條件(總加簽人數不超過10人):
[1]欲加簽同學第一堂課請務必本人出席,僅會在第一次正課處理加簽問題。
[2]欲加簽同學皆需已修畢(且及格)初會(一)與初會(二)。
[3]加簽順位依序如下(僅可能加簽底下順位1、順位2、順位3 三種類型):
*順位1:會計系乙班(「不」包含甲班)。建議備妥初會(一)與初會(二)成績資訊以備用。
*順位2 雙主修會計系同學:以高年級為優先。遇同一順位者,將參酌初會(一)與初會(二)成績。建議備妥初會(一)與初會(二)成績資訊以備用。
*順位3雙主修財政系同學(但僅限:因其他課時間衝堂而無法直接修習財政系所開授之中級會計學 (四234)者):以高年級為優先。遇同一順位者,將參酌初會(一)與初會(二)成績。建議備妥初會(一)與初會(二)成績資訊以備用。
==============
*因為根據行事曆周五的課會放假三次(9/25、10/9、12/25),故調整上課時間為D567(除了第一周,其餘皆會超過三小時)以平衡進度。D567「不」包含實習課。實習課時間將於第一周正課時由助教與修課同學當場協調。
*其中有兩次小考會安排在正課(而非實習課)時進行(各次小考預設時間均為兩小時,考試完畢後則繼續上正課),詳見各周安排。
*期中考與期末考會安排在正課時進行,預設時間均為三小時(視狀況彈性延長),考試完畢後則直接結束,不繼續上正課。
*修課學生應於開學第二週完成「座位之登記」,以利課堂互動與相關紀錄。
*本課程介紹中級會計學(一)之核心議題(原則上以Kieso課本展開主要授課內容,視狀況彈性補充其他中文課本&準則內容),中會(一)之主題通常包括:財務報導與會計準則、財務報表之表達、客戶合約之收入、現金及應收款項、存貨、不動產、廠房及設備、無形資產等。課程除著重會計處理與計算外,亦強調交易之經濟實質、會計判斷及財務報表影響。
*建議修課學生應持續進行課前準備、課堂參與及課後練習。本課程將列舉具體標準,以評量出席、課堂準備及學習參與情形。
objectives:
一、建立財務會計觀念架構與準則理解基本能力
二、連結至財務報表分析、企業決策與專業判斷能力
三、應用數位工具、溝通協作與專業責任能力
grading:
成績評量方式(暫訂):
一、成績評量方式:
(一)課堂參與、平時表現及出席:20%
本項成績主要依據學生之出席情形、準時狀況、課堂練習、討論參與及其他指定之學習活動綜合評定。
將於第二次正式上課時請學生填寫【座位表】。除經教師同意調整座位外,學生原則上應依登記座位入座,以利教師辨識、記錄出席情形及課堂參與表現。座位表僅作為課堂學習紀錄之輔助。
(二)期中考試:30%
期中考試主要評量學生對前半學期重要會計觀念、準則規定、計算程序、會計分錄及財務報表影響之理解與應用能力。
(三)期末考試:25%
期末考試主要評量學生對後半學期課程內容之理解與應用,並得包括跨章節整合、會計判斷及財務報表分析等題型。
(四)實習課、作業(包含兩次Excel)、及其他指定學習活動:25%
本項成績實際項目、繳交方式及各項配分等,屆時將於課堂或數位學習平台另行公告。
*各項成績合計最高可能為100分。課堂參與及平時表現應反映於其所屬之20%成績項目。
二、評量成績相關原則

title: 成本管理會計(一) Cost and Management Accounting(I)
description:
Course Description
Cost and Management Accounting provides managers with essential information for planning, controlling, decision-making, and performance evaluation. This course introduces the fundamental concepts of cost and management accounting while emphasizing the practical application of cost information to solve real-world business problems and support managerial decision-making.
The course integrates:
Real-world business cases
Excel-based data analysis
In-class discussions and group activities
Rather than focusing solely on computational techniques, the course aims to develop students' analytical thinking and managerial decision-making skills.
Course Requirements
Attendance is mandatory during the first week of class. Course policies, group assignments, homework requirements, and the final project will be explained during the first class. Students who do not attend the first class should not enroll in or waitlist for this course.
Complete the seating chart during the second week. Students are required to sit in their assigned seats and complete the seating chart for attendance and classroom management purposes.
Course enrollment is generally closed to add requests. If vacancies become available, students will be admitted according to the University's official waitlist procedures. Please do not email the instructor requesting permission to add the course.
Attend class regularly and participate actively. The course includes in-class exercises, quizzes, case discussions, and group activities. Attendance and participation will be considered as part of the course evaluation.
Attendance at mid-term and final exams is mandatory, barring official university-approved leave.
Prepare course materials before each class. Some learning materials will be provided through Moodle or other digital learning platforms. Students are expected to complete assigned homework before class.
Copying assignments from other students will result in a zero score. Late submissions will also receive zero points.
objectives:
Course Objectives
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:
Understand the fundamental concepts of cost and management accounting.
Develop analytical skills for interpreting cost information.
Apply cost information to support managerial planning and decision-making.
Analyze organizational cost structures and profitability.
Utilize cost management techniques to improve organizational performance.
Apply IT and data visualization tools to solve accounting problems, in alignment with AACSB's experiential learning objectives.

title: 財務管理 Financial Management
description:
This introductory course, Financial Management, is designed to provide undergraduate students with a fundamental understanding of corporate finance, including principles and practices.
Throughout the semester, students will explore key concepts such as financial analysis, planning, and decision-making. The course will cover fundamental topics including the time value of money, risk and return, capital budgeting, financial markets and institutions, and the role of financial managers in corporate settings.
objectives:
By the end of this course, students will be able to:
Understand Core Financial Principles: Explain the fundamental concepts of financial management, including the time value of money, risk-return tradeoff, and cost of capital.
Analyze Financial Statements: Interpret and evaluate financial statements to assess a firm’s performance, profitability, liquidity, and solvency.
Apply Capital Budgeting Techniques: Use tools such as Net Present Value (NPV), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), and Payback Period to evaluate investment opportunities.
Assess Capital Structure and Financing Decisions: Understand the trade-offs between debt and equity financing, and evaluate the impact of capital structure on firm value.
Communicate Financial Analysis Effectively: Present financial data and investment recommendations in a clear, concise, and professional manner, both in writing and orally.

title: 管理學 Management
description:
本課程旨在引導學生系統性理解管理學之核心理論與實務基礎,透過經典管理學派與當代管理思維之介紹,建立學生對組織運作與管理決策的整體觀。課程聚焦於管理的四大基本功能──規劃(Planning)、組織(Organizing)、領導(Leading)與控制(Controlling),使學生能掌握管理者在不同情境下的角色與責任。
透過結合理論講授、國內外企業個案、課堂互動式問題討論,培養學生將抽象管理概念轉化為具體行動方案的能力,強化實務情境中進行問題分析、決策判斷與價值創造的管理素養,以奠定未來進階管理或職涯發展基礎。
objectives:
修習本課程後,學生應能達成以下學習成效:
理解與說明管理學核心理論與經典著作
能夠掌握主要管理學派與代表性學者之理論觀點,並理解其在現代組織管理中的意涵與限制。
掌握管理四大功能之基本概念與運作邏輯
能夠清楚說明規劃、組織、領導與控制之內涵,並理解其在企業經營與組織運作中的相互關聯。
運用管理理論分析實際管理問題
能將管理概念與分析工具應用於企業模擬情境中,進行問題診斷、成因分析。
發展策略思考與價值創造的管理視角
能從整體組織與長期發展角度思考管理議題,理解管理決策如何影響組織績效與競爭優勢。
強化溝通表達與團隊討論能力
透過課堂討論與小組活動,能清楚表達管理觀點,並在團隊互動中進行理性溝通與整合不同意見。

修課學生應於每週課前完成指定教材章節與當週個案之預習。

title: 管理學 Management
description:
在現代組織架構中,專業人才往往同時兼具「管理者」與「部屬」的雙重角色。因此,本課程的核心目標在於協助同學同時掌握這兩種身分所需的關鍵技能與核心觀念:
厚植管理者的領導與決策力:建立扎實的管理學理架構,培養同學在面對組織目標時,具備宏觀的規劃、資源配置與團隊引領能力。
精進部屬的向上管理與協同力:引導同學深度理解組織行為與主管的決策邏輯,內化「向上管理」的溝通智慧,成為團隊中高效協同的關鍵夥伴。
本課程高度重視理論與實務情境的深度結合。除了結合理論文獻研讀、企業個案分析與小組同儕思辨外,另將特別貫穿一套「小組學期專案」作為核心實踐載體。專案將要求同學從目標設定、專案執行構想到最終成果產出,完整模擬真實企業運作,並實質融合管理四大功能:規劃(Planning)、組織(Organizing)、領導(Leading)與控制(Controlling)。透過專案的滾動式修正,引導同學全面內化管理知識,在高度互動的專案協同中,切實鍛鍊並彈性切換「管理者」與「部屬」的雙重角色,將學理轉化為職涯發展的即戰力。
objectives:
1. 每週的實際案例討論,建立學生對企業管理基本的認識。
2. 了解企業管理的基本理論觀念並能與實務結合。
3. 藉由小組學期專案,培養學生團隊合作能力。
4. 藉由多次報告學習表達與思考能力,增進學生聽、說、讀、想(思考)能力。
grading:
期末考 (30%)
課堂參與 (30%) : 出席/遲到狀況、發言、課堂討論、個人作業
小組學期專案報告 (40%)

description: The course structure has three parts: 1) the role of marketing, which is Creating Values for Customers, that creates value based on customer needs and the buying process; 2) marketing strategies, including segmenting, targeting, and positioning; 3) the implementation of marketing tactics, including product, pricing, distribution, and communication strategies.
objectives:
The objective of the course is to provide a framework for understanding the applications of marketing concepts and theories. Students shall learn the principles and basic knowledge of marketing management, which includes consumer and business purchase behavior, marketing research, product management, pricing strategies, channel management, promotion skills, and other related issues. The course aims to reinforce skill-based and knowledge-based competencies and will seek to prepare students for more advanced marketing studies. Students are expected to develop an intuition and systematic thinking about marketing decisions to solve real marketing problems in this course.
The course aims to:
Introduce students to the major marketing concepts
Facilitate students’ development of the ability of marketing analysis and planning
Strengthen students’ marketing tactics
Reinforce students’ abilities in problem-solving and decision-making in marketing

title: 投資學 Investments
description:
This course is an introductory investment class designed for undergraduate students, providing a foundation for advanced courses in investments, portfolio management, asset pricing, and derivatives. The course focuses on the fundamentals of investments, balancing both theoretical and practical aspects. Key topics covered include: Financial markets (basic concepts), Portfolio theory and Asset allocation, Asset pricing models, Portfolio performance evaluation, Efficient market hypothesis,Pricing and management of equity, fixed-income securities, equity options, and futures.
Students will also learn essential financial strategies such as diversification, hedging, replication, and arbitrage.
objectives:
The course will use the textbook "Investments" by Z. Bodie, A. Kane, and A.J. Marcus to teach the following financial and economic professional knowledge:
(1)Financial markets and securities trading
(2)Asset allocation, portfolio analysis, and the Markowitz portfolio selection model
(3)Capital Asset Pricing Model, index models, Arbitrage Pricing Theory, and multi-factor models
(4)Portfolio evaluation methods
(5)Efficient Market Hypothesis and behavioral finance
(6)Equity asset pricing models
(7)Fixed Income
(8)Derivatives markets, futures&options pricing, and risk management

The course “Introduction to Multimedia and Programming” is designed to equip students with fundamental skills in multimedia software and basic programming. It comprises three core modules—image editing, video editing, and programming—as well as an optional module in document processing. With an emphasis on hands-on practice and collaborative learning, the course aims to help students develop the following practical competencies:
Attain a sound understanding of multimedia tools and basic programming, with the ability to apply these skills in real-world development contexts.
Make informed choices when selecting appropriate tools and software for different professional tasks, and develop an awareness of the software requirements commonly encountered in the workplace.
Gain confidence in the practical use of multimedia applications and programming through guided exercises and experiential learning.
Enhance leadership, organisational, and communication skills through team-based project work, and become proficient in the integration and application of various multimedia tools.

title: 資料分析與程式設計入門 Introduction to Data Analysis and Programming
description:
本課程提供同學對資料處理及應用的一些初步的正確觀念,以及實作經驗,包括:(1)資料庫管理系統、管理資訊系統、系統分析與設計、程式設計、資訊安全、隱私與道德等相關議題;(2)常用的資料處理軟體:EXCEL(試算表)及ACCESS(資料庫管理系統)實務操作練習;而以實務操作為本課程內容與評分重點。本學期16週,其他進行方式有面授(7週含期中、期末考)和非同步遠距教學(9週)兩種型式,並以下述方式進行:
(1)課程講授:
如果是遠距教學,則將教材以錄影及教學網頁二種方式置網站上;教師並提供其他學者或工作者所提供值得參考的教學YouTube影片連結,建議去閱讀。
(2)觀念介紹與議題討論:
請學生遠距時,閱讀觀念介紹後,進行單元測驗自我審視觀念是否清晰。而對於價值分享類主題,放置該單元之相關議題,讓同學發表意見或心得。
(3) 遠距及面授作業:
對技術類則以1次遠距作業、4次面授作業以及期末專案作為學生學習練習。
可使用學校政大雲的Office,但不建議使用Office 365。
Mac愛好者請注意:
本課程之教學環境以微軟Windows平台為主,
面授教室亦是一般PC的微軟Windows環境。
考試、面授習題需繳交微軟Windows檔案,而且Mac上沒有一些本課程會用到的Excel的功能以及Access;本班課程也不會特地說明Mac介面問題,面授課堂練習機會也只有4次。所以,若你自家或宿舍環境只有Mac,沒有Window,不建議修習本班課程。
另提醒:本課程雖是遠距教學,但是有面授週次。請仔細評估各自狀況,若學期未結束即想出國交換遊學、或因校外實習常常無法在面授時段參加,均不適合本課程。其他提醒,請於選修成功後,進入Moodle看公告及議題二說明。
objectives:
(1) 能了解做一個可信賴的有效決策時,如何使用資料處理的必要科技與知識(如資訊安全、系統 發展、基礎程式邏輯等)。
(2)能透過EXCEL及ACCESS實作方式,利用現有資料並發展一個標準卻有彈性的模式,以做出有效的決策。
(3)能擁有整理及分析資料並建立一個簡單ACCESS資料庫的能力。
(4)能理解與應用可幫助資料處理、需求溝通、及問題解決的適當EXCEL及ACCESS技術與軟體。
grading:
EXCEL 上機期中考 15%:在實體教室,個人考試,不得使用個人筆電,限用電腦教室PC, 上傳Moodle線上平台。限1人交,檔案名稱註明姓名、學號(如〔聯絡資訊已移除〕王小魚_期中考.xlsx)。考試全部Closed Book,沒有補考。
ACCESS上機期末考 15%:在實體教室,個人考試,有2部分,不得使用個人筆電,限用電腦教室PC,上傳Moodle線上平台。限1人交,檔案名稱註明姓名、學號(如〔聯絡資訊已移除〕王小魚_期末考_A.accdb、〔聯絡資訊已移除〕王小魚_期末考_B.accdb)。考試全部Closed Book,沒有補考。
單元測驗 10%(4次*2.5%):在Moodle線上平台,閱讀完教材後。系統的設定是「可以讓你練習多次」、所以可以作答無數N次;但是,看不到每次的成績,也看不到正確答案。接近期末,12/17 24:00期限到達後,才可看到正確答案,系統將統計N次成績,直接將『最高分』作為該次單元測驗之成績。
議題討論 14%(規定的議題7次*2%):在Moodle線上平台,閱讀完教材後。除了議題七外,期限均為12/17 24:00 (議題七期限為12/22 24:00)。
面授隨堂作業 16%(4次*4%):隨堂作業上傳Moodle線上平台,1人交一檔案。檔案名稱註明姓名、學號、年月日、該日第幾部份作業(如 115/3/17同學〔聯絡資訊已移除〕王小魚交第1部分,檔名形式:〔聯絡資訊已移除〕王小魚1150317-A.xlsx),第2、3部分則為B、C。
遠距作業(1次*4%):依時限上傳Moodle線上平台,限每1人獨立作業,檔案命名仿上述。期限為9/22 0:00 ~ 9/25 24:00。
EXCEL或ACCESS期末專案 26%:
3-6人一組,如真要1~2人獨立一組,需特別經老師同意。請盡可能在9/22,透過Moodle線上平台「課程討論板」「期末專案小組成員張貼」張貼分組名單。最遲應在9/29前成立分組,分組名單確定後,變更需經老師同意;自10/31後就不得拆組、變更組員、更換組長。
EXCEL專案最低要求:功能上必須包含「2個以上的Worksheets版面配置、跨表格樞紐分析、藍本分析管理員、運算列表、規劃求解」
ACCESS專案最低要求:功能上必須包含「2個以上的資料表Table維護、基於連結之表單Form、數個有意義的查詢Query、參數方式查詢、報表Report」。
若同時完成下列EXCEL與ACCESS者(EXCEL或ACCESS可針對同一問題或不同問題),兩者會各別評分後平均,再將平均乘以1.25,作為該組的期末專案成績。
題目資料集可自行假設(但應合理)、自行收集,或運用以下說明之資料集,但不管何種來源,EXCEL專案必須包含2個以上的Worksheets(或Workbooks),ACCESS專案必須包含2個以上的資料表。不管是EXCEL或ACCESS,除非經助教特許,若只有2個工作表或資料表(第三個不限),每個表筆數各別不得低於50筆。
EXCELL跨表格樞紐分析應有兩類表格,如基本的較靜態的產品表、每日變動的訂單表,如此互補資訊,才有意義;若只有訂單表,只是切成不同統計方式的訂單表來跨表格,其意義不大。
EXCELL藍本分析管理員的各方案,最好是互斥的,才有助於決策者選擇。例如,淡季、旺季是一般商品一年銷售必有時段,所以,不會有「淡季」方案、「旺季」方案;而是可能應有淡(旺)季情境下,商品項目或人力調度方案的選擇。
第三種專案的方式,第三種專案是將資料儲存在Access,日後資料的新增、刪除、修改均在此,Excel是做輔助性的分析,因為它的樞紐分析功能比Access強。基本要求:2個以上的Worksheets版面配置、樞紐分析(不強調跨表格)、以及2個以上的資料表Table維護、基於連結之表單Form、資料筆數限制(若只有2個工作表或資料表,每個表筆數各別不得低於50筆,第三個不限)。是「Excel樞紐分析使用Access資料來源」的整合,只有1個分數,沒有2個分數,將分數直接乘以1.1,作為該組的期末專案成績。(可參考網站上所列「Access 資料庫教學可參考」46集)
鼓勵使用真實或公開資料集,以下三者,其專案成績得分,視原資料集的簡化程度(也就是忠實於原資料集的程度:除非原資料需清洗,盡量全部欄位、筆數都採用?是否純採用原資料集、而無額外假設其他欄位資料?),最多乘以1.05。(a)使用以下表之連結資料集,(b)使用「其他公開資料」(如農產運銷公開資料)。此二者均請註明資料集名稱、使用之筆數以及資料來源網址。(c) 有「產學合作」者,請提供正式公司證明(需大小章)之文件,另註明資料筆數。若聲稱使用上述三者,但欲假設其他資料,亦應對額外假設資料表的欄位有詳細說明;其數值(不管是售價利潤、成本費用性質)亦應有合理假設。例如,由下列連結只能取得「航空班機延誤」資料,如欲進一步假設「賠償費用」、「票價」、「利潤」,應先去網路搜集相關訊息、討論,再做合理簡化假設,以免過於突兀與不切實際。
若資料來源非上述,而是由網路自行收集(如利用網路爬蟲爬取)真實資料,若相較該目標領域,已收集到足夠的大量資料,請說明清楚收集方式、目標領域可能資料量、本專案已收集到的資料量,其專案成績得分,亦可能經判定最多乘以1.05。
為鼓勵同學嘗試VBA,若在期末專案(Excel專案或第三種專案的方式)中加上VBA功能(請在文件上註明清楚其功能的運作方式、帶來的方便性),其期末專案最會先酌予加分(視「VBA功能之複雜度」以及「與專案的結合程度」,此等加分最高可達10分),再考量上述1.25、1.1、1.05等之加成。
期末專案成績經各項加分後,最高上限為200,超過以200計。
期末專案為一項實踐課堂電腦技術之過程,希冀同學在設定情境後,可以思考「該資料集可以解決甚麼問題」、「該資料集可以如何處理」以及「該資料集可以如何呈現」,因此除「封面頁」外,必須有不限頁數的詳細「說明與分析文件」。以word檔、12號字體繳交。該文件應是可獨立於EXCEL、ACCESS檔案之「自我說明解釋清楚」的文件,應清楚說明專案中對所要求的功能做了什麼嘗試,產生出何種結果,並引述結果中的一些具體數字來說明對於何種決策分析有何幫助。所有圖表均需引述數字說明。要想像成這是一份交給你工作上司的文件;換言之,即使沒有EXCEL、ACCESS檔案的人,只要看到此文件,就能清楚瞭解專案做到哪些功能,對決策幫助的程度。
請在12/14 00:00~12/15 24:00前繳交,透過Moodle線上平台作業區上傳檔案(線上平台會鎖時間,請勿遲交),請將你們的所有的「EXCEL或(與)ACCESS」檔、word說明檔,包含原始資料檔、含公式設定之求解各決策後的結果檔(可分功能多個檔),一起壓縮成一個rar檔案,檔案名稱請只用組別編號,如T01.rar(不得加密,並請盡可能用學校授權軟體Winrar或免費的7-zip軟體壓縮,以免老師無法打開。並請留意Mac環境與Window不同,最好在Window下壓縮)。word說明檔封面頁請註明「組別編號、題目、各組成員系級、姓名、學號、日期、標註是EXCEL或(與)ACCESS專案」。請留意:上傳後檢視檔案是否存在且正確。一組多位同學,請由組長一人繳交即可,其餘組員請勿重複交。
Bonus VBA心得額外加分,最高6%:學生得自由決定是否繳交「我的VBA程式學習歷程與心得」報告,程式焦聚於本學期的VBA(若願意,可與其他第三代程式語言比較);個別學生心得,不可多人合寫;需於12/13 00:00~12/20 24:00前上傳Moodle專區,繳交2個檔案:(a)word心得與說明檔、A4、12號字,至少1頁、至多12頁,字數至少1000字以上。(b) Excel含有巨集的xlsm附錄檔。必須滿足下列要求,否則不予加分:請先務必先看完兩週遠距教學的公版教材,同時助教錄製的Practice 1~10應全部自行修習完畢。請寫心得時,請先逐一分10段註明看完每一集的心路歷程,再來寫綜合學習心得。最後,進階自我學習:請自己另外找一小段他人寫的正確沒有錯誤的VBA程式(可於網路上找、教科書摘錄、或請AI生成);word檔中說明其功能與你的心得,xlsm檔當附錄。
Bonus討論額外加分5%:本課程之議題討論區除了規定的議題外,歡迎同學於12/20 24:00前於「課程討論板」自由開設與本課程相關的議題號召同學們討論,但不歡迎在其上做社交、或只是將其他人、或網路的意見貼上而無自己真正的想法。所謂「與本課程相關的議題」,雖然本課程包含廣泛的資訊管理或技術面,但在討論區只做一次性的「蜻蜓點水的名詞介紹」或「轉貼網路搜尋到的資訊」,並無意義與幫助,不會得到加分,建議焦注於對於Excel以及Access的進階功能個人心得討論。希望是真能帶給其他同學幫助之「進階功能個人心法」,不是複製網路資訊,也不要只是辛苦談,更不是交談。若純粹的VBA心得,請去另繳交「選交的VBA心得作業」。老師會一一判定其對同學們瞭解本課程之幫助與價值,給予自由議題討論有貢獻的同學(不限開設者或參與討論者)與本課程相關,最給予額外加分,最高加分學期成績5%。但請留意:越近課程結束越沒有可能號召其他同學討論,故此等加分從開學第一天起隨著時間趨近截止日遞減,不建議在最後2週才作此討論(最後2週加分可能低於1%)。

description: 本課程內容所涵蓋的主題包括資料庫管理系統、管理資訊系統、系統分析與設計、程式設計、資訊安全、隱私與道德等,以及簡易商用軟體含EXCEL試算表軟體、VBA程式語言、ACCESS資料庫軟體等的基本功能介紹與實作,同時也概括介紹其他資料分析相關軟體。本課程採面授(8週含期中、期末考)及非同步遠距教學(8週)的方式交互進行,每週各有一個單元主題。另有補充教材1-管理資訊系統發展方法-系統規劃與系統分析方法及補充教材2-管理資訊系統發展方法-系統設計與資料庫設計方法等兩個加強單元,分別納入第11週和第12週的教材之中。

title: 統計學(一) Statistics(I)
description:
Statistics is the art and science of using sample data to make generalization about populations. This course is the first in a two-semester sequence (Statistics I & Statistics II) that aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental statistics and the basic concepts of data analysis. It is intended for undergraduate students who either have no prior statistics courses, or who wish to review the fundamentals before taking additional advanced statistics courses. The core topics in this semester will include descriptive statistics, basic concepts of probability, type of distributions, confidence interval, and hypothesis testing for one-sample problems. Note that the "Course Schedule & Requirements" are subject to change depending on the actual progress of the class.
註:教室容納人數有限,故加簽於第一週課堂登記、抽籤決定,請不用來信詢問。
objectives: The course provides students the underlying foundations of statistics with applications. Students successfully completing this course should be able to: 1) distinguish between population characteristics and sample information, 2) understand the methods for collecting, organizing and describing sets of data, 3) comprehend the role of random variables and sampling distributions applying to statistical inferences, and 4) recognize the fundamental concepts of statistical inferences.
grading:
Quiz 30% (on TA class), Midterm Exam 35%, Final Exam 35%
(註:小考會在TA課,請確認可以上TA課再修課 !)
(註:每週教學內容、課程進度與活動,會依實際授課狀況做調整!)

title: 統計學(一) Statistics(I)
description: Statistics is a course about data analysis. This course will begin with a brief overview of the discipline of statistics and descriptive statistics, and then introduce graphical methods of describing data. You will learn the standard and typical probability theorems and random distributions, the latter of which serves as the foundation for statistical inference. Besides we will focus on both estimation and hypothesis testing issues. We will also examine the techniques to study the relationship between two or more variables.
objectives:
An introductory course in statistics is designed to introduce students to some of the basic concepts related to statistics. Topics included are summary statistics of variables, probability, sampling distributions, estimation, and statistical inference.
At the end of this course, the students should be able to
- Develop statistical thinking.
- Learn how to create, read, and interpret graphs, charts, histograms, and diagrams.
- Learn basics about statistical inference.
- Understand variability and sampling distributions.
- Have quantitative skills to employ and build on in flexible ways.
- Develop programming skill

description:
在大數據的時代,統計學方法空前重要. 學好統計學之基本觀念與方法,才能正確應用於面對的各種實務問題.此外,也要能利用統計軟體運算和解釋分析結果,以培養自己數據分析能力和洞析未來的創意商機能力。
統計學已為現代人必備的基本知識,也是AI背後的核心基礎。兩者在基本原理、資料處理及應用上緊密結合。本課程將使初次接觸統計學領域的學員瞭解資料的種類,如何正確收集資料,取得資料後又如何整理資料,分析資料,以獲得可靠的推論或預測資訊,據以為問題解決或做決策之參考。教學方式是先介紹資料的種類,重要的資料收集方法,繼而介紹統計分析方法,各舉實例加以說明,學生参與實作,練習上並配合電腦軟體(Minitab)運算和統計分析說明結果。

title: 統計學(一) Statistics(I)
description:
本課程介紹統計學的基本概念與方法,內容涵蓋資料視覺化、描述統計、變數間關係、基本機率、隨機變數、常用機率分配、抽樣分配、中央極限定理、信賴區間、假設檢定、兩組母體比較及簡單線性迴歸。課程將搭配真實資料、統計模擬及 R 或 Excel 操作,培養學生整理資料、進行基礎統計分析、解讀統計結果與撰寫資料分析報告的能力。
PS:課程所有加簽請於開學後第一週至課堂上進行。
objectives:
課程目標
建立學生統計思維(Statistical Thinking),理解統計學在科學研究、商業分析及資料科學中的角色與應用。
培養學生整理、描述及視覺化資料的能力,能運用適當的統計圖表與描述統計量探索資料特性。
建立基本機率、隨機變數及常用機率分配之概念,作為統計推論的重要基礎。
培養學生利用抽樣分配、信賴區間及假設檢定等方法,由樣本資料推論母體特性的能力。
建立學生初步建立與解讀簡單線性迴歸模型的能力,並培養利用統計方法分析真實資料及解決問題的能力
學習成效
說明統計學的基本概念,辨識不同型態的資料及其適合的分析方法。
運用適當的統計圖表與描述統計量整理及探索資料特性。
計算並解釋基本機率、期望值及常用機率分配之相關結果。
解釋抽樣分配與中央極限定理的概念,理解抽樣變異的來源。
建立並解讀信賴區間與假設檢定結果,正確詮釋 ppp-value 及統計顯著性的意義。
比較兩組資料之差異,並能解釋統計推論所得之結論。
建立簡單線性迴歸模型,解釋模型參數並進行基本預測。
運用 R 或 Excel 完成基礎資料分析,並以口頭或書面方式呈現分析結果。
grading:
期中考 40%
期末考 40%
作業成績 20%

title: 統計學(一) Statistics(I)
description:
This course offers an introduction to statistics for undergraduate students with no prior background in the subject. As a foundational discipline in data science, statistics equips students with the essential tools and language needed to analyze data and communicate effectively with professionals in related fields. Statistics is about summarizing, interpreting, and making predictions about real-world phenomena through data.
This course introduces students to fundamental statistical concepts. Topics covered in the first semester include descriptive statistics, classical probability, random sampling, point estimation, confidence intervals, and one-sample hypothesis testing.
objectives:
By the end of this course, students will be able to:
Understand the role of statistics in scientific reasoning and data analysis, and explain key concepts such as populations, samples, random variables, probability distributions and parameters.
Summarize and visualize data using descriptive statistics, including measures of central tendency, variability, tables, and graphical displays.
Understand the principles of statistical sampling and estimation, including the concept of a sampling distribution, point estimation, and construction of confidence intervals.
Formulate and evaluate statistical hypotheses using one-sample tests (e.g., z-tests and t-tests), and interpret results in context.
Communicate statistical findings effectively, recognize limitations of statistical methods, and critically evaluate statistical claims in everyday life.

title: 商事法 Commercial Law
description:
商業活動的法律規範係以民事法律為基礎,再依據不同行為的特性,立法加以規範。商事法其實非常廣泛及多元,可略分為:商業組織,如公司(含各種類的公司組織)、有限合夥、(從事營利行為之)財團法人、金融機構、信託等;商業行為,如證券交易、國際貿易(海商)、保險等商業行為;商業工具,如票據、信用卡、電子/第三方支付、虛擬資產、信託及貨幣市場工具等。若從國家考試角度,商事法主要涵蓋:公司法、證券交易法、商業會計法、票據法、海商法、保險法等。
由於商事法之範圍廣泛,無法奢求在一個學期二學分的課程中,予以詳盡介紹與說明;必要的取捨勢在必行。考量本課程修課同學為大學二年級以上,均已完成民法概要之課程,具備基礎民事法律概念之期待可能。因此,本課程不贅述民法基礎概念,而將介紹商業社會中主要的商業組織:公司、有限合夥;商業行為:證券交易;商業工具:票據。希望本課程能協助同學建立對於商業組織與行為法律規範的基本認識。
此外,本課規劃在後半學期安排一次客座講師,相關安排再適時於課堂上說明。本課程相關事務,敬請聯繫本課程講師政治大學電郵及助教。
objectives:
本課程採知識導向學習(knowledge-based learning)及問題導向學習(problem-based learning)並重之講述與課堂討論方式進行。知識導向學習的重點,在於協助同學了解商事法律的規範框架;問題導向學習的重點,係以不同的公司法問題為範例,練習「認識事實、確認爭點、尋找規範、法律分析及做成結論」的法律問題處理方式。問題導向的學習,學生應先預習課程資料或參考書籍,發現問題,在現今的時代中,學習利用人工智慧工具,分析問題及做成結論。結論可以和老師不同,但是要有自己的立論基礎及邏輯思辨能力。
期待同學在課程結束後,能有在理解法條的基本能力上,梳理商業社會事件與行為及熟悉處理法律問題的基本程序,以更強的思辨邏輯面對各式各樣的訊息,具備在充斥真實與謊言的(人工智慧)資訊爆炸時代的生存能力。
grading: 上課時說明

title: 商事法 Commercial Law
description:
商事法課程係為提供修課學生對於基本商事法律制度的系統基礎認識,以期未來進入職場中有關商事法律及其實物運作的規範有一個基本掌握和理解,
本課程內容之介紹與授課內容涵蓋商事活動之規範。傳統之商事法侷限於公司、票據、海商及保險,但本課程內容不僅僅以這些法律領域為限。還將穿插基本民事法律的輔助性介紹,以得能使學生有一個法律制度的互動連結的相互關係,不至淪為技術性法規的說明和使用為已足。
本課程係為上下學期整合課,本學期設課內容以公司法為主,兼及部分保險法內容。
objectives:
本課程係為提供商事法律初學者之入門體系掌握與理解。將龐雜的商事法律體系規範,以大綱並列整理及比較分析方式,將冗長敘述性的法令及相關行政解釋或重要判決,以大綱架構或摘要式的文字呈現,輔以具體案例之分析,以實務中實際案例或判決為輔助,能讓商事運作中的案例與學習者之生活經驗相結合,並輔助以具體法律的適用,使學習活潑化,促使學生能做批判式之思考,加以重點提示比較、指引、精解,讓初學者得以體系性的掌握,以期能知悉並適用商事法之運用。
本課程的教學將使同學宏觀掌握商事法律的基本規範掌握。以使學生面臨相關法律問題與個案時,具備初步以商事法律解決問題的能力。

出席20%

1.本課程將隨時提供授課教材。在課程進行中所需涉及之相關法規以及補充參考資料,授課教師在上課前一週將會提供,具體法規授課中從網路上呈現或以電子檔方式傳送。
2.本課程主要以我國商事法律環境發展的背景為主軸並兼及商事基本法律制度一併的討論與分析,修課同學不需對於商事法制有基本概念,但要有興趣。課程進行中,隨時就具體案例議題的插入與互動。
3.本課程之授課,全程以power point進行,同學可在授課前先取得所有授課power point內容大綱與參考文獻資料。
4.相關商事法制發展背景以及體制變遷的內容,將在課程中穿插介紹,並適度以實際案例、檔案、網站內容與個別事件進行輔助性說明與介紹。授課期間具體發生的商事法律事件案例或商事政策性發展,都將作為及時性的討論題材,以使修課同學能敏銳地掌握動態事件的分析能力。

title: 微積分 Calculus
description: 微積分是重要的基礎大學數學課程,做為先備知識,微積分在很多領域都有廣泛的應用。本課程介紹極限、微分、積分等概念及其應用,以利後續專業課程的理解學習。
objectives:

objectives:

平常分數-50%(出缺席、學習態席,缺席12小時以零分計算)

這門課不加簽,謝謝.
Please bring your own swimming gear and other personal items.
Please be punctual for class. Do not use mobile phones (or sports headphones) or eat during class.
Make-up classes during menstruation: Make-up classes will begin in the fourth week. Students who miss classes due to menstruation should make up the missed classes on their own.
If you miss a class, please remember to follow the leave application process. Missed classes due to menstruation will be considered as missed classes due to other illnesses.
Please take two hours off. Four hours without asking for leave.

Tennis Course Assessment Criteria
Grading Criteria:
Tactical & Technical Skill Assessments: 40%
Class Participation & Performance: 20%
Attendance: 30% (Note: Three unexcused absences will result in a zero for the attendance grade)
Assignments & Class Records: 10%
Detailed Breakdown
Tactical & Technical Skill Assessments (40%)
Controlled Wall-Rally Height & Consistency (15%): Strategy and technical execution of maintaining consistent ball height against the wall.
Multi-Angle & Variable-Height Rallying (15%): Tactical adaptability and shot-making across varying incoming angles and heights.
Volley-to-Volley (No-Bounce) Test (10%): Assessed on proper segment positioning/mechanics, fluidity, rhythm/tempo, shot control, and footwork adjustment (weighting subject to adjustment as appropriate).
Class Participation & Performance (20%)
Evaluated on proactive learning attitude, active participation, teacher-student interaction, engagement in instructional feedback, and timely submission of tasks.
Attendance (30%)
Three unexcused absences will result in a score of zero for the attendance component.
A maximum of two approved leaves of absence is permitted, provided the classes are made up.
Make-up options: Students may make up missed sessions primarily through activities such as tennis, physical fitness training, or brisk walking.
Class Records & Assignments (10%)
Weekly Class Records: Tracking in-class progress and performance each week (an absence counts as a missed class record).
Assignments: Freeze-frame photos, sequence shots (continuous movement photos), video imitation/modeling, peer evaluations within groups, and learning self-assessment scales.

title: 體育[男女合班]—網球初級 Physical Education [male and female]--Tennis Primer
description:
一、暸解網球運動簡史及各種網球比賽的各項技術及比賽規則。
二、認識網球各種比賽技術及策略的見解,並能進行單、雙打比賽。
三、享受參與網球運動並列入生活上學習目標。
四、能藉由專項運動的學習,提昇個人專項運動能力,並具備參與運動的知識與技能 。
五、能在各運動項目的學習中,養成主動關心與賞析各項運動賽事的能力,並享受高品質休閒生活。
objectives: 本課程主要網球初級之課程,進一步修正及強化學習者之各項基本技術及觀念,同時在本學期課程中開始融入各項組合練習,期使透過不同的練習情境,使學生能熟練基本技術,並逐漸發展出個人的擊球特色,同時也藉此熟悉網球單、雙打比賽的規則、觀念及比賽策略。
grading:
評分標準為:策略及技術測驗佔40%、平常課堂表現20%、出缺席30%、(整體出缺席若缺課三次以零分計算)、課堂作業及紀錄10%。
策略及技術測驗:一、控制對牆高度穩定擊球策略及技術15%。 二、來回不同角度及高度來球的策略及技術15%。 三、凌空不落地對截測驗10%(動作肢段到位技術、動作流暢性、擊球節奏、擊球控制、腳步調整等,評分比例會適時調整)
平常課堂表現:上課態度積極度、勇於表現、師生互動、回饋教學、準時繳交作業等
出缺席:整體出缺席若缺課三次以零分計算,最多以兩次請假但需要補課 (若缺課可進行補課方式,如網球、體適能、健走位主)
課堂紀錄:每周課堂紀錄課堂表現(若缺課等同缺席課堂紀錄)
作業繳交:定格照、連貫圖、影像模仿、各組同學互評、學習量表
Tennis Course Assessment Criteria
Grading Criteria:
Tactical & Technical Skill Assessments: 40%
Class Participation & Performance: 20%
Attendance: 30% (Note: Three unexcused absences will result in a zero for the attendance grade)
Assignments & Class Records: 10%
Detailed Breakdown
Tactical & Technical Skill Assessments (40%)
Controlled Wall-Rally Height & Consistency (15%): Strategy and technical execution of maintaining consistent ball height against the wall.
Multi-Angle & Variable-Height Rallying (15%): Tactical adaptability and shot-making across varying incoming angles and heights.
Volley-to-Volley (No-Bounce) Test (10%): Assessed on proper segment positioning/mechanics, fluidity, rhythm/tempo, shot control, and footwork adjustment (weighting subject to adjustment as appropriate).
Class Participation & Performance (20%)
Evaluated on proactive learning attitude, active participation, teacher-student interaction, engagement in instructional feedback, and timely submission of tasks.
Attendance (30%)
Three unexcused absences will result in a score of zero for the attendance component.
A maximum of two approved leaves of absence is permitted, provided the classes are made up.
Make-up options: Students may make up missed sessions primarily through activities such as tennis, physical fitness training, or brisk walking.
Class Records & Assignments (10%)
Weekly Class Records: Tracking in-class progress and performance each week (an absence counts as a missed class record).
Assignments: Freeze-frame photos, sequence shots (continuous movement photos), video imitation/modeling, peer evaluations within groups, and learning self-assessment scales.

2.以遊戲及培養球感的練習方法,引領學生進入桌球世界,使初學者學得桌球基本技術、喜歡桌球運動,並進而續選桌球中級課程。
3.引領學生認識桌球運動各項基礎技術、專有名詞及訓練方法。
4.促進身心發展及培養終身運動之觀念,進而將運動排入生涯時序。
5.本學期因課程需要,需1-2次的課程調整,例如:運動賞析/桌球技術分析文章/校外實務教學等安排
objectives:
1.介紹桌球運動起源以及現今國內外國際發展趨勢。。
2.簡介桌球運動之禮儀、規則、器材之選擇與運動傷害防護。
3.講解桌球基本技術(正手發球/正手抽球/正手拉球/正手扣殺/正手切球/正手挑球/反手發球/反手推球/反手擋球/反手挑球/反手拉球/反手切球及步法)以及相關之步法運用。
4.本學期課程目標必須達成上述之基本動作與基本技術。
grading:
1.平時成績35% (1)缺、曠課情形(2)遲到、早退(3)上課精神及學習態度。
2.術科考試50%(期中20%(包括:站位/動作正確性/力道控制/落點控制)/期末30%(包括:站位/動作正確性/步法移位/力道控制/落點控制))。
3.體育常識15%(裁判法/專有名詞以及比賽成績)
weeklyText:
第一週:桌球簡史/桌球運動基本常識簡介/握拍法介紹/熱身運動介紹/球感練習/訓練方法的介紹:單球、多球練習。
第二週: 講解正手發球及反手推擋以及正手抽球動作。自主練習/分組練習
第三週:複習上週反手及正手動作/教授正手抽球 1/2 步法移位
第四週:複習上週課程>教授推擋+側身+步法移位
第五週:複習上週課程>教授左推右攻+步法移位。練習推擋+側身+推擋+移位+右攻
第六週:複習前五週全部課程。講解桌球雙打規則/練習比賽
第七週:講解期中考考試內容。複習考試內容
第八週:期中考週:反手推球(2大對角線)(連續推擋不失誤)共50球及格
第九週:正手發旋球介紹/切球介紹/自主練習/組合練習。
第十週:雙打比賽
第十一週:講解正手扣殺
第十二週:講解正手拉球
第十三週:小組分組對抗賽。
第十四週:期末考內容講解及執行細則。
第十五週:期末考試。
第十六週:補考週(未考試合格者)

title: 體育[男女合班]—慢速壘球初級 Physical Education [male and female]--Slow Softball Primer
description:
慢速壘球在國內非常盛行,如果妳在學校期間能參與此運動是很好選擇,

title: 體育[男]—男體適能 Physical Education [male]--Health Fitness
description:
一.有氧運動之項目介紹及認知
二.肌力與肌耐力之提昇要領
三.柔軟度實施之要領
四.綜合體適能之實施
五.利用政大特有的步道實施有氧運動
六.腹背肌群認識與實施要領
七.核心肌群認識與實施要領
八.運動傷害的預防與保健
九.測驗
objectives:
一.透過有氧運動.建立良好的心肺適能
二.增強肌力與肌耐力.維技較佳的健康體育
三.增進柔軟度.避免運動傷害.維持較佳的健康適能
四.維持較優良健康適能提升生活品質
grading:
一.術科測驗百分之四十
二.出缺席及學習精神佔百分之四十
三.體育常識佔百分之十
四、校園環山健走百分之十
weeklyText:
第一週:1.介紹相關簡單生理智識.營養與運動關係及個人健康體能的評
估實施。
第二週:1.單人伸展操之操作。2.雙人伸展操之操作。3.基本肌力測試。
第三週:1.伸展操之操作〈單、雙人〉。2.啞鈴器材實施之要領。
第四週:1.伸展操之操作〈單、雙人〉。2.有氧運動〈慢跑〉。3.基本肌
力練習。
第五週:1.伸展操實施。2.重量訓練室器材之介紹與練習。
第六週:1.伸展操實施。2.循環訓練之介紹與實施〈重訓器材〉。3.有氧
運動〈登山〉。
第七週:1.有氧運動之練習、慢跑,追逐跑與間歇訓練。
第八週:1.伸展操實施。2.重訓器材之循環訓練。3.無器材之肌力練習。
第九週:校園環山健走測驗。
第十週: 1.有氧運動〈快速登山〉。2.基本肌力練習。
第十一週:1.綜合練習〈循環訓練、靜性肌力訓練、有氧訓練〉。
第十二週: 1.單、雙人伸展操之操作。2.地板肌力訓練〈軀幹腹背肌群〉。
第十三週:1.單、雙人伸展操之操作。2.重訓器材槓鈴介紹與實施〈上肢
肌力練習〉。
第十四週:1.啞鈴練習〈上肢肌力練習〉。2.槓鈴練習〈下肢肌力練習〉。
第十五週:1.綜合練習〈上肢肌力練習、下肢肌力練習、腹背肌之肌力
練習〉
第十六週:1.重訓器材肌耐力之說明練習。2.重訓器材肌瞬發力之說明練
習。
第十七週:1.總複習。2.學習心得分享
第十八週:補測驗

title: 體育[男女合班]—排球初級 Physical Education[man and woman]--Beginning Volleyball
description: 本課程以發展排球初級能力為主.在技術方面:以單項基本技術為主.在戰術方面:以初級難度的比賽隊形為主.在體能方面:以單項基本技術與初級難度比賽隊形的體能為主.在心理方面:以單項基本技術與初級難度比賽隊形的視覺預測與注意力焦點為主.
objectives: 本課程核心能力為:一.具備規劃與執行運動內容的能力.二.具備預防運動傷害的能力.三.具備欣賞運動比賽的能力.四.養成團隊合作能力.五養成終身運動的習慣.

出席率與參與感佔50% ̧三次缺席無法通過本課程.術科測驗佔50% ̧含期中考與期末考.

Practical assessments:50%(including the midterm and final exams)
Students with three absences will not pass the course

(一)1.一般體能2.專項體能。

(三)1.旋轉球2.高手傳球3.低手傳球4.一步助跑攻擊。
(四)1.高手發球2.低手發球。
(五)低手舉球加三步助跑攻擊。

(十四)練習測驗項目。
(十五)接發球測驗。
(十六)隊形練習。

title: 體育[男女合班]—桌球中級 Physical Education [male and female]--Intermediate Table Tennis
description:
1.引領學生認識桌球運動,從桌球技術的項目中學習預測/判斷與決策,融入生活情境中。
2.以遊戲及培養球感的練習方法,引領學生進入桌球世界,使中級學習者學得桌球基本技術與組合性變化,喜歡桌球運動,並進而續選桌球 高級課程。
3.引領學生認識桌球運動各項中階技術/專有名詞以及訓練方法。
4.促進身心發展及培養終身運動之觀念與知識,進而將運動排入生涯時序。
5.本學期因課程需要,需1-2次的課程調整,例如:運動賞析/桌球技術分析/閱讀相關桌球運動之文獻/校外實務教學等安排
備註:未修習過桌球初級課程或僅略懂基本動作(正手抽球/反手推檔/反手切球/正手殺球/正手拉球/步法移位以及組合性動作)者,請勿選習本課程。
objectives:
1.介紹國內外桌球發展現況。
2.強化桌球初級技術與動作,例如:正手發球/正手擊球/正手拉球/正手扣殺/正手切球/正手挑球/反手發球/反手推球/反手擋球/反手挑球/反手拉球/反手切球及步法。除此之外,深入體察桌球技術如何整合練習/球體旋轉概念/訓練方法以及相關之步法運用。
3.學習如何應用穩/快/狠/準/轉/變等六字訣涵義應用於桌球比賽當中。
4.「輔導-落後之學生」與「協助-精進技術與應用之學生」為兩大主軸,藉由分組、建檔、拍攝、記錄並施以種子概念偕同本課程之學生共同提升、精
進與成長。
5.本學期課程目標必須達成上述之要求。
grading:
1.平時成績30% (1)缺、曠課情形(2)遲到、早退(3)上課精神及學習態度。
2.術科考試50%(期中20%(包括:站位/動作執行/力道運用/步法移位/落點掌握/進球率)/期末30%(包括:站位/動作執行/力道運用/步法移位/落點控制/進球率))。
3.體育常識20%(裁判法/專有名詞/雙打比賽/分組對抗賽成績)
weeklyText:
第一週:大綱介紹/進行分組/基本動作檢視/說明本課程之目標/訓練方法介紹。
第二週:正手4條線各15球(20min內完成)推檔2條線15球/正手1/2檯/步法解說。
第三週:正手4條線各15球(20min內完成)推檔2條線15球/左推右攻(2個動作+步法移位)多球練習(輕/重配置)/單球操作左推右攻。
第四週:正手4條線各20球加速狀態(20min內完成)推檔2條線15球/推檔側身+左推右攻(4個動作+步法移位)多球練習(輕重配置)/單球操作推檔側身+左推右攻。
第五週:正手4條線各20球加速狀態(20min內完成)推檔2條線15球/切球型態(正/反手)介紹/發球型態(正反手)介紹:正手---上旋/下旋/右旋/側下旋。反手---上旋/下旋/左旋/側下旋。下蹲式以及高拋式。多球與單球混搭組合練習。
第六週:正手4條線各20球加速狀態(20min內完成)推檔2條線15球/切球與推檔之辨識(轉與不轉)。
第七週:正手4條線各25球(20min內完成)推檔2條線20球/講解期中考項目之相關細則(推/側/推/正手) /正手扣殺講解/推檔+側身扣殺應用。多球與單球混搭組合練習。
第八週:正手4條線各25球加速狀態(20min內完成)推檔2條線20球/複習考試項目:左推+右攻(一人控球/一人練習)。多球與單球混搭組 合練習。
第九週:期中考週:推/側/推/正手(正手擊球)4組X8=32球(拍攝影音檔繳交)。推檔+側身+推擋+正手(4球一組)循環賽—雙打比賽。
第十週:正手4條線各30球(20min內完成)推檔2條線25球/講解正手拉球動作/反手切球+正手拉球(一左一右)反手切球+側身拉球(多球練習)。
第十一週:分隊/分隊共同練習
第十二週:正手4條線各30球加速狀態(20min內完成)推檔2條線25球/正手拉球+正手扣殺反手切球+正手拉球(一左一右)+正手扣殺(多球練習)3球1組。
第十三週:正手4條線各35球(20min內完成)推檔2條線30球/雙打發球與接發球講解。單球實務操作。
第十四週:正手4條線各35球(20min內完成)推檔2條線30球/2人1組各組排點練習賽暨與鄰桌交流賽(單/雙/單/雙/單)。
第十五週:分隊對抗賽
第十六週:期末週

title: 體育[男女合班]—桌球中級 Physical Education [male and female]--Intermediate Table Tennis
description: 本課程旨在學習與培養良好的各種基本技術外,並加強單、雙打技術、戰術的理論與應用的結合,以期能在比賽中獲得有效的成果。且透過課程中針對比賽制度、設計與安排的學習及進行比賽、觀摩,同時學習裁判執法經驗,使學生在享受桌球運動之餘,也能提升良好的社會行為與團隊合作精神。

objectives: 本課程主要係延續網球初級之課程,進一步修正及強化學習者之各項基本技術及觀念,同時在本學期課程中開始融入各項組合練習及腳部移位練習,期使透過不同的單、雙練習情境,使學生能熟練基本技術,並逐漸發展出個人在網球場上的擊球特色,同時也藉此熟悉網球單、雙打比賽的規則、觀念及比賽策略,並在本學期可參觀男女子網球職業賽,讓學生「提升網球技術」列入生活上的學習目標之一。

Tennis Course Grading Policy
The final grade is based on a multifaceted evaluation of technical mastery, tactical execution, and professional conduct.
I. Tactical & Technical Proficiency — 35%
This component assesses stroke mechanics, kinetic chain efficiency, ball control, and tactical decision-making.
Integrated Match Performance (10%):
Directional Control (5%): Accuracy in ball placement and angular control.
Strategic Execution (5%): Proficiency in utilizing various hitting techniques and court strategies.
Comprehensive Fundamental Skills (25%):
Wall Rally (5%): Stability and consistency in continuous hitting.
Short Ball / Drop Shots (5%): Precision in touch and finesse near the net.
Groundstrokes & Lobs (20%): Assessment of baseline depth, power, and high-clear lobs.
Serve & Return (5%): Technical execution and strategic placement of the serve.
II. Daily Performance & Participation — 20%
Evaluation of the student’s Affective Domain, focusing on:
Proactive engagement and initiative during training.
Quality of teacher-student interaction and feedback receptivity.
Overall contribution to the learning environment.
III. Attendance & Conduct — 25%
Zero-Tolerance Policy: Accumulating three (3) or more absences will result in a score of zero (0) for this entire category.
This score integrates both physical attendance and the professional learning attitude demonstrated during class sessions.
IV. Tournament & Match Play (Singles/Doubles) — 10%
Assessment of competitive application, sportsmanship, and tactical awareness during formal singles or doubles match play.
V. Assignments & Documentation — 10%
Submission of multimedia technical analysis and learning journals, including:
Motion Analysis: Freeze-frame and sequential motion analysis.
Technical Logs: Weekly documentation of skill acquisition and self-reflection.
