title: 審計學 Auditing
description:
介紹審計學的基本目的、用途及觀念架構,並藉由學理的解說與實務經驗的補充、呼應,引領同學進入與審計最相關的專門行業:會計師的執業領域,擴展同學對未來職涯規劃的深度、廣度及想像。
This course introduces the fundamental purpose, practical applications, and conceptual framework of auditing. Through theoretical explanations complemented by real-world experiences, it guides students into the professional field most closely related to auditing: the practice of certified public accountants (CPAs). The course aims to broaden and deepen students’ understanding of career planning, expanding both their perspectives and imagination for the future.
objectives:
學生將了解審計專業,審計工作存在的原因和價值,會計師事務所的工作,會計師報告的格式及會計師的法律和專業責任。
Students will understand what the auditing and assurance service are, the reason and objective of the auditing jobs, the works in a CPA firm, the format of the auditor’s reports and the legal and professional responsibility of an auditor.
學生將了解審計程序.審計工作的目標,證據如何收集,如何進行審計規劃,評估審計憑證的重大性及風險,如何進行公司內控的查核,如何偵查公司管理舞弊及設計全面性的審計計劃和程式。
Students will understand the audit procedure, how to collect the audit evidences, how to evaluate the materiality and risk of the audit evidences, how to detect management fraud and design the overall audit plan and program.

description: 本課程主要是介紹成本效益分析(Cost-Benefit Analysis, CBA)在理論探討與實務應用的內容,尤其針對在社會有限資源下,如何能夠透過經濟分析,強化在公共政策或民間企業的未來決策;另外,也會跟同學介紹現階段國內外很常使用的社會投資報酬(Social Returns of Investment, SROI)之理論基礎、操作流程與實作案例,鼓勵同學在修課結束後報考 Social Value International Practitioner 國際級證照,相信修課同學在學期結束後,將可對於相關議題能有更清晰的了解。

title: 行政法 Administrative Law
description:
行政法不但是法律學系重要的基礎學科,更是政治學系學生的重要進階法學訓練課程。行政法並非單獨法典,而是由不同的行政相關法典、大法官會議解釋、行政法院判例及行政機關發布之行政命令或函示所構成。其中,在法律層級,更包括與一般人民權利密切相關之行政程序法、行政執行法和行政罰法,以及人民權利受行政機關違法行政處分侵害時,可尋求救濟之行政訴訟法、訴願法。至於與公務人員權益相關者,還包括公務人員服務法、公務人員任用法、公務人員退休法和公務人員行政中立法等。為幫助學生有效學習行政法,本課程將跨越純法學層次對行政法的探討,整合公共行政領域之政治制度與公法等研究範疇,以理論與實務案例並重的授課方式,讓修課之政治學系學生快速領會行政法之體系架構、重要理論與實用範圍。
本課程為全學年課程。第一學期先以引導學生建立行政法基礎概念為主,從法源、一般原則到各類行政行為(行政處分、行政契約等)之合法性控制;第二學期則進一步探討行政制裁(行政罰)、強制執行、公務員法制,以及人民權利受侵害時之救濟途徑(訴願、行政訴訟)與國家責任(國家賠償),期能培養學生完整處理行政法律問題之能力。為此,本課程將跨越純法學層次對行政法的探討,整合公共行政領域之行政制度與公法等研究範疇,以理論與實務案例並重的授課方式,讓修課之公共行政學系學生快速領會行政法之體系架構、重要理論與實用範圍。
objectives:
一、課程目標 (Course Objectives)
課程進行將以清楚易懂之方式,幫助學生系統性的學習及建構行政法學的知識體系,強調「基礎理論」與「實務應用」並重,故有以下具體目標:
(一)建構完整體系
引導學生從憲法基礎出發,融會貫通行政法之原理原則、行政作用、行政救濟等核心領域,建立見樹又見林的法律思維 。
(二)培養實戰能力
透過案例分析,培養學生在面對公務生活、職場工作或國家考試時,具備精準的法律問題意識與解決問題之能力 。
(三)提升學習興趣
以深入淺出的講授方式,降低法學入門門檻,讓非法律系背景同學也能領略行政法學的邏輯之美與實用價值,進而產生學習樂趣 。
二、學習成效(Student Learning Outcomes)
(一)專業知識掌握
修課學生將有系統地建構行政法學的完整體系。透過本課程,學生不僅能理解「依法行政」、「比例原則」及「信賴保護」等重要原理原則,亦能清楚區辨行政處分、行政契約、法規命令等各類行政行為的法律性質與構成要件。同時,學生亦須學習《行政程序法》、《行政罰法》、《行政執行法》及行政救濟制度的主要規範內容,進而掌握行政法之理論基礎。
(二)實務應用能力
課程設計著重培養學生解決具體法律爭點之實用能力,透過指標性判決與實例演練,學生將學會運用「涵攝」技術,將抽象的法律規範適用於複雜的行政爭議個案(例如公務員懲戒、違建拆除等)。不僅能提升學生在未來公務職涯中識別法律風險與依法行政之能力,亦能強化其在國家考試申論題中建立層次分明、論證嚴謹的答題技巧 。
(三)價值判斷與人文關懷
課程進行中,將引導學生反思在法治國(Rechtsstaat)原則下,行政權力行使與人民基本權利保障之間的動態平衡,培養對公共事務的敏銳度。學生將不只停留在法規的字面解釋,更能從合法性與正當性的雙重維度,對重大行政決策或社會議題進行批判性思考,具備身為公共行政專業人才應有的社會關懷與價值視野 。

title: 比較行政 Comparative Administration
description:
比較行政學是源於戰後西方國家對落後國家現代化研究之其中一項分支,是一種西方本位的學問,強調未來與西方發展之趨同性。本課程定位上改以我國/東方為中心,透過各國與我國公共行政發展之比較,來進行自我瞭解及反思我國行政管理制度之特徵,剖析我國與其他國家行政運作異同之處。透過比較分析讓學生領悟我國行政制度之運作邏輯與優缺點,也可以透過對國外制度之剖析,發掘我國行政改革之各種可能性及盲點。現實上,作為後進同時兼具悠久深厚行政發展的國家,我國不斷移植國外經驗到本身既有制度之中,究竟兩者之兼容程度為何?我們是否錯誤學習某些國外經驗?移植國外經驗是否必須符合某些先決條件?在回答這些問題前,我們應先好好學習國外制度的邏輯,並與我國制度作有系統的比較。以上是本課程的學習主旨。
本課程首先針對行政體系比較的主要面向進行授課,當中會對比我國的相關體制發展。除期末考試外,同學須閱讀一篇本課程所附的學術文獻,並作心得報告;此外,修課同學會以分組形式自行開發專題,比較我國與國外公共行政與政策之異同,作為學習成果。

title: 公共政策 Public Policy

公共政策是政府機關制定來解決公共問題並尋求社會福趾而採取的行動。在制定公共政策過程中之複雜及涉及社會上的不同利益,因此本課程以學習到公共政策理論來應用到實際的政策制定過程及增加我們對社會及政治體系的認識。
本課程希望從公共政策理論、方法及案例配合,來達到以下的目的:
認識公共政策理論;
認識制定公共政策過程中的各因素; 及
反思政府制定公共政策的方案

title: 政府預算與財政 Public Budget and Finance
description:
本課程旨在引導學生全面了解公共預算與財政的基本概念、制度與相關議題,並深入探討政府財務行政管理的過程及其實務應用。課程內容涵蓋公共預算的意義、編製、審議與執行等流程,探討政府在財政上的角色與功能、成本效益分析及租稅制度。透過教學講義、即時資料查詢、問題導向學習、分組報告與遊戲化教學等多元方法,提升學生批判思考、解決問題與實務操作能力,使其在未來能具備分析與理解公共預算與財政事務的能力。
This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the basic concepts, systems, and related issues of public budgeting and finance, with a focus on both theoretical knowledge and practical applications. It covers the meaning, preparation, review, and implementation of public budgets, the roles and functions of government in finance, cost-benefit analysis, and the tax system. Through diverse teaching methods—such as lecture notes, real-time data inquiries, problem-based learning, group presentations, and gamification—students will enhance their critical thinking, problem-solving, and practical skills, preparing them to effectively analyze and interpret public budgeting and financial affairs in their future careers or academic pursuits.
objectives:
課程目標
建立學生對公共預算與財政之核心概念及制度架構的理解。
培養學生分析政府財務運作及政策影響的能力。
增進學生應用成本效益分析與財政評估工具的能力。
養成學生批判性思考與解決公共財政問題的能力。
提升學生在公共預算與財政領域的實務操作與溝通表達能力。
學習成效
修畢本課程後,學生應能:
說明公共預算與財政的基本概念、流程與制度。
分析並評估政府財務政策與預算編製的影響。
運用成本效益分析等方法,提出具可行性的財政建議。
透過分組討論與報告,展現協作與口頭表達能力。
具備解讀財務數據與理解財政決策背景的能力。
Course Objectives
To develop students’ understanding of the core concepts and institutional frameworks of public budgeting and finance.
To equip students with the ability to analyze government financial operations and policy impacts.
To enhance students’ capacity to apply cost-benefit analysis and fiscal assessment tools.
To cultivate critical thinking and problem-solving skills in the field of public finance.
To improve practical skills and communication abilities related to public budgeting and finance.
Learning Outcomes
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:
Explain the fundamental concepts, processes, and systems of public budgeting and finance.
Analyze and evaluate the impacts of government fiscal policies and budget preparation.
Apply methods such as cost-benefit analysis to provide feasible fiscal recommendations.
Demonstrate teamwork and oral communication skills through group discussions and presentations.
Interpret financial data and understand the context of fiscal decision-making.

title: 行政學 Public Administration
description: 本課程為公共行政領域之基礎課程,課程內容在於介紹公共行政理論與實務的基本內涵,為一學年之課程。上學期授課主題為公共行政領域的基礎概念與理論背景,包含公共行政的概念、行政學的理論、政府行政組織、政府行政管理、政府資源管理、公務人員角色規範等主題。下學期主要為政策管理、公共管理以及公共行政最新議題及展望等議題。
objectives: 本課程以國內外行政學的基礎教科書主題為依據,學生藉由瞭解行政學的主要內涵與相關理論,得以培養對於公共行政學科的興趣,進而思考台灣當前公共行政的主要議題及脈絡,儲備分析公共行政及處理公共事務的相關能力,奠定未來從事公共行政實務或研究工作的基礎。對於有志投身公職的學生,本課程亦希望藉此讓學生了解國家文官所必備之核心素養、專業知能、以及公共服務價值觀。課程設計除了教授面對面授課,亦透過教材研讀、政府部門實務界專家與系友的演講與互動、電影欣賞、個案討論、主題報告影片製作、及測驗等多元方式,充實學生公共行政的理論及知識,激發學生對於我國公共行政實務分析與理論研究的興趣。
grading:
1. 考試(70%):
期中考30%、期末考各占40%,以上課教材內容為主要範圍,所有考試皆為關書筆試,並以課堂講授之各主題章節為範圍,題目形式為選擇題、解釋名詞或簡答題、情境申論題。
2. 專題/行政專有名詞解說報告(20%):
本學期共有五個行政學探究主題,分別為「行政學理論內涵」、「政府行政組織」、「政府行政管理」、「政府資源管理」以及「公務人員角色規範」,所有同學須選擇一個主題做一個專有名詞解說影片;影片報告時間約5分鐘,期末時上傳至老師指定平臺。
3. 課堂回應與出席(10%)
課堂參與包含出席及發言;而於課堂及Moodle者,依主動發言次數於期末成績予以加分。

title: 行政統計學 Fundamental Statistics for Public Administration
description:
首先,讓我們先談談許多同學心中的大哉問:「當初我就是討厭數學才選社會組的,為啥公共行政學系、甚至所有社會科學領域科系的統計學都還要必修 XD」
作為所有專業領域(包括公共行政與政策)的資料科學(data science,如圖)入門課程,本課程主要是讓從未接觸過統計分析方法的同學,具備公共行政與政策專業中量化資料分析的基礎知識與技能,並有助於銜接進階專業課程(公行系學士班113-115學年度適用必修科目表、公行系學士班114-1學期必選修課程)。
課程首先介紹敘述統計(descriptive statistics)與相關圖表的製作與呈現;其次將介紹作為推論統計(inferential statistics)基礎的相關機率理論(probability theory)與抽樣分配(sampling distribution);最後則操作推論統計分析中常用的點估計與區間估計,並實作卡方檢定、變異數分析、相關與簡單迴歸分析。
除了運用統計知識的紙筆計算,本課程也須搭配演練電腦軟體 ,如微軟 Excel、Google 試算表、與 JASP (開源免費的專業統計軟體)。另外,鑑於生成式人工智慧(generative artificial intelligence, GenAI)工具的普及,本課程也將搭配善用政大的 @g.nccu.edu.tw 帳號操作 Gemini 輔助學習,相信也有利於修課同學們後續自學、或銜接本校相關專業課程(例如 AI 中心的相關學程)。

title: 研究設計與方法 Research Design and Methods
description:
*計畫修課與加選同學請務必出席第一堂課,未出席者學期成績將評定為 0 分,請自行退選。唯有同時實體出席第一堂課並完成第一堂課出席問卷的同學,才視為完整出席第一堂課。
本課程為針對研究方法所設計的基礎課程,包含對於量化以及質性的介紹與應用,課程目的在於讓同學對於社會科學研究的認識,加強學生的實務操作能力,培養同學對於研究方法的應用,循序漸進地練習社會科學研究過程中的各項步驟,期許同學能實際應用。本課程與政治大學新生書院導師陳立威合作,10:10-10:30 將由陳立威老師帶領同學進行合作學習與反思。
本課程具有高度參與性、實際整合應用性、並且需要團隊協力合作(依照實際學生人數,由授課教師分組)。本課程設計著重實作練習與實際課堂參與互動,所有課堂作業與練習皆為培養同學對於研究方法的應用,循序漸進地練習社會科學研究過程中的各項步驟,因此上課出席、實際參與及課前預習將關鍵性決定學生成效。
*課程主題及進度將依照講者時間及演講細節、校外教學安排、學生學習狀況及需求等進行適時調整(例如必要時:調換週次、延後下課),若有變更將提前告知,精彩充實的課程活動安排需要共同協調配合,請慎重考慮課程時間並全程參與。
*未出席上課且未有符合學校請假規定事由將不得參與當天課程隨堂活動、團體報告相關作業、其他需要被評分的作業,若有未能出席上課事由,請事前email同時通知授課教師與教學助理(email以外方式無效,請勿私訊)並取得許可。須提供相關證明,並於學校系統完成請假程序。
*本課程將進行課程記錄(例如:課堂觀察、攝影與錄影等),並將進行教學研究設計與創新課程建構、開發合作學習新教材,以促進學生學習成效,進而提升公共行政領域大學生「社會科學研究方法學習成效」與「進行學習與研究之多元核心能力」。
objectives:
本課程介紹相關之質化及量化研究方法,使同學對社會科學之研究方法有基本的認識,熟悉資料蒐集、分析與詮釋的方式,並培養從事社會科學研究的能力,同時能應用所學。目標:1. 學生對社會科學研究方法具有基本的認識與實作應用;2. 培養質化與量化研究分析能力,同時省思研究倫理並確實遵守; 3. 培養進行學習與研究的多元核心能力(團隊合作與領導能力、批判性思考與分析能力、多元關懷與跨領域思考) 。
本計畫預期透過合作學習的實踐,在修習「研究設計與方法」課程後,能有效提升學生的學習成效。學習成效分為兩個面向:
學生進行學習與研究之多元核心能力:本研究將多元核心能力著重在團隊合作與問題解決能力、批判性思考與分析能力、多元關懷與跨領域思考。
社會科學研究方法學習成效:本計畫期待學生學習課程內容後,能發展並提升進行社會科學研究之能力。
grading:
本課程設計著重實作練習與實際課堂參與互動,所有課堂作業與練習皆為培養同學對於研究方法,循序漸進地練習社會科學研究過程中的各項步驟,因此上課出席、實際參與及課前預習將關鍵性決定學生成效。
*本學期無故缺席 2 次且未事先取得許可,將導致課堂參與成績 0 分,未經許可無故缺席每次扣總成績5分。本學期無故缺席1/3且未事先取得許可,將導致學期總成績0分。請假規則請參閱並依照「國立政治大學學生請假規則」,事先辦理請假手續,如有特殊情況,請立即 email 通知授課教師與助教。
*團體作業成績將依照實際團隊參與的角色與貢獻度、自評與同儕評鑑結果評分。未實際參與的團體實作與作業部分也將導致 0 分。
*本學期研究計畫主題需於期中考前確定,期中考後將不得更換主題。

title: 組織理論與管理 Organization Theory and Management
description: 本課程將區分為兩大部分,循序漸進地了解組織理論與管理的內涵。學期前半將介紹個體與組織的差異以及這些差異所可能帶來的管理問題,並逐一深入探討激勵理論、學習理論、領導風格以及衝突理論等議題。學期後半段,將著重在公部門管理以及管理工具的應用上,透過團體報告及個案討論等方式,使同學充分理解與體會組織理論與管理的樣貌。
objectives: 本課程之主要目標,在使大家熟悉組織理論以及組織管理上可能面臨之各種挑戰。在不同的組織中,組織內部要素間的相互作用、以及組織與外部環境的相互作用皆會有所不同,因此,如何在變動的環境中追尋不變的組織基本理論架構就越顯重要。本課程除介紹組織理論與行為的基礎知識概念外,也將從公共管理實務中挑選適切的主題,能夠將所學理論運用於公部門管理實務上。
grading: 一、課堂參與及討論:30% 本課程為組織行為基礎知識建構之重要課程,課前預習以及積極的課堂參與討論,將能夠讓所學與現實生活結合,幫助理論與概念的理解與融會貫通。 出席(10%):老師將於學期末綜合評量出席程度給分。 課堂參與 (20%):老師將於學期末綜合評量參與程度給分。上課主動發言並對課堂有貢獻者,老師將給予加分鼓勵。 二、摘要報告及個案討論(Presentation & Case Study):30% 分五組、每組7~8人(視修課人數調整),每組將各自負責兩週之主題(學期前半、後半各一週,粗體標示之週次為可選週次),除閱讀及摘要該週主題之教材內容外,需準備一個與該主題有關之時事或案例,並於課堂上進行報告(請準備PowerPoint投影片及相關補充資料),報告時間約20~30分鐘。 負責報告之組別應準備3個問題,於報告完畢時提出,並帶領同學們進行團體討論,討論時間約15分鐘。 三、學期報告:40% 期中報告(計畫書):20% 學期報告分5組、每組7~8人(視修課人數調整),各組應於學期結束時繳交一份學期報告。期中報告時,應繳交書面的研究計畫書、並給予口頭報告,計畫書之內容應包括公部門人力篩選之相關規劃。請於10/26 (一) 10pm前,將期中報告上傳至Moodle(請提供Word檔)。 期末報告:20% 期末報告包含書面報告及口頭報告,完整的報告除計畫書之內容外,應加入實際選才規劃應用之實驗結果及討論等內容。請於12/21(一) 10pm前,將期末報告上傳至Moodle(請提供Word檔)。 最終修正版期末報告請於12/29(二) 4pm前上傳至Moodle資料夾中(請提供Word檔)。 學術倫理 本堂課所繳交之報告,內容如有借用過去研究發現、引用過去文獻內容者,應清楚註明出處。如有抄襲之情事經查證屬實,學期成績將以零分計算,並且按照校內規定辦理。

title: 公共政策新興議題 Emerging Issues of Public Policy
description: 這門課程專為大一學生設計,旨在提供公共政策領域的啟蒙學習機會。課程的第一個特色是其基礎性和啟蒙性,幫助學生初步了解公共政策的基本概念和重要性,為未來的進階學習奠定堅實的基礎。第二個特色是課程師資的多樣性與豐富性,除了由政大公共行政學系的專業老師授課外,還邀請了幾位優秀學長回校與學生分享他們在公共政策領域的經驗與見解,這將為學生提供更廣泛的視野與實踐經驗。第三個特色是課程形式靈活,每週一個小時,專注於當前公共政策的最新議題。每次課堂中,將由一位老師針對其專長領域的公共政策新興議題進行深入講解,並與學生進行互動討論,鼓勵學生積極參與並發表自己的見解,從而提升他們對公共政策的興趣與理解。
objectives:
(一) 心得文章撰寫(佔總成績60%)
心得報告:本學期當中,為了確保同學上課的參與,並鼓勵學生對課程內容進行批判性的思索,學生將負責完成十篇心得報告。其做法為,同學在學期中必須選擇數次自己喜歡的演講內容,於上課後一週,繳交心得文章,並放上Moodle平台。字數不超過500字(單行間距12號字形約一頁)。內容請含下列三個項目:
主要討論議題
主要論述內容與結論
您個人的評論與看法 (重要!請務必提出)
(二) 上課到課與參與(佔總成績40%: 30%到課,10%發問)
不論是到課或是上課參與,都將列入計分,一次沒來扣兩分直到前一部份30分扣完為止。問問題是思考的開始,能思考才會問問題,有了問題才能夠解決問題,這些就是觀察公共事務的首要修養,因此,本課程十分重視課堂討論,請學生務必參與發問與討論,上課「有意義」的發言將使提高學生參與成績。允許請假三次, 第四次開始扣分

title: 公共價值與公務倫理 Public Values and Public Service Ethics
description:
「倫理」涉及人的價值觀念、行為規範及社會秩序。而各行各業,不同部門都有特定的倫理觀及規範。這些觀念及規範有一些共同之處,也因應行業性質,會有一些特殊考量及規範。本課程是分析討論公部門工作之倫理問題,涉及公共價值及各專業的倫理觀。本課程會從應然面與實然面探討公務倫理之各個面向,並針對國內外的公務倫理實踐情況(包括政策制度及真實個案)做具體分析。公務倫理建設是公部門良好運作的重要基石,但這也是公部門管理一直以來難以克服的問題之一。本課程企圖建立正確公務倫理觀,為即將進入公部門工作的學生打好相關基礎(即應然面);同時,也企圖點出公務倫理建設所面臨的各種挑戰與矛盾(即實然面),以學術觀點整理各種公務倫理問題之本質。而作為一般公民,也應對影響公共事務運作的公務倫理有所認識。修讀本課程之同學需學習以道德思維分析各種公務倫理困境。本課程期末要求同學分組就各類公務倫理問題進行個案資料蒐集,透過道德推理(moral reasoning)進行分析,提出合理的處理方案。
本課程安排三分之二時間為老師授課,講授公務倫理的基本知識、學術觀點及政府之相關政策措施,並引用經典個案作為闡釋。最後部分為同學分組報告(三至四人一組,共分為十二組)。為使報告能涵蓋所有面向(1、公務人員與政治關係;2、公、私部門關係;3、行政運作(含公共服務輸送);4公共決策),分組會進行議題抽籤,就其抽中之議題面向尋找適當個案,進行資料蒐集及分析,最後進行口頭及書面報告。每組口頭報告會安排另一組進行評論。

title: 公民社會組織與創新 Civil Society Organizations and Innovation
description:
「第三部門」是什麼?日常生活中常見的非營利組織、非政府組織、公益與慈善組織、志願服務組織、公民社會組織、草根組織與社會服務組織,伴隨民主化而興起,對政府治理與公民社會發展扮演關鍵角色。
本課程介紹非營利組織與公民社會的概念與理論,分析其角色與功能,探討非營利組織、政府與企業之間的關係,並進一步聚焦於社會創新(social innovation)與社會企業如何回應當代公共議題,包括社區營造、環境與永續轉型,以及跨國的政策移轉與比較治理。
objectives:
課程目標(Course Objectives)
分析公民社會組織與社會創新的基礎概念與理論。
應用理論架構,評估社會需求、組織動態與創新模式。
透過台灣、中國大陸與香港的比較,認識不同政治社會脈絡下公民社會的發展路徑與差異。
批判性地分析國家—社會關係如何形塑公民社會組織的角色、空間與限制(以中國大陸與香港為例)。
將共同參與、協力合作建制於團隊互動中,並能以簡潔、清晰的方式書寫報告與有效溝通。
預期學習成效(Intended Learning Outcomes)
知識/認知:具備公民社會、非營利組織與社會創新領域之專業知識。
人格特質:批判性思考與自省;對多元與包容的熱忱。
價值/倫理:擁抱多元、關懷弱勢、追求社會正義。
能力:社區進入、利害關係人分析、比較政策分析與創新方案規劃。

title: 地方治理 Local Governance
description:
目前地方公共事務已非由地方政府單方以行政命令或層級指揮方式處理,而是涉及中央部會、地方行政機關、地方議會、社區組織、非營利組織、民間企業、公民團體及在地居民等多元行動者之共同參與與協力。因此,地方治理同時涉及地方自治制度、地方行政與立法關係,亦涵蓋地方財政、公民參與、社區治理、城市發展、地方創生與永續發展等面向。
本課程以我國地方自治制度與相關法制為基礎,將分別介紹地方政府、地方自治及地方治理之基本學理,說明我國地方自治之歷史沿革、地方自治團體之法律地位、自治權限及地方財政制度。其次,課程亦將進一步探討地方選舉、府會關係、公民參與、社區治理、原住民族自治、跨域治理、智慧城市,以及地方創生及地方永續發展等地方自治相關議題。
本課程將以教師講授、法規與理論導讀、個案討論及地方自治問題觀察,帶領修課學生將制度與理論應用於實際地方公共問題案例之分析。
objectives:
一、課程目標
引導學生理解地方政府、地方自治與地方治理的基本概念及其差異。
幫助學生認識對我國地方自治制度、地方政府組織及自治權限。
說明地方行政機關、地方議會、中央政府及其他治理行動者之間的互動關係。
培養學生分析地方財政、公共服務、公民參與及跨域合作問題之能力。
帶領學生運用地方治理理論分析實際地方公共政策與社區問題。
幫助學生能針對具體地方治理問題,提出兼具合法性、可行性與公共價值之治理方案。
二、學習成效
認識地方治理與地方自治法制:促進學生對地方政府、地方自治、地方分權與地方治理之理論與概念,以及地方自治制度之歷史背景、沿革、法制運作、中央與地方的權限劃分等主題的認識與暸解。
分析地方行政、立法機關之互動與政策形成:提升學生學習地方選舉、地方派系、府會關係,以及跨域治理、公私協力、社區治理和公民參與等課程主題之興趣。

title: 科技法律與資料治理 Technology Law and Data Governance
description:
I. Course Objectives
This course is designed to help students understand the legal and governance issues arising from the development of digital technologies, with data governance as its central focus. It addresses major emerging topics, including personal data protection, artificial intelligence governance, digital platform accountability, open government data, data sharing, cybersecurity, cross-border data flows, and the European Union(EU)’s data governance framework.
Taught entirely in English, the course introduces students to core concepts in contemporary international technology law. It examines legal issues that arise throughout the data life cycle, from collection, processing, use, retention, and sharing to deletion. The course also considers the legality of artificial intelligence systems in model training and content generation, and analyzes the respective responsibilities and obligations of governments, businesses, digital platforms, and data intermediaries in data governance.
The course further incorporates Taiwan’s legal framework, the EU’s General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), Data Governance Act, Data Act, Artificial Intelligence Act, and other significant legislative developments and international trends. Through this comparative approach, students will develop a stronger interest in technology law and acquire the analytical skills needed to address practical legal issues.
II. Course Description
This course begins with legal issues related to data use as an entry point into technology law. It introduces key legal concepts, including personal data protection, informational self-determination, privacy, and data governance, before moving to issues such as open government data, data sharing, data intermediary services, data altruism, data access for Internet of Things devices and connected products, cloud switching, regulation of artificial intelligence technologies, algorithmic transparency, disclosure obligations, and legal requirements for cross-border data transfers.
The course focuses on recent developments in the EU’s data governance regime and explains how the GDPR, Data Governance Act, Data Act, and Artificial Intelligence Act together shape a technology law framework grounded in trustworthiness, data access, and risk management. In addition to introducing major international technology laws, the course includes weekly case discussions to help students examine the relationship between data governance, personal data protection, public interest, industrial innovation, digital market competition, national data sovereignty, and the protection of fundamental rights.
objectives:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
Understand the foundational theories and regulatory structure of technology law and data governance.
Examine legal issues concerning personal data protection, data sharing, digital platform regulation, risk-based regulation of artificial intelligence, and cybersecurity safeguards.
Compare Taiwan’s digital legal framework with the GDPR, Data Governance Act, Data Act, and other major technology laws of the EU.
Assess, from legal and governance perspectives, personal data protection risks and appropriate levels of regulatory oversight arising from artificial intelligence and other technological applications.
Analyze current disputes and cases involving the application of technology law from an independent perspective and propose appropriate legal or policy reforms.

title: 治理中國:政治變遷、社會轉型與台港澳關係 Governing China: Political Change, Social Transformation, and Relations with Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macau
description:
This course examines the rise of China as the defining force shaping politics and society across the Greater China region. Over the past four decades, the People’s Republic of China (PRC) has transformed from a poor, isolated polity into the world’s second-largest economy and a leading geopolitical power — with profound consequences not only for its own governance but for its relationship with Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan, three societies bound to the mainland by deep cultural and historical ties yet possessing distinct institutional inheritances. The course asks: how has China’s rise reshaped the political institutions, social fabric, and external relationships of each of these polities, and what does the resulting variation tell us about the reach and the limits of Chinese-style governance?
The first half of the course maps the mainland system that drives these dynamics: major theoretical traditions for understanding Chinese politics (authoritarian resilience, fragmented and consultative authoritarianism, adaptive governance, party-state institutionalism); the organisation, ideology, and cadre system of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) under Xi Jinping; political change and policy implementation under the post-2012 leadership; the social transformation generated by urbanisation, hukou reform, demographic change, and growing inequality; and state–society relations including civil society, religion, ethnic politics, surveillance, and platform politics.
The second half traces how the rise of China has reshaped — and is being reshaped by — its peripheries. In Hong Kong, the asymmetric integration of the Special Administrative Region into the mainland’s political and economic order has accelerated since 2014, culminating in the 2020 National Security Law, the 2021 “patriots-only” electoral overhaul, and the 2024 Safeguarding National Security Ordinance (Article 23). In Macau, the rise of China has been managed through a quieter politics of accommodation, with deepening integration into the Greater Bay Area and continued reliance on a gaming economy increasingly aligned with Beijing’s strategic priorities. In Taiwan, China’s rise has driven both deepening economic interdependence (trade, investment, ECFA, semiconductors) and an intensifying security competition, with democratisation, identity politics, the 2024 presidential election, and the role of the United States all shaping the cross-Strait equation. The final two weeks are reserved for student case presentations.
objectives: By the end of the course, students should be able to: (1) compare leading theoretical models of Chinese governance and assess their analytical reach; (2) explain how the CCP organises power and recruits, monitors, and disciplines cadres; (3) trace the principal directions of political change under Xi Jinping; (4) analyse social transformation and state–society contention in mainland China; (5) compare the post-handover political trajectories of Hong Kong and Macau; (6) account for the trajectory of Taiwan’s democratisation and cross-Strait relations; and (7) deliver a research-grade case study and reflection note that engage critically with primary scholarship.

title: 全球衛生治理 Global Health Governance
description:
Today’s world is becoming more interconnected and globalized. Public health issues — such as infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases, climate change, and emerging technologies — are no longer national or regional problems; they are increasingly addressed through a global, integrated, and multidisciplinary approach.
This course empowers students, future policy-makers, and practitioners to analyze and engage with global health issues. Each week introduces a topic in global health governance — such as the World Health Organization and the International Health Regulations, pandemic preparedness, climate change and human health, health technology and digital health, health financing, and One Health — led by the instructors or invited guest speakers. Reflecting recent World Health Assembly priorities, the 2026 edition gives expanded attention to climate change and human health, health technology, and the financing of global health.
In the final weeks, the class executes a simulated public health emergency under the World Health Organization framework (the WHO Simulation), joined by outside experts, civil society, and journalists. Students are divided into four to five countries and assigned roles as key legal, policy, and public health decision-makers responding to the scenario. The simulation consolidates what students learn across the term and builds their competencies in global health governance.
objectives:
• Understand current global health issues and risks, including emerging infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases, climate change, and the role of new health technologies.
• Understand how global health governance works — its institutions, strengths, and weaknesses in addressing global health challenges.
• Develop the ability to participate in international conferences, deliver oral presentations, and collaborate in teams.
• Build research capabilities using media, literature, and databases, and gain front-line experience of health policy-making through the WHO Simulation.
• Broaden horizons beyond students’ own disciplines, deepening understanding of public health, biomedicine, law, and international relations.

• Project presentation and report — 30%
• WHO Simulation — 40%

title: 認識災害管理與風險治理 Introduction of Emergency Management and Risk Governance
description: 邁入風險社會時代,面對氣候變遷帶來的極端氣候影響,防救災已成為我國政府與民眾不可忽視的重要課題。本課程透過閱讀相關文獻以及課堂活動,認識災害管理與風險治理相關議題與研究,課程的進行採教師講課、學生分組導讀、課堂討論活動,以及邀請業師演講或校外參訪等多元方式進行,讓修課學生藉此了解災害管理與風險治理相關領域之研究與實務。此外,修課學生需設計個人/家庭防災計畫書於期末課堂上進行口頭報告。本課程依照修課學生之研究興趣,藉由閱讀相關理論累積專業知識,以及師生之間的互動討論,建立災害管理與風險治理的基本知能,並希望能從社會科學面向幫助修課學生認識災害相關研究,並同步提升個人防災意識。
objectives: 本課程透過社會科學角度來認識災害管理與風險治理,以幫助學生:1) 學習災害管理、風險治理的基本概念;2)了解台灣災防相關歷史、組織、體系、與政策;以及3)思考防救災過程中,政治與領導、組織協力、智慧防災、風險溝通、社區防災、防災教育等議題。修課學生期能藉由研讀資料與文獻、參與課堂討論與活動,建立對災害管理與風險治理概念的初步認識與知能,培養災防研究之興趣,並提升個人防救災意識。
grading:
分組導讀 (30%)、設計個人/家庭防災計畫(40%,包含紙本報告25%、期末口頭報告15%)、演講心得(15%)、課堂參與討論與出席 (15%)
一、課堂分組導讀(30%):針對課程的主題內容,修課學生分組進行導讀,每組成員約2-3位,整學期各組約導讀2次,導讀內容須包含文獻摘要與問題討論兩大部分,以簡報方式呈現,並鼓勵結合時事進行相關個案或新聞的介紹。當周負責導讀小組,導讀時間以60分鐘為原則,針對每篇導讀文章至少須提出2項問題,並在上課前三天,先將討論問題上傳Moodle供其他同學閱讀。 其中教材若設為參考用,則不列入導讀範圍。若組員當中無大學部學生,則需額外找一篇與該週主題相關的中英文期刊文章進行導讀介紹。
評分標準參考:
二、個人/家庭防災計畫(40%,包含紙本報告25%、期末口頭報告15%):修課學生每人期末時需繳交個人/家庭防災計畫書,並於期末時透過口頭報告與同學們分享。個人/家庭防災計畫書須包含以下幾大部分:
詳細介紹個人/家庭居住地主要的災害潛勢 [20%]
回顧當地災害史 [20%]
規劃居家逃生路線、介紹鄰近避難處所以及規劃會合地點[20%]
建立緊急連絡方式[10%][個資部分請隱匿呈現]
緊急避難包的介紹與準備[10%]
建立緊急食物、飲水、醫藥、工具裝備確認表 [10%]
建立重要證件、文件、緊急避難金確認表 [10%][個資部分請隱匿呈現]
口頭報告以時間控制、報告內容清楚與熟悉程度、計劃書依個人狀況詳細設計程度、報告的是否準時繳交PPT等項目來評分。
三、演講心得(15%)
演講心得撰寫需繳交至少1000字心得感想,繳交方式為上傳至Moodle;心得內容須結合課程主題,並於最後提出一至兩個討論問題做為反思與回饋,並請依規定時間繳交電子檔與紙本。
四、課堂出席與參與(15%)
將參照事前課堂提問內容、課堂上發言次數,與出席情況計分。
A(90分以上) | 優良,導讀文獻內容完整且正確清楚呈現重點,口頭報告PPT具有內容且活潑有創意,報告人口條清楚且在表定時間內完成報告。
B(89-80分) | 佳,導讀文獻內容完整,內容符合所有要求外,口頭報告PPT具有內容,報告人口條清楚且在表定時間內完成報告。
C(79-70分) | 尚可,大致交代導讀文獻內容,內容大致符合要求,口頭報告PPT有基本架構,報告人在表定時間內完成報告,但報告人口條待加強。
D(69-60分) | 及格,內容勉強符合要求,口頭報告PPT內容架構鬆散,報告人口條不清楚,對自己所要報告的內容不熟悉,未能在表定時間內完成報告。
E(59分以下) | 不及格,內容不符合要求,未能準時繳交作業,未上傳導讀提問,口頭報告PPT內容架構鬆散,報告人口條不清楚,對自己所要報告的內容不熟悉,未能在表定時間內完成報告。

title: 思辨:當代社會議題 Contemporary Social Problems and Justice
description:
This course is designed to introduce the benefits and methods of interdisciplinary study and research for exploring complex social problems and justice. Starting with the U.S. and Taiwan contexts as its foundation, this course expands its global context and weekly discussions by featuring several talented guest lecturers specializing in public administration and management. Their diverse international insights and perspectives provide a rich learning environment.
Students will be guided through the process by learning and applying critical thinking, problem identification, and problem-solving skills to discuss and explore creative policy approaches that integrate differing perspectives.
* Course Schedule and Adjustments:
The course topics and schedule may be adjusted based on speaker availability and details, field trips, as well as students' learning progress and needs. Changes such as rescheduling sessions or extending class time until 12:30 PM may occur when necessary. Any modifications will be announced in advance. As the course includes engaging and diverse activities, your cooperation is essential. Please carefully consider the course schedule and commit to full participation.
* Class Time and Attendance:
Classes begin promptly at 9:20 AM. Please arrive on time and follow the teaching assistant’s instructions at the start of class to complete the required activities, which will help facilitate the day’s lesson. There will be one scheduled break during the session, depending on the course progress.
* Attendance Policy:
Students who plan to enroll in or add to the course must attend the first class. Failure to do so will result in a final grade of zero (0) for the semester, and you will be responsible for withdrawing from the course. Only students who are physically present and complete the First-Day class attendance survey and self-introduction will be considered to have fully attended. First-day attendance and Regular Participation are required. Please read the course schedule carefully.
* Absence and Leave Policy:
Students who are absent without a valid reason, as outlined in the university’s leave policies, will not be allowed to participate in in-class activities, group presentations, or any graded assignments for that day. If you are unable to attend, please notify both the instructor and teaching assistant in advance via email (other forms of communication, such as messaging apps, will not be accepted) and obtain approval. Supporting documentation is required, and you must also complete the official leave process through the university’s system.
* This syllabus is a guide for the course and is subject to change with advance notice. Please pay attention to the newest course announcements, email notifications, and Moodle for updated course materials.
*AI tools may be used only when permitted and in strict accordance with assignment instructions; students must clearly disclose their use, take full responsibility for the content, and ensure academic integrity through proper citation.
*This course is highly participatory, integrative, and collaborative. All assignments are designed to guide students in building critical thinking, problem identification, and problem-solving skills.
objectives:
This course is highly participatory, integrative, and collaborative. Please note that this course is designed as a project-based learning approach with relevant tasks at different phases to help you develop your project and respond to feedback. All assignments are designed to guide students in completing their final project, developing critical thinking, problem identification, and problem-solving skills.
At the completion of this course, students will be able to:
Understand the process and language of interdisciplinary study and research.
Build tolerance for dissonance in conducting interdisciplinary study and research.
Build a deeper understanding of diversity, inclusion, and social justice embedded in the context of interdisciplinary social problems.
Analyze and apply perspectives of multiple disciplines to shape your understanding of complex social problems and social justice.
Critically examine, interpret, and explain the multiple perspectives from disciplines of social science that apply to complex social problems and creative policy solutions/resources.
Practice collaborative, interdisciplinary approaches to problem identification and disciplinary integration.
grading:
* Each student is expected to:
Actively participate in course discussions, in-class activities, and group project assignments
Complete all required assignments and activities on time
* All the assignments are designed to guide you in completing your final project with your critical thinking, problem identification, and problem-solving skills.
* All students are required to attend each class meeting and be ready to discuss the reading materials and assigned social problems with others.
Evaluation:
Preparation, Engagement, and Participation (including In-Class Activities, Peer Feedback, Self and Peer Evaluation, and After-Class Feedback) (10%)
* Absence 3 times without university-eligible reasons and permission from Dr. Shie in advance will lead to zero credit.
* Also, absence will lead to zero credit for those weekly assignments assigned for the week absent.
* When submitting assignments, students must clearly label their individual or group submissions by specifying both their names and the names of the assignments.
Individual Assignments (40%)
Weekly Questions (Due every Tuesday at 23:59, 1-2 meaningful questions based on required readings and weekly topics), and Weekly Notes and Reflective Journals (Due the following Tuesday at 23:59)
Group Assignments (50%)
Group Discussion and Progress
Group Project Presentations:
Midterm Presentation
Group Project and Final Integration Presentation
* Group assignments will be graded based on your role(s) and contributions in each assignment, as well as self & peer evaluation. Non-participation will result in a zero for your group project grade.
* Graduate students are expected to complete their group projects with a full research design and thorough literature review.
* Course and Lateness Policy:
If you have any questions, challenges, or special learning needs, contact Dr. Shie to discuss your situation and a learning plan before any deadlines for this course. At the same time, you have to reach out to NCCU resources and/or other relevant sources to support your situation and be able to request a letter of support.
Students who are unable to attend classes due to illness or other university-approved reasons are required to apply for a leave of absence, providing documentary evidence. Please email both Dr. Shie and the teaching assistant for approval before leaving.
Without an excused absence, no late work will be accepted. From the due date, students with an excused absence have 24 hours to submit missing assignments, unless otherwise arranged with the instructor. If you have any questions or difficulties, contact Dr. Shie as soon as possible before the due dates. Late homework submissions will only be accepted with a university-approved excused absence given to Dr. Shie within 24 hours of the missed due date. If you anticipate you won’t be able to meet the deadline for eligible reasons, you have to get approval from Dr. Shie in advance.

description: 都市發展是一個動態過程,隨著都市發展與變遷,規劃理論亦不斷創新。都市規劃被定義為一個理解經濟、社會、文化和環境目標並且透過各種工具實踐的決策過程;而都市計畫及相關政策就是協助目標達成的工具。

title: 不動產概論 Introduction to Real Estate
description:
本課程介紹不動產基本概念,包括不動產定義、類型、運作,影響不動產價格因素,及相關學術領域與未來可從事相關行業等範疇。
並從不動產投資、生產、交易、使用各階段衍生的問題,探討不動產契約、不動產貸款、不動產稅賦與不動產交易實價等法規與政策,讓學生同時學習不動產的學術及實務領域。
課程亦將安排實地參訪活動,參觀建案、地政事務所等,使學生有實際體驗。
本課程為地政系一年級土地管理組必修課程,課程內容也適合非地政系對於不動產知識有興趣的初學者修習。
objectives:
課程目標:
本課程是地政系一年級學生的入門課程,透過本課程可讓學生對不動產知識有基礎的理論與實務瞭解。課程設計包括課堂講授及實地參訪,各週討論主題也將搭配時事說明,期望透過本課程學習,學生能具備基本知識與分析能力。
學習成效:
希望同學修習本課程之後,能得到以下學習成效:
1.瞭解不動產運作各階段基本知識
2.具備不動產基礎資料閱讀與分析能力
grading:
1.期中考試佔25%
2.上課出席與討論佔20%,同學應出席課堂與參訪活動,以確保良好學習狀況。(不定期點名3次)
3.書面作業佔40%(遲交扣分)
給分標準(分成A+、A、B、C、D等級)
A+:優良(問題回答完整、清晰、有條理,有充分資料支持結論,心得或個人觀點言之有理且豐富)
A:佳(問題回答完整,內容大致正確,有心得或個人觀點)
B:普通(問題回答雖完整,但缺乏結論、心得或個人觀點)
C:待改進(問題回答過於簡略)
D:抄襲
4.課堂分組報告佔15%
給分標準(小組互評)
一、口語表達與台風:(40%)
報告同學台風是否穩健? 報告流程是否順暢? 時間掌握是否妥適?
二、報告內容正確性:(40%)
報告內容與主題連結度?報告內容邏輯嚴謹度?資料引用?實例分析(是否能提出貼切豐富實例,協助聽眾理解)?
三、創意呈現:(20%)
進行小組報告不要僅呈現文字或唸稿,希望多用圖表、短片,報告時甚至可納入短劇、辯論等創意呈現方式。

title: 規劃實務(二) Planning Practice (II)
description: 本課程目的在透過規劃個案之模擬操作,提供學生都市規劃之實際經驗。經由分組操作方式,由同學選定規劃地區,設定規劃主題與目標,進行規劃模擬。課程安排上,將介紹相關之都計法令與規劃理論,使學生能熟悉法令與理論在實務應用上的關係。其次介紹與分析規劃方法及目標導向之規劃流程。輔以個案探討方式,啟發學生規劃觀念與規劃技巧,以培養學生獨立規劃之能力。使學生熟悉計畫方案之研擬及計畫方案之評估與選擇,以及財務計畫之編列。
objectives:
1.具備規劃與分析都市空間議題之能力。
2.具備有效運用大學各項學習資源。
3.具備蒐集及運用資料分析之能力。
4.具備結合規劃策略與土地開發方式之能力。
5.具備觀察都市問題之習慣與能力。
6.具備團隊合作與專題製作能力。
grading:
第一次分組報告10%
第二次分組報告(期中報告)10%
第三次分組報告(期末報告)10%
進度報告10%
期末總結報告30%
課程參與(出席、發問、討論、報告製作)30%
prerequisite: [ 規劃實務(一)(全學年)(修習且及格)]

title: 土地使用管制 Land Use Control
description: 本課程旨在建立土地使用管制之基本理念並說明其應用情形。課程內容為除介紹土地使用管制的基本理論與現行土地使用管制制度(包括土地使用分區管制(zoning)與開發許可制(planning permission)等)外,亦對土地市場在土地使用管制下的運作與問題進行論。主要內容分為四部分,1.介紹土地使用管制之基本理念,以及土地使用分區管制之形成、基本精神、制度內容及制度的延伸應用。並以美國土地使用分區管制為例,說明形成土地使用分區管制制度的財產權爭議、規範及執行。2.說明開發許可制之形成、基本精神及制度內容為主軸,並以英國執行開發許可制為例,介紹制度的演進與改變、以及在執行開發許可時,對土地市場之影響。3.說明臺灣實施土地使用分區管制與非都市土地使用管制之背景、現行制度內容與制度執行情形,同時探討土地使用分區管制之實行對於土地市場之影響。4.介紹未來實施國土計畫法中有關土地土地使用管制的理念及可能的執行方式,以及與現行土地使用管制制度的銜接情形。
objectives: 建立土地使用管制之基本理念、介紹土地使用管制之相關制度(如土地使用分區管制與(zoning)及開發許可制(planning permission),討論台灣地區土地使用管制(都市土地與非都市土地)之內涵。讓同學瞭解土地市場中土地使用管制之角色,並對土地資源配置之利用政策與土地/不動產市場進行分析。
grading:
期中考試 30%
期末分組報告 40%
平時成績(不定期小考、報告、出缺席、上課情形) 30%

title: 大地測量學 Geodetic Surveying
description: 大地測量學(Geodesy)是一門研究地球形狀、大小、重力場及其時空變化的地球科學分支,旨在為測繪、導航、空間定位及地球動力學提供理論與技術基礎。本課程介紹經典與現代大地測量學的核心概念,包括地球參考系、坐標系統、測量技術(如: GPS、衛星測量技術)、重力場模型,以及地殼運動與潮汐等地球動力現象的監測。學生將學習如何應用數學、物理與空間技術解決實際測量問題,並理解大地測量在工程、環境監測與全球定位系統中的應用。課程結合理論講授、案例分析與實務操作,幫助學生掌握大地測量的基本原理與現代技術。
objectives:
課程目標
使學生理解大地測量學的理論基礎,包括地球形狀、重力場與坐標系統的定義與應用。
培養學生應用現代測量技術(如: GNSS、VLBI、InSAR)進行空間定位與地球監測的能力。
提升學生解決實際測量問題的數學與物理分析能力,特別是涉及大範圍的地球形狀、重力場和大地水準面的計算。
促進學生對大地測量在工程、環境科學與地球動力學中應用的認識。
培養團隊合作與工程倫理意識,確保測量數據的精確性與可靠性。
學習成效(完成本課程後,學生應能夠):
描述地球參考系與坐標系統的類型及其在測量中的應用。
執行基本的測量數據處理與誤差分析,包括坐標轉換與重力場計算。
使用現代大地測量技術進行數據收集與分析。
解釋地殼運動、潮汐與極地運動等地質現象的測量方法與意義。
撰寫清晰的測量報告,並在團隊合作中展現專業素養與倫理責任。

title: 地圖學 Cartography
description:
Cartography is the technique, science, and art of transforming data into maps. These maps help us see and understand complex spatial patterns and relationships in a visual way.
Maps are everywhere --- they are part of our daily lives, often used without us even noticing. While traditional paper maps are still important, they have largely been replaced or supplemented by digital maps. However, the core idea of turning data into useful visual information remains the same. Thanks to the digital revolution, cartography has undergone major changes and successfully adapted to modern tools and technologies.
This course introduces students to Digital Cartography by focusing on how maps are made --- from choosing and organizing data, to filtering and interpreting it, to designing clear, effective maps. Students will explore these steps while creating their own maps using powerful digital tools.
Because of its ability to store, manage, analyze and visualize spatial data, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) plays a central role in this process. Throughout the course, students will use GIS to support their cartographic work and bring their map ideas to life.
In addition to traditional cartographic concepts, the course introduces students to modern technologies, including Machine Learning (ML), that are beginning to influence how maps are made, interpreted, and automated. Students will gain foundational insights into how ML techniques can be used to classify spatial data, detect patterns, or assist in map generalization and feature extraction, helping them understand the growing role of intelligent systems in the future of cartography.
objectives:
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the theoretical and practical foundations of cartography and map design in the digital age. It emphasizes how spatial data is transformed into effective visual communication through maps. Students will gain hands-on experience using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and be introduced to state-of-the-art technologies, such as Machine Learning tools for mapping, hat are reshaping the way spatial data is analyzed and visualized.
Map creation will focus on a variety of use cases, including physical maps, charts and plans, complex thematic maps incorporating relevant topics such as hazard mapping and Sustainable Development Goals (in particular SDG 11 and 15), and topological maps (network maps)
By the end of this course, students will be able to:
Understand and apply core cartographic concepts, including scale, projection, generalization, and symbolization.
Identify, evaluate, and select appropriate spatial data for specific mapping purposes.
Design effective map concepts that reflect the intended message and audience.
Transform raw data into higher-level, interpretable information through filtering, classification, and visual hierarchy.
Produce digital maps using standard cartographic techniques and GIS tools that adhere to principles of effective visual communication.
Use international cartographic terminology to describe and critique their map products.
Gain foundational awareness of how AI and machine learning are used in cartography, e.g., in automating feature recognition, supporting data generalization, or enhancing spatial pattern detection.
Critically assess the strengths and limitations of AI-supported mapping workflows.
grading:
This course is developed around map projects. Additional homework assignments and bonus exercises will help to consolidate the obtained knowledge.
The midterm examination will be a portfolio of online questions and/or a project covering the theoretical foundations of cartography.
The final exam will be a mapping project. In order to complete the final project suceesfully, students will set up a mapping project, produce a digital map and describe their mapping concept and realization.
weeklyText:
Classes are 3 hours and take place in the GIS lab (270610). Due to the highly practical nature of this course, we will follow a hybrid approach with mixed theory and practice.
This course and all handout/upload material are provided in English, therefore a basic command of the English language will be required. Also, a basic understanding of spatial data and a feeling for spatial information and relationships are of advantage. For the technical aspects of this course, a basic knowledge of trigonometry and trigonometric identities, and a basic understanding of coordinate systems and transformations will be beneficial.
WEEK 1 (09/10). Introduction to Digital Cartography and Basics of GIS
CONTENTS. This week introduces the scope and purpose of digital cartography and distinguishes it from traditional mapmaking. You will become familiar with what a map represents in digital systems, the concept of spatial data, and the role of GIS software. The objective is to provide a conceptual foundation while setting up the digital environment for mapping.
READINGS. Course script and selected sections in Robinson et al. (1995), Field (2018), Tyner (2010), and other sources.
ACTIVITIES. You attend an introductory lecture on the nature and roles of digital maps, followed by a hands-on lab exercise within a GIS environment with basic layer operations and an initial map design.
HOMEWORK. Readings and review.
WEEK 2 (09/17). Coordinate Systems, Projections and Map Scale
CONTENTS. This session focuses on geographic and projected coordinate systems, projection types, and their effects on spatial accuracy. You will learn how to choose and apply map projections and understand the importance of scale in spatial representation and interpretation.
READINGS. Course script and selected sections in Robinson et al. (1995), Snyder (1987), Field (2018), Tyner (2010), and other sources.
ACTIVITIES. The lecture introduces map projections, scale concepts, and distortion principles. In the lab, you will reproject layers, observe differences between map projections and reference systems, and explore scale impacts on geography.
HOMEWORK: Start of Map Project 1: Population Density Thematic Map
WEEK 3 (09/24). Symbolization, Colour, and Visual Hierarchy
CONTENTS. This week covers visual variables such as colour, shape, size, and texture, along with symbol classification methods (e.g., quantile, natural breaks). Emphasis is placed on creating visual hierarchy and meaningful symbolization for thematic mapping.
READINGS. Course script and selected sections in Robinson et al. (1995), Bertin (2011), Field (2018), Tyner (2010), and other sources.
ACTIVITIES. After a theoretical overview of symbol design and classification techniques, you will practice applying symbology in GIS, experimenting with different classification schemes and colour palettes to visualise population data.
HOMEWORK. Continue Map Project 1
WEEK 4 (10/01). Labels, Legends, and Map Composition
CONTENTS. Students explore cartographic composition, focusing on text labelling, map elements (legend, north arrow, scale), and visual balance. The goal is to produce clear, readable layouts that communicate spatial information effectively.
READINGS. Course script and selected sections in Robinson et al. (1995), Field (2018), Tyner (2010), and other sources.
ACTIVITIES. The lecture discusses typefaces, label placement rules, and the function of cartographic elements. The lab is devoted to refining the thematic map layout, adding labels for cities, and finalising composition.
HOMEWORK. Finalise Map Project 1
WEEK 5 (10/08). Terrain Representation and Land Cover Data
CONTENTS. This week introduces elevation models and terrain visualisation techniques, including hillshading and contouring for physiographic and topographic maps. Students will also begin working with land cover raster datasets to understand physiographic mapping.
READINGS. Course script and selected sections in Robinson et al. (1995), Field (2018), Tyner (2010), and other sources.
ACTIVITIES. The lecture covers elevation representation, contour logic, and land cover classification. The lab includes generating contours from Digital Elevation Models, styling hillshading, and importing land cover data.
HOMEWORK. Start of Map Project 2: Physiographic Map
WEEK 6 (10/15). Generalisation and Feature Extraction with Machine Learning
CONTENTS. This session explores generalisation techniques such as simplification and smoothing, and introduces basic machine learning for land cover classification. The aim is to automate the extraction of urban, water, and vegetation features.
READINGS. Course script and selected sections in Robinson et al. (1995), Field (2018), Tyner (2010), and other sources.
ACTIVITIES. Students will experience vector generalisation methods, then use supervised classification to extract land cover types for a defined area. These features are converted into clean vector layers for further map use.
HOMEWORK. Continue Map Project 2
WEEK 7 (10/22). Map Refinement and Styling for Terrain Visualisation
CONTENTS. This week focuses on blending multiple terrain visualisation techniques and achieving expressive cartographic styles. Students will consolidate topographic features with elevation cues and meaningful symbology.
READINGS. Course script and selected sections in Robinson et al. (1995), Field (2018), Tyner (2010), and other sources.
ACTIVITIES. Students finalise their physiographic map by integrating shaded relief, generalisation results, and proper labelling. Emphasis is placed on stylistic coherence and effective visual communication.
HOMEWORK. Finalise Map Project 2
WEEK 8 (10/29). Midterm Exam Week
---
WEEK 9 (11/05). Topology and Network Structures in Cartography
CONTENTS. Students are introduced to topological relationships and their use in transportation networks. The focus is on nodes, edges, and how spatial topology differs from visual or geographic fidelity.
READINGS. Course script and other sources.
ACTIVITIES. The lecture explains network logic, topological rules, and abstraction in metro maps. In the lab, students digitise station points and rail lines, ensuring correct topological structure.
HOMEWORK. Start of Map Project 3: Metro Network Topological Map
WEEK 10 (11/12). Spatial Adjustment and Network Geometry Control
CONTENTS. This session develops practical skills in aligning, snapping, and editing geometries while maintaining topological relationships. Students learn to optimise layout for readability without violating topology.
READINGS. Course script and selected sections in Robinson et al. (1995), Field (2018), Tyner (2010), and other sources.
ACTIVITIES. After a lecture on geometric control, students modify and adjust metro networks, snapping nodes and refining layout while preserving logical connections between stations.
HOMEWORK. Continue Map Project 3.
WEEK 11 (11/19). Finishing the Network Map
CONTENTS. This week emphasises map finalisation and symbol simplification for abstract networks. The goal is to create a clean metro map with readable labels, coherent linework, and a functional layout.
READINGS. Course script and other sources.
ACTIVITIES. Students finish the metro map using abstraction techniques inspired by transit design standards. They apply symbology, finalise label placement, and prepare the map for submission.
HOMEWORK. Finalise Map Project 3
WEEK 12 (11/26). Digitizing and Working with Scanned Maps
CONTENTS. Students learn to georeference scanned historical maps and digitise vector features. Focus is on parcels and alignment to control points while maintaining topological consistency.
READINGS. Course script and selected sections in Robinson et al. (1995), Field (2018), Tyner (2010), and other sources.
ACTIVITIES. The lecture covers georeferencing and digitising best practices. In the lab, students begin working with a historic parcel map, aligning it to base data and starting parcel digitisation.
HOMEWORK. Start of Map Project 4: Parcel Plan
WEEK 13 (12/03). Survey Constraints and Parcel Editing
CONTENTS. This session involves applying geometric constraints to parcel boundaries and editing nodes and edges while preserving clean topology. Students will learn to encode survey information and manage parcel attributes.
READINGS. Course script and selected sections in Robinson et al. (1995), Field (2018), Tyner (2010), and other sources.
ACTIVITIES. Students complete parcel digitisation, manage shared edges, and adjust geometries to match survey-derived measurements. The lab includes layout preparation and styling for cadastral clarity.
HOMEWORK. Finalise Map Project 4.
WEEK 14 (12/10). Capstone Project Launch: Complex Thematic Map
CONTENTS. The capstone project introduces complex thematic mapping with multivariate symbology and multiple thematic layers combined with topographic basemaps. Students will work with earthquake point data, scale and colour symbols, and derive patterns from hotspot surfaces.
READINGS. Course script and selected sections in Robinson et al. (1995), Field (2018), Tyner (2010), and other sources.
ACTIVITIES. After visiting multivariate and derived mapping, students begin compiling earthquake data from online catalogs. They explore magnitude-depth visualisation and generate kernel density maps to identify seismic clusters.
HOMEWORK. Start of Capstone Map Project: Complex-Thematic Map
WEEK 15 (12/17). Advanced Layouts and Capstone Integration
CONTENTS. This session supports the final integration of thematic layers, tectonic context, and cartographic refinement. Emphasis is placed on clarity, storytelling, and thematic coherence.
READINGS. Course script and selected sections in Robinson et al. (1995), Field (2018), Tyner (2010), and other sources.
ACTIVITIES. Students finalise their capstone maps by adding tectonic plate boundaries, labels, legends, and compositional elements. The focus is on exporting a polished product for submission.
HOMEWORK. Continuation of Capstone Map Project: Complex-Thematic Map
WEEK 16 (12/24). Final Exam Week

title: 民法(一) Civil Law (I)
description:
民法是地政領域相當重要的法學基礎科目,雖然是處理人民與人民間的法律關係,但因為民法為萬法之母,因此,無論是不動產交易、土地開發,甚至土地行政都會與民法的基礎觀念有密切的關聯性。民法的內容主要包括財產法及家族法,前者可以說是處理一般市民的法律行為,包括債編及物權編;後者則處理家族之間的身分關係及財產關係,包括親屬編及繼承編。這些篇章的基本運作邏輯及規範則另外規範於總則編,包括權利主體、權利客體及法律行為等概念,都是許多法律關係會運用到的觀念,可以認為是所有民事法律關係運作的基礎。
本學期主要著重在民法總則編及債編總論債之效力前基本概念的介紹,由於涉及基本概念的建構,課程主要由教師講授,透過案例的方式協助同學理解,並輔以討論確保同學對於基本概念的掌握度。由於課程時間有限,不可能逐一講解各個條文,因此,主要針對重要的法律概念及條文規範做討論,並讓同學可以了解到各個法律規範的立法目的、立法理由,並希望同學們可以透過學習,有能力面對具體個別的案件時,找出正確的條文,並有基本的法律解釋能力。
objectives:
本課程主要的目的在於透過學習,讓同學有以下的學習成效:
1.具備深度閱讀的能力:希望同學透過課堂的學習及對於課堂資料的研讀,對於民法的基本理念及立法意旨有所了解,並有能力閱讀並正確理解法院判決,提升基礎學養的厚度。
2.具備有效運用大學各項學習資源:本校有諸多圖書及資料庫的資源,希望同學有能力查找資訊,運用工作來解決問題。
3.養成自主與終身學習的態度與策略:讓同學了解到法律規範及法律解釋往往需與時俱進,因此,需要隨時掌握社會脈動,對民法的相關發展有所掌握。
grading:
本課程的學習成效評量工具及評分標準如下:
1.主要透過學期考試來檢驗,針對課程簡介及前述進度的授課內容。此一部分占學期總成績的40%。命題方式為選擇題等非申論式題型占(著重在記憶15%、理解15%及應用20%)75%(25題),申論題及實例題(主要著重在對法規範的理解10%及應用15%)占25%。
2.課程的參與度,此部分共占總成績的30%。包括課程現場專注程度,透過教師印象評量,占30%、出席率占50%、課堂或課後與教師針對授課內容的互動占20%,共占總成績的30%。
3.本課程也會鼓勵同學針對特定議題進行分組討論,占總成績的30%,此部分重視同學對於法規範的理解及獨立思考的能力,各占50%。評分衡量的因素包括執行方案之規劃、文獻佐證 及結果佐證。

title: 土地登記 Land Registration
description: 本課程藉由課堂講授與討論方式,使瞭解我國不動產登記制度、各種登記內涵與法規範現狀。課程內容主要包括:1. 主要不動產登記制度;2.. 土地登記之事項、程序及各類型登記之內涵;3.歷來與不動產登記相關之圖資及簿冊。
objectives: 期履修者瞭解我國不動產登記制度之抽象原理原則、不動產登記相關之法律與法規命令等具體規定(如民法總則物權、土地法、土地登記規則暨地籍測量實施規則等),及地政實務上各種不動產登記簿與地籍圖冊(如土地與建物登記簿謄本、建物平面圖、地籍圖等),使掌握不動產登記法之基礎,進而具備辦理不動產相關登記暨對其審查之能力。

title: 環境數值模擬與災害潛勢分析 Environmental Numerical Modeling and Hazard Potential Assessment
description: 極端降雨與複合型災害日益頻繁的背景下,水災、坡地崩塌與土砂運移等環境現象已成為國土環境風險的重要來源。本課程以「環境數值模擬」為核心,帶領土地資訊與測量組學生建立從物理機制到空間化成果的完整能力鏈:理解水文與土砂運移等基本過程、掌握模型所需之輸入資料(如 DEM、土地覆蓋、土壤/地質、降雨歷線等)與前處理方法、學習模型參數與邊界條件設定,並透過校驗、敏感度分析與不確定性表達,判讀模擬結果的可信度與適用範圍。課程將以淹水範圍、水深/流速、沖刷與堆積熱區、土石流可能路徑與影響範圍等為主要輸出,進一步轉換為可在 GIS 中整合之災害潛勢圖資與指標,並示範其在都市與國土相關工作中的支援角色,例如:潛在熱區辨識、基礎設施與聚落暴露度盤點、不同情境下風險差異比較,以及跨領域溝通所需的技術性說明。整體目標在於培養學生具備「理解模型—產出圖資—解讀限制」的專業素養,使其能以一致且可檢核的量化方法支撐環境風險之空間分析與應用。
objectives:
本課程將介紹都會與山區天災類型與風險評估、數值地形於災害判釋原則與防災韌性與國土調適策略。課程將學習以遙測圖資及GIS工具產製災害潛勢圖之基本原則、圖資來源與分析方法等,支援都市與國土防災相關應用之技術溝通:能以技術語言清楚說明潛勢成果、資料需求與限制,並示範與土地利用、建物、基礎設施等資料的疊合與暴露度盤點方法。
課程中亦將教授災害數值模擬核心概念,包含理解環境數值模擬之基本概念、控制方程與主要假設,說明模型適用尺度與限制條件。同時學習掌握輸入資料與前處理流程,具備整備 DEM圖資分析、土地使用、降雨歷線、土壤/地質等關鍵資料之能力,理解資料品質對模擬結果的影響。完成基本建模與情境設定建立可重複之模擬流程,並進行多情境(現況/極端/假設情境)比較。透過判讀結果可信度:能執行校驗與敏感度分析,辨識誤差來源,並以合理方式呈現不確定性與結果解讀界線。最終產製不同災害類型之潛勢圖資與指標:將模擬輸出轉換為 GIS 可用的潛勢圖層與空間指標(如土砂災害範圍、沖刷堆積熱區、影響熱區等),建構國土防災與空間分析基礎情資之能力。
grading:
每周實作作業與練習:20%(DEM處理、資料整備、模擬操作、GIS圖資產製等分項作業)。
期中報告(個人書面):30%(RAMMS數值模擬與分析資料報告)
期末專題報告(分組書面與發表):50%(災害議題選定與災害潛勢圖資評估成果)

title: 不動產空間分析 Applied Spatial Analysis for Real Estate
description: 不動產空間分析是一門問題導向式的實作綜整課程。課程以不動產市場、都市發展、區位條件、公共設施、環境風險與開發決策等實際議題為核心,透過雙週一單元的設計,結合理論講授、空間資料操作、學生討論與成果review,引導學生將不動產專業知識轉化為可操作的空間分析能力。課程採多位教師協作模式,由不同教師提供議題與理論框架,以及對應之GIS操作與成果整合,使學生能在連續實作中,完成具問題意識的不動產空間分析成果。
objectives:
課程目標:本課程以不動產實務問題為核心,培養學生運用空間資料與GIS方法分析不動產區位、市場、環境與開發議題的能力。課程透過理論講授、操作實作、學生討論與成果回饋,引導學生完成具問題意識與應用價值的不動產空間分析成果。
學習成效:
1. 將不動產議題轉化為可分析的空間問題。
2. 整理並整合不動產相關空間資料。
3. 操作GIS工具完成基本空間分析。
4. 解讀空間分析結果,說明其意涵。
5. 以地圖、圖表與簡報呈現分析成果。
6. 整合理論、資料與方法,完成實作型專題。
grading: 每次報告佔12.5%。

title: 空間資料應用於環境變遷偵測 Spatial Data for Environmental Change Detection
description: This course introduces senior undergraduate students to the advanced application of modern geospatial technologies for monitoring and analyzing environmental change. Moving beyond basic GIS, the course emphasizes the use of geospatial artificial intelligence (Geo-AI) as the core methodology for integrating multi-source, high-precision spatial data from various Earth systems. This integrated approach allows students to accurately assess the dynamic impacts of environmental change on land resources.
objectives:
The primary objective of this course is to train students to effectively apply modern geospatial technologies and Geo-AI methodologies to analyze environmental change. This includes integrating multi-source spatial data—such as satellite imagery, GPS/GNSS, hydrological, and seismic information—to monitor, analyze, and assess the dynamic impacts of environmental change on land resources and national spatial planning. The ultimate goal is to generate actionable intelligence that supports disaster early warning and sustainable development in the domain of land administration. Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to demonstrate the following competencies:
Data Integration and Technical Proficiency (Interdisciplinary Integration)
Assess the dynamic impacts of environmental phenomena (Multidimensional Decision Support)

title: 毀滅與新生—二次大戰後德國都市、鄉村及其建築的重構 Destruction and Reborn – the New Developments of German Urbanplan and Architecture after WWII
description:
本課程為短期國外移地教學,預計於115年8月中下旬辦理。
鑒於德國是第二次世界大戰期間被摧毀最嚴重地區,且歷經冷戰時期之分裂,在二戰後重建迄於統一後,表現出極度多元的都市規劃與建築設計思維,往往在極小空間範圍中,高度集中典範等級之規劃與設計案例。固本次教學行程規劃,精選由都市到鄉村、由古蹟維護到新建綠建築的典範及案例,分別位於柏林、呂布腦、德勒斯登、林茲、雷根斯堡與加米許-帕登基爾許的都市規劃與建築案例。藉此希望同學可以由其中了解現代都市、鄉村規劃與建築間整體思考的重要性與創意。
objectives:
1. 參訪、觀察樣區及個案在空間規劃與建築上的特殊考量之處,並練習結合地圖做成觀察紀錄。思考城鎮規劃如何與建築管理互相結合。
2. 拜訪相關機關,了解德國、奧地利在制度面向與台灣不同之處。思考這導致台灣與德奧在執行土地使用管制與建築管理時,所形成的差異。
3. 學習辨識歐洲不同時期建築風格及其時代背景,並觀察如何在發展現代都市機能之同時,維護大量文物古蹟以及自古流傳的街道布局。
4. 觀察農村生活模式與經濟產業間的關聯,以及歐盟主導下歐洲山村的治理邏輯。反思在台灣如何處理山村所面臨各種課題。
grading:
教師於出國前開列應觀察、學習之重點,回國後由參與同學針對所列出應觀察、學習重點繳交學習報告。
1. 樣區地圖記錄
2. 觀察分析

title: 住宅研究與資料科學 Data Science for Housing Research
description: 本課程為學士班高年級與碩士班合開課程,將從住宅供、需、價、量不同層面,探討現今住宅問題與相關研究,並特別著重在當前社會住宅政策與過去較少關注的租賃市場,課程亦將安排實地參訪社會住宅或老人住宅。且因應循證研究需求,將在課程中帶領同學運用程式語言及統計分析工具,建立資料分析思維與初階分析能力。
objectives:
希望同學修習之後,能達到以下學習成效:
能學會基本的統計分析工具及資料庫查詢語言,撰寫以「描述統計」為基礎之住宅政策分析報告,包含背景說明、重要發現、重要發現彙整等。
使學生對住宅相關研究有初階理解,能辨識問題,運用循證政策分析,解讀資料數據意涵。
grading:
1.出席及課堂討論 30%
同學應出席課堂與參訪活動,以確保良好學習狀況。(不定期點名3次)
2.書面作業 20%
給分標準(分成A+、A、B、C、D等級)
A+:優良(問題回答完整、清晰、有條理,有充分資料支持結論,心得或個人觀點言之有理且豐富)
A:佳(問題回答完整,內容大致正確,有心得或個人觀點)
B:普通(問題回答雖完整,但缺乏結論、心得或個人觀點)
C:待改進(問題回答過於簡略)
D:抄襲
3.分組報告 50%
一、口語表達與台風:(40%)
報告同學台風是否穩健? 報告流程是否順暢? 時間掌握是否妥適?
二、報告內容正確性:(40%)
報告內容與主題連結度?報告內容邏輯嚴謹度?資料引用?實例分析(是否能提出貼切豐富實例,協助聽眾理解)?
三、創意呈現:(20%)
進行小組報告不要僅呈現文字或唸稿,希望多用圖表、短片,報告時甚至可納入短劇、辯論等創意呈現方式。

title: 國土計畫概論 Introduction to Spatial Planning
description: 國土計畫法自105年1月6日公布後,全新的國土管理法制將取代實施半世紀之久的區域計畫法制,對於土地使用及空間發展等各層面影響甚鉅。其中,不但涉及空間管理法制新舊制轉換之差異,亦納入許多新的規劃概念與工具,如氣候變遷、國際公約、都會區域計畫、特定區域計畫、鄉村地區整體規劃等,所涉及的空間規劃與土地管理法制龐雜,並與其他相關法規及制度密切相關。因此,本課程將全面性的講授國土計畫所涉及的面向與觀念,使同學對國土計畫之理論、法制與實務有基礎性的理解。
objectives:
1.對國土計畫法制有基礎性之認知。
2.瞭解國土空間規劃體系與管制架構。
3.瞭解國土計畫涉及的各專業領域知識。
4.具備觀察國土規劃與管制議題之習慣與能力。
5.具備有效運用國土計畫知識之能力。
6.具備蒐集國土規劃與管制相關資料之興趣與能力。
grading:
本課程評分項目如下
1.出席狀況及課程參與(30%)
2.授課教師之作業(70%)
3.本課程沒有期中、期末考試

title: 都市更新與容積代金估價實務 Valuation Practice for Urban Renewal and Bulk TDR
description:
本課程聚焦不動產估價產業兩項核心且高度專業的業務--都市更新權利變換估價,以及容積移轉與容積代金估價。兩者皆配合都市計畫運作,專業性與複雜性兼具;課程分為兩大部分,分別建立其法令框架、估價技術與實務操作能力。
一、都市更新權利變換估價(第1–9週)
依都市更新條例第五章及都市更新權利變換實施辦法,權利人以更新前之土地、合法建物及他項權利參與更新,於更新後按「更新前權利價值比率」分配更新後之土地、建築物或權利金。課程探討權利變換估價之主要對象——更新前權利價值(土地權利價值與比例、合法建物殘值、租金補償、舊違章戶處理)、更新後總權利價值,以及共同負擔(公共設施用地、工程費用、權利變換費用、貸款利息、稅捐、管理費及容積獎勵/移轉所支付費用等)之計算與折價抵付,並說明評價基準日(權利變換計畫報核前六個月)與權益分配機制。法令與技術依據包括不動產估價技術規則第124至128條、各縣市估價報告書範本及審查注意事項,以及估價師全聯會第六號公報(都市更新權利變換不動產估價報告書範本)。
二、容積移轉與容積代金估價(第10–16週)
本部分沿「從容積移轉(TDR)到容積代金、再到跨基地容積調配」的制度演進主軸,引導同學理解發展權如何成為可定價、可治理的資產。先以國際視野(空中權 Air Rights、TDR 與開發利益回饋、紐約中央車站)切入,續談台灣 TDR 兩階段演進(古蹟與大稻埕歷史街區保存,到公共設施保留地取得)與送出基地五大類型;再進入容積代金之核心估價邏輯——以「容移前/容移後」雙情境比較、土地開發分析法為主、比較法與收益法為輔,並佐以實務案例(如士林科技園區企業總部之容積代金估價)說明定價流程。法令依據包括都市計畫容積移轉實施辦法、各縣市容積移轉自治法規與代金估價報告書範本,估價技術另參酌估價師公會所發布之相關公報以及通用原則。
課程結合估價師全聯會技術公報、各縣市政府估價報告書範本與多個個案實例,並安排權利變換估價說明會與容積代金說明簡報之模擬演練;修課同學最後以分組個案報告展現學習成果。
objectives:
課程目標:
將估價理論與方法運用於不同的土地開發或都市計畫執行業務上,讓同學了解權利變換估價及容積代金估價的核心關注與實務運用的細節。
學習成效:
具備都市更新權利變換之基本概念與法令框架。
具備運用估價技術於權利變換權益分配(更新前後價值、共同負擔)之能力。
具備容積移轉制度與發展權貨幣化(容積代金)之基本概念。
具備以雙情境比較及土地開發分析法評估容積代金之技術。
具備向報告書使用人(主管機關、實施者與權利人)清楚說明估價結論之溝通能力。

title: 空間決策 Spatial Decision Making
description:
TL;DR. Learn how to make smarter, evidence‐based decisions about real‐world spatial problems.
We start with core decision‐making tools, then dive into GIS, spatial analysis, and machine learning to tackle challenges like planning infrastructure, mapping hazards, and shaping land‐use policy. By the end, we will be able to design, run, and evaluate powerful spatial decision workflows from the ground up.
Long Version.
How can we make better decisions about places, spaces, and the world around us?
This course explores the tools and approaches that help answer that question.
It begins with the basics of decision-making — breaking down complex choices into manageable steps and comparing options in a structured way. Core methods such as multi‐criteria analysis, weighting techniques, and simple statistical models provide a foundation for understanding robust decision processes.
During the second half of the semester, the focus then shifts to spatial problems — those that involve geography and location. Using Geographic Information Systems (GIS), the class works through real-world challenges including site selection, infrastructure planning, hazard zone mapping, and land-use policy evaluation. Hands-on labs demonstrate how Spatial Decision Support Systems (SDSS) are designed, adapted, and assessed for different decision contexts.
The course introduces machine learning approaches — including decision trees, logistic regression, and clustering — to identify patterns in decision-making. Spatial machine learning models and feature ranking strategies add a leading‐edge complement to traditional analysis.
By the end of the semester, we will have the skills to:
Apply GIS and integrated tools to address spatial decision problems,
Design and implement complete decision‐making workflows,
Evaluate the robustness and reliability of decision processes.
Relevant to fields such as urban planning, environmental analysis, disaster management, and policy design, the course equips students with a practical toolkit for evidence‐based spatial decision making.
objectives:
Course Goals
This course aims to:
Explore key theories, methods, and tools for spatial decision making.
Examine case studies from the literature to highlight successful applications and common challenges.
Provide hands‐on experience in the design, implementation, and evaluation of spatial decision workflows.
Integrate Geographic Information Systems (GIS), statistical methods, and machine learning techniques to support evidence‐based decisions.
Learning Outcomes
By the end of the course, we will be able to:
Identify and critically assess existing spatial decision-making projects from academic and applied contexts.
Select and adapt appropriate approaches for a given decision problem.
Collect, prepare, and model spatial and non‐spatial data for analysis.
Design and implement a complete spatial decision workflow, from problem definition to outcome evaluation.
Apply GIS software and integrated modelling tools to create a targeted decision-making system from scratch.
Incorporate statistical and machine learning methods to analyse patterns and improve decision outcomes.
Evaluate the robustness and reliability of conclusions based on multiple criteria, variables, and uncertainty considerations.
grading:
This course has a midterm and a final exam.
Homework assignments and bonus exercises will help to consolidate the obtained knowledge.
The midterm examination will be a portfolio of online questions and/or a project covering the theoretical foundations.
The final exam will be a project. In order to complete the final project successfully, students will set up a spatial decision-making project, and produce a workflow with evaluation criteria.

title: 土地重劃 Land Consolidation
description:
本課程介紹台灣土地重劃的相關制度內容,以市地重劃為主、輔以農地重劃及農村社區土地重劃之介紹。
透過土地整合及重劃之理念與目的,對於市地重劃、農地重劃及農村社區土地重劃的目的、內容及實施方式進行講解;針對台灣的三種重劃制度進行說明及於現行社會的應用與問題。討論市地重劃於都市發展的角色及影響,亦探討台灣現行農地利用與農地重劃之關係,以及農村與農村社區土地重劃之間的關聯性。
objectives:
本課程主要學習土地重劃制度的基本理念,瞭解土地重劃制度之目的、內容、執行與檢討。
探討其他國家實施土地重劃之經驗,與台灣實施土地重劃互相比較與學習,分析動態社會變遷下土地重劃之制度變遷、制度內涵之改變及對土地市場與土地利用之影響。讓同學具備土地重劃的基本制度與運作。

description: 本課程介紹物件導向程式設計之基本概念,透過應用實例讓學生了解如何運用Python設計程式解決實務的問題。本課程將著重於物件導向程式設計在空間資訊領域之應用,修課者應已經具有Python程式設計的基礎。
objectives:
完成本課程所有教材內容後,學生能夠達成以下學習成效:
能了解Python之語法結構,撰寫完整的程式,有除錯的能力。
具備邏輯思考能力,可以分析問題的解決方法,透過程式以解決問題。

能使用Python語言撰寫物件導向程式 。

具備搜尋網路上軟體資源的能力。
養成自主與終身學習的態度。
具有閱讀英文教材的能力。
grading: 期中報告:30%;期末報告:40%;平時成績:30%(含作業、上課出席及參與等)。

title: 數值製圖 Digital Mapping
description:
地圖是地理學的語言,其研究內容涵蓋地理資料的收集、處理、分析、與展示。本課程擬就地圖學的各個子題進行廣泛的介紹。使學生具有
1.瞭解地圖學的基本理論與概念。
2.學習地圖的判讀和分析技能。
3.熟悉地圖繪製的理論與技術、及基本繪圖的技術。
ˋ4.利用地圖進行地理或空間分佈相關研究之基本能力。
作為學生選修遙感探測、電腦地圖學及地理資訊系統等相關課程之基礎基礎。
objectives:
修畢本課程後,可了解數值攝影測量之原理,並利用程式撰寫相關基礎數值影像處理之方法以及各階段如單像後交會、空間前交會、相對方位、絕對定位、DSM產製與正射影像產製之原理。
修畢本課程後,可達成之核心能力為:
1.具備測量及空間資訊基礎理論之能力
2.具備程式設計與各種測量計算之能力
3.具備土地空間資訊資料蒐集及分析之能力
4.具備應用3S(GIS、GPS、RS)技術進行土地之管理、分析與決策之能力
5.具備規劃與執行測量專案之能力
6.具備領導測量專業團隊之能力

title: 都市設計 Urban Design
description:
This course mainly teaches the background knowledge and characteristics of "urban design", the legal rank of urban design, the role of urban designers, urban space patterns in different periods, the influence of urban land on urban design, urban design theory, and urban design tools and management, overview of urban renewal, urban design review system, urban design cases and future trends of urban design (sustainable city).
本課程主要講授「都市設計」的背景知識與特質、都市設計的法律位階、都市設計師的角色、各時期的都市空間型態、都市土地對於都市設計的影響、都市設計理論、都市設計的工具與管理、都市更新概述、都市設計審議制度、都市設計案例及都市設計的未來趨勢(永續都市)。
objectives:
This course is expected to achieve the following objectives:
1. To help students understand the relationship between urban planning and urban design.
2. To help students acquire the skills and theories of urban design.
本課程預期將可以達到以下目標:
1.使學生瞭解都市計劃與都市設計的相互關係。
2.使學生習得都市設計的技巧與理論。
grading:
Individual assignments (2-4 times). 20%
Midterm exam. 20%
Special Report (twice). 30%
Attendance, questions, class Performance. 30%

title: 海洋測量 Hydrography
description: 本課程探討海洋水文、定位、潮汐及測深等原理,並實際進行海洋測深作業及資料處理。
objectives:
本課程目標主要著眼於海洋環境、水文、潮汐、定位及測深等原理及各式海測儀器簡介,輔以實際儀器操作與外業實習,使理論與實務配合。期望學生所獲得之學習成效:
1.具備各種海洋測量相關基礎理論之能力

title: 建築學概論 Introduction to Architecture
description: 「建築學概論」是一門將建築學相關的學術理論,經由淺顯易懂的方式,深入淺出的介紹。一位土地政策的制訂者與土地使用的管理者,在進行國土規劃與都市計畫時,若能適度的考量建築尺度的思維,其將來所創造的生活環境將得以兼顧經濟與美學的要求。
objectives:
1. 讓修課學生了解建築計畫之內涵與目的。
2. 藉由建築計畫案例討論,瞭解建築設計與景觀計畫之介面與整合方法。
3. 學習建築計畫過程的邏輯,建構景觀設計計畫的步驟與思維方式。
grading:
1.期中報告(35%):第一次設計作業總成果呈現。(包含過程中之5次作業)
2.期中考試(20%+extra10%):上課時除教師於課堂講解外,透過期中考試以瞭解同學對於課程的瞭解。
3.期末報告(35%):第二次設計作業總成果呈現。(包含過程中之5次作業)
4.出席率與特殊表現(10%):包含平時上課之出席率、問題答詢、作業表現。

title: 規劃實務(二)實習 Planning Practice (II) (lab)
description: 本課程目的在透過規劃個案之模擬操作,提供學生國土規劃之實際經驗。經由分組操作方式,由同學選定規劃地區,設定規劃主題與目標,進行規劃模擬。課程安排上,將介紹相關之都計法令與規劃理論,使學生能熟悉法令與理論在實務應用上的關係。其次介紹與分析規劃方法及目標導向之規劃流程。輔以個案探討方式,啟發學生規劃觀念與規劃技巧,以培養學生獨立規劃之能力。使學生熟悉計畫方案之研擬及計畫方案之評估與選擇,以及財務計畫之編列。

4.具備結合規劃策略與土地開發方式之能力。

title: 計量經濟學(一) Econometrics (I)
description:
This is the first of a two-semester sequence of introductory courses in econometrics, with a primary focus on linear regression analysis with cross-sectional data. The purpose of this course is to equip students with the knowledge and practical methods for analyzing economic data, testing economic hypotheses, and measuring empirical relationships between economic variables. We will closely follow Chapters 1-8 of Wooldridge's Introductory Econometrics. We will introduce instrumental variables and two-stage least squares (Chapter 15) if time permits. We will use R as the statistical software for this course.
Prerequisites: Two semesters of Calculus and two semesters of Statistics.
Simple college-level algebra such as equations involving Sigma notation should not present any difficulty for you.
You are expected to be familiar with most of the material in Appendices A–C of Wooldridge's text, though a brief review will be provided. In particular, a clear understanding of sampling distributions, statistical inference, and hypothesis testing is essential.
While prior knowledge of linear algebra is not required, we plan to work with basic matrix algebra (Appendix D of Wooldridge's text) in our treatment of multiple regression analysis.
grading:
Class attendance and participation (10%)
Problem sets (20%):
The problem sets will include both problem solving and computer tasks.
You are encouraged to form a study group with your classmates, but you must write up your own answers. Problem sets with highly similar answers will not be accepted.
No late problem sets will be accepted for any reason.
Two mid-term exams (15% for the first exam and 25% for the second).
Final exam (30%).
All exams will be in-class and closed-book.

title: 國際貿易 International Trade
description: 在社會科學的領域中,如果說有什麼學問應該以台灣作為研究典範的,無疑是國際貿易了。台灣自與西方文明世界接觸的四百年來,都是以貿易為立足點,因此台灣經濟充分展現國際分工的特色,發揮專業生產的利益。無論是狩獵時代、農業時代、工業時代或者是「新經濟」時代,台灣均曾利用對外貿易達成資源的有效運用和經濟的成長。因為外在環境和內部政治局勢的演變,台灣在貿易政策上曾經歷鎖國、開港、貿易保護、貿易擴張等不同的時代。
objectives: 本課程主要目的在於探討貿易發生的原因以及各國所常採行之貿易政策及工具。此外,將結合貿易理論之基本概念與世界貿易時勢,以引導同學發掘問題,解決問題,希望能誘發同學們的學習興趣,並有助於未來專業知識之培養。

title: 產業經濟學(一) Industrial Economics (I)
description: 本課程探討不完全競爭市場中廠商的策略互動,著重於經濟模型的建構、推導,以及模型結果的經濟意涵。課程將先回顧古典寡占模型,並介紹分析多階段賽局的基本方法,作為後續分析的基礎。在此基礎上,進一步探討產業經濟學的核心議題,包括產品差異化、企業併購、垂直整合與垂直契約、研發與創新,以及網絡外部性,並探討相關的競爭政策意涵。整個課程中,數學模型不僅是分析工具,也是推導理論結果,建立經濟直覺,以及理解實際產業現象的重要基礎。
objectives:
課程目標
本課程旨在透過經濟模型的建構、推導與應用,使學生理解不完全競爭市場中廠商的決策、策略互動與市場結果,並培養其運用經濟模型分析產業問題及解釋其經濟與政策意涵的能力。
學習成果
順利完成本課程,學生將能夠:
1. 運用經濟模型分析不完全競爭市場中的廠商行為與市場結果。
2. 運用賽局理論推導模型均衡,並解釋其經濟意涵。
3. 解釋產品差異化、企業併購、垂直整合與垂直契約、研發創新,以及網絡外部性等主要議題的經濟機制。
4. 應用經濟模型分析現實產業問題。
5. 解釋模型分析結果的經濟與政策意涵。
grading:
期中考:50%
期末考:50%

title: 勞動經濟學 Labor Economics
description: This course has two main objectives. First, it develops students' ability to use labor economics theory to analyze past and ongoing changes in labor markets. Second, it introduces key empirical facts and evidence about work, wages, and employment, highlighting how economists use data to evaluate labor market outcomes and policies. While students are not expected to conduct advanced statistical analyses, the course will help them understand the basics of empirical reasoning, interpret research findings, and appreciate the role of evidence in testing economic theories. Special attention will be given to current and emerging challenges in labor markets, with frequent discussion of the potential impacts of labor market policies.
objectives:
Explain central concepts in labor economics and discuss their relevance to real-world labor market issues.
Apply basic mathematical models to describe and clarify labor market problems.
Understand the role of empirical research in evaluating labor market policies and interpret findings from published empirical studies.
grading:
Exams (50% of total grade)
Midterm Exam (25%) and Final Exam (25%) will cover concepts, theories, and empirical findings from lectures and readings.
Presentation and Policy Brief (50% of total grade)
Each student will prepare two presentations and a written policy brief on a selected labor market policy (e.g., minimum wage, parental leave, unemployment benefits, gig economy regulation).
Midterm Presentation: 5%
Final Presentation: 15%
Written Policy Brief: 30%
Institutional background: Describe the policy, how it works, when and why it was implemented, and relevant legal/administrative details.
Theoretical analysis: Use labor economics theory to explain expected effects on labor market outcomes.
Evidence review: Summarize results from at least two credible empirical studies
Presentation Schedule
10/22, 12/10, 12/17
Submission Deadline
The final written policy brief is due December 31th.
prerequisite: [ 經濟學(全學年)(修習且及格)]

title: 環境經濟學 Environmental Economics
description:
This course is designed to introduce to undergraduate and postgraduate students the pertinent economic theories and their applications to contemporary environmental problems. We will firstly introduce the Economics-based analytical approaches for environmental studies. We particularly focus on contemporary environmental issues such as pollution, greenhouse gases emissions and virtual trade of natural resources. Secondly we will discuss the literature on the nexus between trade, national economy and sustainability. Countries derive additional economic benefits from trade than otherwise, for example, with augmented domestic production. Natural environment and resources are used as input for producing exported goods (or to accommodate pollutants discharged from the production process). However, environmental stress concomitant with the economic boom was not properly attended nor charged. Typical of such case, Asian-Pacific economies are attracting the world’s attention in their rapid economic growth, sizable markets and increasingly significant role in the global economy. Domestic and global factors have together shaped the diverse economies in this region, particularly in their economic structure and development pathways and strategies. Inextricably linked with economic activities, environmental quality and natural resource endowment in this region are facing tremendous stress from far and near. Developed and developing countries of this region share a common development experience by thriving their economies on trade, though now even more intensive globalization. Sustainable development in both the economy and environment is thus concerned. A good grasp of the economy-environment nexus from both economy-wide and world-wide perspectives is imperative and helpful in guiding pertinent policies to effectively tackle the dual challenge of sustainability transition.
The course participants are encouraged to get involved in the discussion on issues and analyses particularly from the perspectives of economics, and to summarize in the form of academic writing the insights and policy implications derived from the literature review. Students will form small groups to present and discuss on selected papers. Presentations of the group projects by the students on their literature review of pertinent theories, applications and policy assessment will culminate with the course.
The topics we will review of literature centering the nexus of trade, economy and the environment, mainly from economic perspectives, are:
The nexus between trade, economy and the environment,
Environment impact of economic activities,
Natural resource leakage from developing countries,
Economic development pathways and strategies of the developed countries, and their experiences in managing the concomitant environmental stress,
Economic analysis on policies for correcting negative externality of economic activities, and
Measures proposed for green growth.
The participants will get experience in doing academic literature review and writing-up, in addition to the knowledge of trade and environmental economic theories.

title: 經濟數學(一) Mathematics for Economics(I)
description:
經濟學是一門強調精確的社會科學,精確不意味能無誤地進行分析預測,而是明確地呈現分析的方式,讓自己與其他人能客觀判斷分析過程的合理性與有效性。數學提供了一個共同的語言讓經濟學研究者得以精準地彼此溝通,同時它的分析架構也協助研究者能依照一定的程序去解決問題。
本門課將著重介紹線性代數(linear algebra),因為它是一個分析複雜經濟關係的重要數學工具。一般均衡理論、投入產出模型與計量經濟學等領域,都仰賴向量與矩陣來表示多變數方程組。線性代數讓經濟學家能同時分析多個相互影響的變數,有助於理解市場均衡、穩定性與政策效果。此外,機器學習在經濟研究中的應用日益普及,而線性迴歸、神經網路與主成分分析等方法,都建立在線性代數基礎之上。因此,扎實的線性代數能力能提升經濟理論的理解與資料分析的能力。
objectives:
1. 熟悉線性代數的內涵與分析方法.
2. 學習將線性代數應用於經濟議題分析.
3. 為學生在大數據及進階經濟課程打好數學基礎.
grading:
平常考 30%
期中考 35%
期末考 35%
prerequisite: [ 微積分(全學年)(修習且及格)]

title: 金融,理財與生活 Financing, Portfolio choosing and Living
description:
本課程授課重點在介紹金融制度與個人投資理財的基本概念,並分別從理論及制度上,探討及評估政府的各項金融制度對我們個人投資理財的影響。目的在使學習者能透過經濟學的思考方式,認識政府所扮演的財金角色,並對個人投資理財的影響有所了解。此外,對現階段各國個人投資理財所面臨的重要問題,亦將酌量提出討論。
本課程另一目的在訓練同學能分析、解答一般貨幣金融事件,作為一般個人投資理財之參考。如美國及我國中央銀行今年已多次調升利率:透過檢驗金融市場(如債券、股票及外匯市場等),金融機構(如銀行、保險公司、信用合作社等),及貨幣在當前經濟中所佔之重要性(即金融制度是否健全),希望能適切、周詳的解決一些投資理財之問題(如是否應立即購買股票及債券等)。
基於我個人本身及多年學生反應之經驗,一般同學剛接觸金融理財時;常被複雜的英文敘述所困擾,無法直覺理解其中之經濟邏輯,事倍功半且快速降低學習興趣。故我引用國內最佳中文版的金融理財來教授,希望能引發大家研讀的興趣;且上課時會隨時說明其英文意義,並增加和同學之互動(課堂表現優異者,可酌加平時成績最多十分),以加強大家的國際觀。
本課程之主要參考書為黃昱程撰之 <<現代金融市場,2024, 第12版>> (華泰書局出版)。本書作者先前亦曾撰寫金融、貨幣相關之書籍多版,且以淺顯易懂,內容詳盡著稱;本書是其新著,並增加許多最新資料編輯而成,值得大家細心研讀。另外,更重要的是:本書有國內、外大量之實例及統計資料;希望藉由其的導讀與解說,能使大家未來可無礙的閱讀國內、外專業財經報章雜誌,以增強自己財金的國際觀與判斷力,則是本課程另一目的。
授課方式以講授與討論為主,每一學期有兩次考試及作業報告,各占45%,而課堂表現優異者,可酌加平時成績最多十分。

title: 跨境數位貿易 Cross Border Digital Trade
description:
International trade is the economic backbone of most countries in the world. The development of information technologies has pushed forward the trade facilitation and digitalization of cross border exchange. The digital transformation of international trade has reduced the operation time and costs, facilitated the global value chain, and connected the trade and logistics communities globally.
Cross border digital trade attracts higher attention than ever in the post COVID-19 era. While normal international trade procedures and operations which are heavily dependent on paper-documents are interrupted, the use of technologies helps to make the international trade more resilient and lower the barriers of physical documentation. International initiatives as well as respective government’s actions in the implementation of cross border digital trade to increase the scale, scope and speed of trade will be introduced in this course. Challenges including the adoption of new technologies, policy and regulation issues, change of user behavior during the implementation of cross border digital trade will also be discussed in the course.
This course aims to develop students’ knowledge about the digitalization of international trade for increasing their competitive edges in the global business setting.
objectives:
Course Objectives:
This course is targeted at achieving the following objectives:
To enable students with knowledge of cross border digital trade
To equip students with the knowledge of the emerging information technologies in international trade
To prepare students who wish to enter into global trade businesses
grading:
Grading Policy
The final grade consists of:
Attendance & Participation 30%
The various in-class activities will include case discussion, class participation, and peer review. Students who are unable to attend class should please apply for a leave of absence in advance.
2. Course Reflection 20%
The class reflection should consist of the students’ takeaway, lesson learnt, or insights from the course. It should be a maximum of 2-pages, 12points Times New Roman/Arial, double-spaced.
3. Midterm Paper - A review of your country’s digital trade initiatives 20%
The midterm paper is an individual assignment to understand the students’ knowledge about digital trade. Each student shall write a short review paper about the digital trade initiatives of their respective countries. This assignment should include the concepts from previous lessons, including the challenges faced in the digital trade implementation, the implementation steps, the reengineered processes, the benefits of the digital trade projects and the students’ comments about the current status.
It should be a maximum of 5-pages, 12points Times New Roman/Arial, double- spaced.
4. Final Presentation – Best Practices of Cross Border Digital Trade 30%
The final project is a group project. More explanation on group sizes and how the assignment can be conducted will be provided in class.
Prior to the final presentation, students will be arranged a session to present their proposal about their final projects for obtaining feedback from the instructor and classmates.
Each team shall present a best practice or a new idea of cross border digital trade implementation for the final project. The final project includes an oral presentation and a 2-pages executive summary.
Class Contract
As the course instructor, I aim to help students develop their knowledge of cross border digital trade beyond the textbook. title: 民族學 Ethnology
description: 本課程旨在提供民族學的基礎知識,包括學科的起源及演變、重要的理論內容,並探討本學科在當代的發展取向。
objectives:
本學期(上學期)的課程包含三大單元: 單元一:民族學中討論人群社會時常運用的核心觀念(亦即對於人群文化的理解);單元二:民族學/人類學的起源、分立及其在西方的發展;單元三:民族學與當代世界。
