title: 質性研究 Qualitative Research
description:
本課程為一針對碩士班學生所設計之一學期課程。在此課程中,參與者將透過理論學習與實務操作的方式,經由文獻閱讀、課堂參與、研究設計與實際操作等多元學習管道,以認識質化研究方法之基本原則,並瞭解基本的執行程序。
研究方法的學習,不能只靠「紙上談兵」,需要透過實際的運用,才能獲得較為深入的理解,也只有透過實際操作的經驗,才能發現實作上的問題,並可以經由實際的問題情境尋求解決之道。因此,在這門課中,參與的同學彼此間將會形成合作式的學習關係。首先,在學期開始之初,參與的同學將以約2人為一「研究小組」,並找出共同有興趣的研究主題,透過這門課程,一起規劃、設計並執行一項適合以質性研究方法執行的小型研究(所謂「小型」,是指在一學期內可以本身的資源完成之研究規模)。另外,每一研究小組必須與至少另二研究小組形成「學習伙伴」的關係。「學習伙伴」彼此具有協助學習並提供支持的責任與義務,除了必須負責閱讀並評論彼此每週繳交的作業之外,並需對「學習伙伴」所執行的研究中的每一環節提供適時的建議及所需的鼓勵。也就是說,「學習伙伴」之間,將會形成彼此協助及激勵的關係。
本課程預計在第四週(開始繳作業的週次會在開學後依教學進度作必要的調整)起,會依據課程進度每位參與同學每週繳交作業。繳交作業的目的,在於配合課程進度在自身的研究中實際執行所學,並呈現操作結果。我們會利用每週上課時間,就每一研究小組所繳交的作業進行討論。同學們將於課堂中簡單報告當週研究進度,並可就所面臨的各項問題提出討論。在課堂討論中,除了所搭配的「學習伙伴」必須對所討論的作業以及研究執行者提出建議外,課堂中的其他參與同學,亦需就所討論的作業內容提出看法。作業請於每週一當晚午夜前上傳作業至數位教學平台之「課程討論區」,以供授課老師及班上其他同學閱讀。為讓老師及同學有時間於上課前閱讀各人所繳交之作業,作業請勿缺繳或逾時繳交!
objectives: 在此課程中,參與者將透過理論學習與實務操作的方式,經由文獻閱讀、課堂參與、研究設計與實際操作等多元學習管道,以認識質化研究方法之基本原則,並瞭解基本的執行程序。

title: 全球衛生治理 Global Health Governance
description:
As the world becomes increasingly interconnected, complex health issues—including pandemics, climate-driven health crises, chronic diseases, and digital health innovations—transcend national boundaries, demanding integrated, multidisciplinary, and global solutions. This course is designed to equip future global health policymakers and practitioners with the analytical skills, evaluative insights, and creative strategies essential for effective health governance in a rapidly evolving global landscape.
Throughout the semester, students will critically examine pressing global health governance issues, including infectious diseases, mental health, NCDs, equitable medicine access, digital health data privacy, health system strengthening, primary healthcare strategies, and the role of international health organizations. Each session, led by expert instructors and guest speakers, encourages students to actively analyze complex scenarios, evaluate diverse perspectives, and propose innovative policy solutions.
In the final weeks, students will actively participate in a World Health Organization (WHO) simulation exercise. This highly interactive simulation challenges students to synthesize knowledge and apply their analytical and creative problem-solving skills in realistic, high-stakes public health emergencies. Students will represent various countries and stakeholder roles, collaborating with invited external experts, civil society representatives, and media professionals. Through this experiential learning approach, students will cultivate competencies essential for addressing complex global health governance challenges in real-world contexts.
objectives:
Knowing the current global health issues and risks, such as emerging infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases, climate change, and accidents.
Understanding how global health governance works, its strengths and weaknesses in addressing global health issues.
Developing student’s ability for participating in international conferences, oral presentations, and group collaboration.
Building students’ capabilities in conducting research via specific media, literature, and databases, having frontline experience of health policy-makers through WHO simulation.
Broadening the horizons beyond students’ current disciplines and professions, increasing the understanding of public health, biomedicine, and international relationship.

title: 教育社會學專題討論 Seminar in the Sociology of Education
description:
本課程為教育社會學的進階專題討論,採取社會學視角檢視教育場域,主要目的在於訓練學生理解教育社會學次領域的相關文獻,理論對話,並涵蓋有關學校角色、學校與家庭之間的關係、從學校到勞動市場的轉銜,以及橫跨不同教育階段之歷史與當代辯論。
要理解教育社會學,首要的條件便是閱讀。透過閱讀文獻和理論,並不斷和這些經典或經驗研究對話,能夠豐富對於教育社會學的理解。我們也會透過最後幾門課,討論何時、如何選擇使用哪些分析概念、以及所閱讀的文獻是否能夠適用於台灣本土的教育議題。此外,我們也將平衡質化和量化方法,探究不同方法如何研究同一教育課題。
objectives: 每週課程約三小時,課堂分為兩個部分。前半堂將討論指定閱讀書目,並介紹補充資料以豐富課堂討論;後半堂則根據指定參考文獻探討問題、學術謎題與延伸議題。每位學生都應積極參與課堂討論,並與同儕交換想法。前半堂課堂討論時,我希望你能具體針對指定讀物發言,而非僅談論其他相關主題。閱讀文獻時,請特別注意以下幾點:(1)學者如何界定其研究問題(2)學者如何承接並連結既有文獻(3)學者提出了哪些答案?(4)這些研究和你自己研究的關聯。主動參與課堂,並且閱讀文獻是這堂課參與的基本條件。另外,在研究所的過程中,授課教師的意見並非絕對,和同儕交換意見也很重要。很多珍貴的想法,往往是由同儕互動過程所激發出來。後半堂課,我們會針對具體的問題交換想法。

成績將依據你的課堂參與、作業評定。規律出席並積極參與課堂討論相當重要,也是本堂課的基礎。

你可以選擇撰寫研究論文或者研究計畫書,可使用中文(一萬字以內)或英文(八千字以內)如下。計畫書與研究論文的差異,在於計劃書是「前瞻性思考研究的可能路徑」,而研究論文則必須建立在基本的發現、論證、和經驗資料之上。歡迎依據個人修課需求而選擇其一撰寫,評分標準則以完整性,獨創性,以及書寫完整性為主。
研究論文應包含學術論文的基本要素,例如緒論、文獻回顧、研究方法、研究發現、討論與結論。我希望你特別重視研究發現,因為這是清楚闡述實證結果並使其與既有文獻對話的部分。如果已經有初稿希望能夠藉由此課堂改寫投稿,也很歡迎。
研究計畫書應包含計劃書的基本要件,例如研究動機、文獻回顧、預期資料與分析方法、理論貢獻。研究計畫書的重點在於「大小適中」,「研究可行性」,以及概念切入角度是否創新或者具有原創性。在這堂課中,我們將透過閱讀,討論究竟何為「大小適中的研究計畫書」。

研究計畫書應包含計劃書的基本要件,例如研究動機、文獻回顧、預期資料與分析方法、理論貢獻。研究計畫書的重點在於「大小適中」,「研究可行性」,以及概念切入角度是否創新或者具有原創性。在這堂課中,我們將透過閱讀,討論究竟何為「大小適中的研究計畫書」。

title: 初階資產管理(一)與(二) Introduction to Asset Management I and II
description:
本課程旨在為有志投入資產管理領域之大專院校學生,提供完整且實務導向的一年期基礎訓練,協助學生在多變的全球金融環境中建立專業能力,並為未來職涯奠定堅實基礎。課程共分兩學期,結合理論與實務,涵蓋總體經濟與國際市場、金融商品基礎、投資組合入門,以及風險識別與法令四大主軸;內容自總體經濟環境出發,逐步深入至個別金融商品之操作策略、投資組合理論與風險管理架構,全面強化學生對資產管理業務之理解與應用能力。
第一學期著重於總體經濟與國際市場動態、資本流動趨勢,以及各類金融商品之特性與投資策略;第二學期則承接前一學期基礎,聚焦於理財規劃與投資策略、風險管理架構與法令遵循。兩學期均由具豐富業界經驗之講師授課,協助學生深入了解市場運作邏輯,並學習將理論應用於實際投資判斷與風險評估。
課程採每週影片自學結合實體課堂之混合式教學模式:學生須於課前自主觀看當週教材影片,於實體課堂中再由授課教師進行重點複習,並透過結構化之合作學習活動深化理解與記憶,最後以隨堂測驗檢核學習成效(詳見「每週學習方式」與「教學方法」二節)。課程亦包含分組課堂報告以強化學習成果,並於學年課程結束後,另行安排跨校交流活動,邀請表現優異學生組隊參與專題報告競賽,由業界主管進行評審與回饋,藉此增進學生與業界之互動與連結;此活動與課程進度表中各週次之「專題演講」為不同性質之安排,前者為學期外之跨校競賽活動,後者為課堂內之邀請講者演講。
本課程對應之基本素養:透過分析總體經濟、國際市場趨勢及各類金融商品應用,培養學生對全球資產管理市場之專業理解與國際視野,提升其於多元文化與跨境資本流動環境中之決策與溝通能力;同時,課程涵蓋風險識別與法令遵循,強調誠信經營與合規精神,培育學生之職業倫理意識與金融責任感。課程亦引導學生思考資產管理於社會責任與人文關懷上的角色,透過保險與信託等工具之應用,探討財富傳承與社會公平之實踐,鼓勵學生於追求財務績效之餘,兼顧個人、家庭與社會福祉之平衡。結合業界實務導師之課程設計,協助學生有效銜接職場,成為兼具理論素養、實戰能力與社會責任感之資產管理新秀。
本課程無先修或先備條件,課程設計係針對尚不具資產管理相關基礎之學生。上、下兩學期修畢且成績及格者,由臺灣金融研訓院頒發證書。
objectives:
建立總體經濟與國際市場基礎知識,理解總體經濟指標與政策對資本市場之影響。
認識主要金融商品(如債券、ETF、期貨與選擇權等)及其運作原理與投資應用。
掌握投資組合理論與基本策略,理解資產配置與風險分散之實務應用。
熟悉金融風險分類與法令遵循要求,具備基礎之風險管理與法遵意識。
培養具國際視野與社會責任感之資產管理專業素養,強化職涯接軌能力與人文關懷思維。

title: 基金管理 Fund Management
description:
本課程將探討基金管理所需財務金融、風險管理、投資分析、經濟、會計及法律等多元層面的考量因素及追求基金長期穩健績效的策略作法:
基金管理為確保財務穩健需落實資產負債風險管理,本課程將探討銀行、保險、退休基金等不同財務架構造成現金流量收入與支出差異,如何建構有效率且穩健的資產負債風險管理策略。
永續投資是全球資本市場的重要發展趨勢,透過 ESG 評估與氣候風險管理,引導資金投入減碳技術與綠色產業,本課程將探討碳稅(費)、總量管制交易等碳定價制度的影響,面對全球氣候變遷風險如何管理基金投資組合之實體風險及轉型風險,並掌握未來潛在之轉型投資機會。
因全球地緣政經風險產生不確定性,導致供應鏈重組引發通貨膨脹疑慮,造成全球金融市場大幅波動,各國多採取財政金融貨幣政策因應,本課程將探討財政金融貨幣政策對金融市場的影響,及如何透過多元資產配置建構具效率的投資組合。
上市櫃公司經營階層與投資人間存在資訊不對稱的代理問題,主管機關推動公司治理相關機制以強化資訊透明度,本課程將探討公司治理相關機制及基金投資如何評估公司治理相關面向以降低投資風險。
基金全權委託資產管理業者代為操作,本課程將探討相關績效與指標及目標差異之歸因分析,以及委託契約及法規對投資限制及利益衝突等規範,內部控制稽核及法規遵循的評估。
本課程將探討證券交易法有關資訊揭露與證券交易規範及民刑事責任。

探討基金氣候風險管理及永續投資趨勢
研析全球政經風險與基金多元資產配置
討論上市櫃公司資訊不對稱與公司治理評估議題

探討證券交易法有關資訊揭露與證券交易規範

title: 永續發展商業模式:選擇、實施與最佳案例分析 Sustainable Business Strategy: Choice, Implementation and Best Practices Sharing
description:
Sustainable Business Strategy: Choice, Implementation, and Comparative Benchmarking in Corporate Governance
永續商業策略:全球標竿企業之 ESG 選擇、實施與治理合規對比
This course aims to lead students into a deep exploration of the core values of Social Responsibility (S) and Corporate Governance (G) within the ESG framework, while critically benchmarking key environmental (E) performance indicators. The curriculum systematically covers the structural impact of the net-zero transition on corporate operations, operational standards for social sustainability, and best practices for implementing corporate governance across distinct industry environments. Special emphasis will be placed on Social Responsibility (such as international human rights, Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion [DEI], and employee family-care benefits) and Corporate Governance (including legal compliance, supply chain governance, and tax transparency).
The core training of this course centers on "Strategic Choice, Implementation Evaluation, and Comparative Industry Benchmarking." Students will systematically read and analyze the English Sustainability Reports of top global tech giants (Apple, TSMC, Microsoft, HP, Google), alongside traditional sectors and global luxury brands (textile/apparel industries and the LVMH Group). The course will guide students to focus on and dissect the differentiation and implementation across three critical dimensions:
Environmental (E) Commitment and Execution: Examine the strategic choices regarding water stewardship and net-zero carbon emission commitments across various industries, and critically track their latest implementation progress.
Strategic Depth of Social Responsibility (S): Deconstruct how corporations align with International Human Rights standards, implement DEI policies—specifically focusing on family-care mechanisms (e.g., parental leave, maternity/paternity leave, and family support)—and manage labor rights within complex global supply chains.
Corporate Governance (G) and Compliance Thresholds: Integrating fiscal and strategic thinking, this dimension explores legal and internal corporate Compliance, and how such compliance is extended to global Supply Chain Governance and corporate tax transparency.
Through domestic and international case studies of both success and failure, expert forum debates, and quantitative/qualitative analysis of sustainability reports, students will learn to objectively evaluate corporate sustainability performance and propose forward-looking strategies and policy recommendations for practical challenges.
本課程專為創新國際學院、財政學系高年級與研究生設計,是一門兼具國際視角、ESG實務規範與公司治理評估的英語教學(EMI)核心進階課程。
本課程旨在引領學生深入探討 ESG 中的社會責任(Social, S)與公司治理(Governance, G)的核心價值及其對現代組織的重要性,同時精準對比環境(E)維度的關鍵績效。課程內容涵蓋氣候變遷淨零轉型對組織運作影響的系統性分析、社會責任的實務操作規範,以及如何在不同產業環境中落實公司治理的最佳實踐。本課程特別針對企業在社會責任(如國際人權、多元平等包容 DEI、員工福利與家庭照護等面向)及公司治理(如法律遵循合規性 Compliance、供應鏈管理與租稅透明度)等提供深入的剖析與探討。
課程的核心訓練在於「實戰報告研讀、利害關係人分析與跨產業比較」。學生將系統性地閱讀並分析頂尖科技巨頭(Apple, TSMC, Microsoft, HP, Google)、自行車產業、傳統產業與國際精品品牌(紡織/成衣業與NIKE, Addidas, LVMH 集團, Zara等)的英文永續報告書(Sustainability Reports)。課程將帶領學生聚焦並剖析三大維度的落實程度與差異化:
環境(E)承諾與實踐: 檢視各產業在水資源管理、零碳排(Net-Zero)承諾上的積極度,並批判性地追蹤其最新的執行進度(Implementation Progress)。
社會責任(S)的策略深度: 深度剖析企業如何因應國際人權(International Human Rights)標準、落實多元平等包容(DEI)政策,特別是家庭照護機制(如適親假、產假、育嬰假等工作與生活平衡機制),以及在複雜的全球供應鏈中進行勞工權益管理。
公司治理(G)與合規底線: 結合財政與策略思維,探討企業在法律與內部規範的合規性(Compliance),以及如何將合規延伸至供應鏈管理(Supply Chain Governance)與國際租稅透明度。
透過國內外成功與失敗案例研究、企業專家分享、以及永續報告書的量化與質化分析,學生將學習如何客觀評估不同產業標竿企業在永續治理上的表現,並能針對實務問題提出具前瞻性的策略與改善建議
objectives:
Learning Objectives and Outcomes
Objectives
Mastering Transition and Governance: Comprehend the impacts of net-zero transitions and water scarcity on corporate operations, and master the best practices of social responsibility, regulatory compliance, and corporate governance.
Connecting Social Strategy with Performance: Deeply explore the practical execution of social responsibility (particularly international human rights, family care, and DEI) and its long-term impact on corporate reputation, talent attraction, and financial/fiscal health.
Advanced Sustainability Report Deconstruction: Cultivate the ability to independently read and critically analyze quantitative E, S, and G metrics and implementation timelines within the sustainability reports of tech, textile, and luxury retail sectors.
Strategic Proposal and Critical Thinking: Develop problem-solving capabilities to combine fiscal tools and organizational strategy to formulate concrete, actionable solutions for corporate governance deficiencies and supply chain vulnerabilities.
Outcomes
Critical Evaluation of Cross-Industry Sustainability Strategies Students will be able to independently read, deconstruct, and critically analyze the English sustainability reports of multinational corporations across tech, traditional manufacturing, and luxury retail sectors. They will develop the practical capacity to precisely evaluate actual implementation progress against environmental (E) commitments (e.g., water stewardship and net-zero targets) and effectively identify potential greenwashing practices.
Strategic Planning for Social Responsibility and Inclusive Governance Students will be able to proficiently apply international human rights and Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) frameworks to deeply dissect the variations in employee welfare and family-care strategies across diverse industries. They will acquire the skills to formulate forward-looking strategic plans and actionable solutions for multinational organizations aiming to protect labor rights and optimize work-life balance
Audit and Assessment of Corporate Governance, Legal Compliance, and Supply Chain Management Risks: Integrating finance and business strategy perspectives, students will be able to systematically evaluate a corporation's compliance thresholds, tax transparency performance, and the execution of its global supply chain governance. They will be equipped to accurately identify and assess potential fiscal risks and reputational damages arising from governance failures or regulatory non-compliance.
教學目標
掌握轉型與治理精髓: 理解淨零轉型與水資源壓力對企業運營的影響,並熟練掌握社會責任、合規性及公司治理的最佳實踐。
深掘社會責任與績效關聯: 深入探討社會責任(尤指國際人權、家庭照護與 DEI)的實務操作,及其對企業形象、人才吸引力與財務績效的長期影響。
具備跨產業報告書解構能力: 培養獨立閱讀並批判性分析科技業、紡織成衣業與奢侈品零售業英文永續報告書中 E、S、G 數據與執行進度的能力。
展現策略提案與批判思考: 培養學生分析和解決問題的能力,能結合財政工具與組織策略,針對企業在供應鏈管理及合規缺陷上提出具體的建議方案。
學習成效
跨產業永續戰略之批判性評估能力 學生將閱讀並批判性分析跨國企業(包含科技巨頭、傳統製造業與國際精品品牌)的英文永續報告書,並能精準評估其在環境(E,如水資源與零碳進度)承諾上的真實執行成效,具備識別「綠洗(Greenwashing)」的實戰辨析能力。
社會責任與包容治理之策略規劃能力 學生能熟練運用國際人權與多元平等包容(DEI)框架,深度剖析不同產業在員工福祉與家庭照護(如親職假、產假與育嬰假等)的布局差異,並能針對跨國組織在保障勞工權益與優化工作生活平衡上,提出具前瞻性的策略規劃與改善方案。
公司治理、法律遵循合規性與供應鏈風險之審查能力 結合財務,法務與商業策略視角,學生能系統性地評估跨國企業的法規遵循合規性(Compliance)、財務透明度表現,以及其將合規機制延伸至全球供應鏈治理的成效,並能準確識別與評估組織因治理失當或違反法規所面臨的潛在風險與商譽損失。

title: 國際租稅法 International Tax Law
description:
Since the 2008-2009 financial crisis, the complex planning of multinational enterprises in the area of tax has caught much attention of the societies around the world. In addition, the events surrounding Panama Papers and Paradise Papers have also caused many governments to attempt to address the enforcement issues for crossborder tax matters.
This course aims to examine the various ways in which various jurisdictions tax individual persons and legal persons on their activities both within and beyond their borders. This course introduces the basic structure of international tax law and its foundational concepts, and prepares students to do research on the contemporary topics.
English is the medium of instruction for this course. English is also the medium of assessment.
objectives:
1. Learning the basic structure of international tax law and its foundational concepts.
2. Learning to do research on relevant topics.
3. Learning the various ways to evaluate the policy implications of law and court judgments.

title: 循環經濟和永續發展 Circular Economy and Sustainability
description: Numerous studies have pointed out that the nature of climate change is an international and intergenerational externality problem. This human-induced change in the rising global mean temperature is mainly due to the enormous emission of carbon dioxide arising from the combustion of fossil fuels. To date, more than 100 countries have adopted a global warming limit of 2°C or below (relative to pre-industrial times) as a general guideline (IPCC, 2007). That is, the concentration of carbon dioxide should be maintained at a range of 400-450 parts per million (ppm). The major topics will at least include: (1) Prof. Kenneth Boulding's Economics, (2) Waste and Externalities, (3) The Outdated Coase Theorem, (4) Capital Depreciation and Regeneration, (5) Endogenous Growth Theory and Sustainable Growth, (6) Circular Goods and Services, (7) Sustainable Finance, (8) Circular Business Models, (9) Circular GDP, (10) The Circular Economy National Income Accounting, (11) The UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and (12) Sustainability Policy. Conceptual and theoretical work will be given equal consideration.
objectives: This course trains students to apply Prof. Brian Lin's CE Set framework analytically. By the end of the semester, students will be able to distinguish sustainability disclosure from measurable sustainable development (SD) and conduct firm-level SD evaluation with structural discipline.

Participation in the designated field trip is mandatory.

title: 循環商業模式 Circular Business Models
description: This course trains students to apply Prof. Brian Lin's CE Set framework analytically. By the end of the semester, students will be able to distinguish sustainability disclosure from measurable sustainable development (SD) and conduct firm-level SD evaluation with structural discipline. Numerous studies have pointed out that the nature of climate change is an international and intergenerational externality problem. This human-induced change in the rising global mean temperature is mainly due to the enormous emission of carbon dioxide arising from the combustion of fossil fuels. To date, more than 100 countries have adopted a global warming limit of 2°C or below (relative to pre-industrial times) as a general guideline (IPCC, 2007). That is, the concentration of carbon dioxide should be maintained at a range of 400-450 parts per million (ppm). As a necessary response to the threat of climate change, more and more corporations and governments have taken measures to promote the circular economy. The major topics will at least include: (1) the circular economy, (2) sustainable development, (3) corporate sustainability, (4) business models, (5) circular business models, (6) natural resource management, (7) waste management, (8) industrial ecology, (9) corporate social responsibility, and (10) green taxation. Conceptual and theoretical work will be given equal consideration.
objectives:
With global progress of the circular economy (or at least "don't waste waste") in mind, students taking this course are required to take the following elements into account when they investigate the circular economy business models:
1) Vision of a modern corporation or company along with its goals: How does a corporation define sustainability or a sustainable business? What does business innovation mean by the company?
2) Measures adopted by the company for fulfilling the goals: Do the measures taken by the company meet the circular economy or zero-waste standard?
3) Check the existence of a sustainability branch/sector: A company cannot well design a circular business model without a sustainability branch/sector.
4) Do the CSR/Sustainability reports release the tax return principles or tax-related news? If the company cares about the society and is willing to assume corporate social responsibility, the company will at least honestly file the tax returns.
grading:

a. Class attendance and participation (10%)
b. Group presentation: EURO STOXX 50 SD evaluation (50%)
c. Individual final report: independent corporate SD estimation (40%)

title: 貿易政策 Trade Policy
description:
貿易政策的議題,在傳統上,是聚焦在政府應否對外開放其本國的自由貿易、或應否對貿易作某種管制的討論上。而無論哪一種政策工具,一旦施行,便不可避免地會國際市場的供需產生或多或少的影響,也因此會影響到貿易的價格、貿易的數量、國內的生產、國內的消費、乃至所得分配等等的面向,而最終也將會影響到社會福利。
The issues of trade policy are traditionally focused on whether the government should open its domestic market, or whether certain types of restrictions should be implemented. Once implemented, any type of trade policy tool will inevitably more or less affect the demand and supply of international market, and hence affect the prices and quantities of trade, domestic consumption, and income distribution, among others, and at last affect the social welfare.
objectives:
本課程以貿易理論為其基礎,以探討貿易政策在國際貿易各個面向中的角色,及其最終對社會福利的影響。在學習完本課程後,你將可以:
一:瞭解政府干預國際貿易的動機,並理解各類的干預手段諸如關稅、配額、出口補貼、出口自動設限等的運作機制。
二:瞭解開發中國家及工業化國家兩類國家常見的貿易政策,並明白其利弊得失。
三:瞭解世界貿易組織對國際貿易的規範,及其對本國的影響。另外也會能瞭解國際上最流行的區域貿易協定的議題。
This course explores, on the basis of the theories of trade, the role of trade policies in various aspects of international trade, and their effects on social welfare. The content of this course can be divided into three parts:
1. I will first talk about the government’s incentives to intervene in international trade, and then introduce various policy tools such as tariffs, quotas, export subsidies, VER (Voluntary Export Restraint), and so on.
2. I will introduce common trade policies implemented by developing and developed countries, and discuss their pros and cons.
3. I will talk about some rules set by the WTO for international trade, and discuss their effects on domestic country. Other issues frequently discussed recently such as regional free trade agreement (FTA) will also be mentioned if time allows.

description: 本課程的起點是Hotelling (1929)模型,他探討雙占廠商如何在一直線市場進行區位與價格競爭,由於Hotelling 錯誤地得到廠商會聚集在市場中央的結果,導致d’Aspremont et al. (1979) 與一系列的論文嘗試解決Hotelling 均衡解的問題,或是將Hotelling 模型修改假設之後應用到不同領域,如產品差異化,或是政黨與媒體競爭的議題。本課程將著重在數十篇重要文獻之詳細解構,使學生可以徹底瞭解文章的重要性與如何用數學軟體重建文章的數學模型,並進而模仿改良完成自己的學期報告。

title: 應用計量分析—中國財政研究 Applied Econometrics for Topics in China's Fiscal Policy
description:
本課程主要是提供財政所、地政所、國發所、東亞所、以及其他研究所想要從事大陸財政或相關實証研究的碩士、博士研究生,在不熟悉以電腦估計模型之背景下,充分瞭解每一個計量模型之緣起、其中蘊含之意義、應用、與熟練之電腦操作技巧,並在其從事中國財政議題,或是其他研究領域(例如,經濟、政治、社會與其他相關領域)之實証研究時,能夠充分掌握計量模型之正確運用。計量模型主要是以統計學為基礎,而發展出來的一種因果關係的研究方法。更具體的說,就是在控制其他因素的情形下,研究一變數對另一變數之影響,或變數之間如何相互影響的方法。計量模型會因分析資料的型態、特質、或研究的課題之不同有所差異。例如,橫斷面資料、追蹤資料、截斷資料、質量資料、期間資料、時間序列資料、空間資料等等之資料型態;與連續變數、選擇變數、計數資料、順序變數、間斷變數等等之資料特質。因此,本課程之授課內容將先講解統計學的基本概念,再介紹不同類型資料所應採用的各種計量模型。
本課程特別開設在上學期,主要的原因如下:
對於碩一的新生而言,修習這一們課可以儘早學習未來碩士論文所要進行模型估計的技巧,並儘早確認碩士論文的研究方向。
對於碩二的同學而言,可以在修習這一門課時,隨著上課的進度將碩士論文所要研究的資料,先將資料處理然後再進行估計,修完本課程也完成碩士論文實証資料的估計。
對於博士班的同學而言,本課程將教授一些目前學術界比較新的實証模型,修習本課程將有助於博士的論文在SSCI期刊發表。
objectives:
有鑑於部分同學對計量分析的涉略不深,因此本課程的設計特點如下:
1. 由簡入深,降低進入門檻。本課程將先簡要複習統計學基本概念,而後將大多數的時間用來說明計量經濟的研究方法,最後介紹近來發展的計量分析模型與運用。
2. 主要以觀念之解說為主,盡量減少以數學的方式說明。
3. 配合各計量模型的多樣化相關應用文獻的導讀(主要是以與中國大陸財政有關的實証研究學術論文為主),來說明各模型之在中國大陸各財政議題的應用方向,並可讓修課的同學瞭解量化分析研究的進行過程與撰寫方式。
4. 特別重視計量軟體之操作技巧與模型估計之解釋,並確保每一位同學都能利用電腦軟體進行估計與解釋。
5. 提供上課時電腦教學每一步驟之圖片說明,以方便同學瞭解與下課後之複習與練習。
相信修習本課程後,同學在從事中國大陸的財政研究或其他領域(例如,國際經濟、政治、社會、大陸、台灣以及其他相關問題)的研究時,在研究方法上能有更多的選擇。並且,對於想以計量分析做為研究方法的碩、博士班的同學而言,這門課程是相當重要且實用的。

每一組選擇一篇與每周主題有關的中文期刊文章,進行導讀與評論。選擇的中文期刊最好是TSSCI,或至少具有同儕互評的審查制度。可從議題的邏輯論述、內容、研究方法等部分切入,以客觀的角度進行評析,製作成PPT在課堂上簡報並上傳所評論的文章,導讀與評論時間以15-20分鐘為原則。請避免選擇書評、邀稿文章、議題對話類的文章。
導讀提問回應(10%)
針對導讀小組提問,依據受指定的評論小組(或個人)能否提出完整且具內容和想法來回應/討論,以及回應/討論的深度來給分。
評分標準參考:
二、個人期末報告 50%(口頭報告15%,紙本報告25%,同學互評10%):
個人專題報告內容需與課堂主題相關,可以是1.完整的個案研究、2.理論文獻檢閱、3.公共管理典範的探討、4.實證分析研究。
若以個案研究為例:
口頭報告以時間控制、報告內容清楚與熟悉程度、個案與理論的結合度、資料分析完整度或評論的深度、報告的是否準時繳交PPT等項目來評分。
書面內容(不含參考文獻總字數至少8000字)須包含下列各項:
(1) 前言
簡述個案背景與問題意識。
解釋為何選擇此個案?以及此個案的特色或價值為何?
希望藉由此個案獲得甚麼?想要回答甚麼問題?
(2)個案介紹
需介紹個案完整的人、事、時、地、物,即為相關的利害關係人或團體是誰? 所發生的政策或事件內容是甚麼?何時發生?為何發生?影響的範圍或地區?
個案內容介紹應具體依照時間順序進行闡述,包括個案發生的背景、發生的過程以及最後的結果。
個案內容皆須標注資料來源,資料內容的引用可從報章雜誌、期刊論文或是政府相關文件與檔案(法條)等中蒐集獲取
(3)與理論結合
將個案結合相關理論,例如此個案與公共行政中哪個理論有關? 個案與理論所預期的有何異同? 以及其可能的解釋因素。
(4)結語:
總結個案發展過程中的價值內涵,並提出對於此個案或是理論的建議。
期末紙本報告評分參考:
三、課堂出席與參與(10%)
依發言次數與出席情況計分
A(90分以上) | 優良,導讀與評論文獻內容完整且正確清楚呈現重點,口頭報告PPT具有內容且活潑有創意,報告人口條清楚且在表定時間內完成報告。
B(89-80分) | 佳,導讀與評論文獻內容完整,內容符合所有要求外,口頭報告PPT具有內容,報告人口條清楚且在表定時間內完成報告。
C(79-70分) | 尚可,大致交代導讀與評論文獻內容,內容大致符合要求,口頭報告PPT有基本架構,報告人在表定時間內完成報告,但報告人口條待加強。
D(69分以下) | 不及格,內容不符合要求,未能準時繳交作業,未上傳導讀提問,口頭報告PPT內容架構鬆散,報告人口條不清楚,對自己所要報告的內容不熟悉,未能在表定時間內完成報告。
90分以上 | 優異,內容符合所有基本要求外,報告言之有物且脈絡清晰,能靈活運用課堂理論,並能於結論提出獨特見解。
89-85分 | 優良,內容符合所有基本要求外,報告言之有物,脈絡清楚,也能靈活運用課堂理論,但所提出的分析或歸納結論原創性不足。
84-80分 | 佳,內容符合要求,報告有清楚的架構,可見一定程度的努力,能做出有條理的論述,但所提出的分析或歸納較為薄弱。
79-75分 | 普通,內容大概符合要求,但無法將理論與分析做緊密的連結,報告的脈絡不清楚,結論也缺乏個人對的深入分析。
74-70分 | 尚可,內容大概符合要求,但報告架構鬆散,理論與分析連結不明,脈絡與文字論述不清楚,結論也未能呈現個人的分析與觀點
69分以下 | 不及格,內容不符合基本要求,報告欠缺架構,脈絡不清楚,文字論述能力薄弱,未能提出有內容的結論,有遲交或發現抄襲行為。

title: 質性研究法 Qualitative Research Methods
description:
本課程為碩士班學生所設計,旨在引導學生深入理解質性研究的哲學基礎、方法論取徑與實務應用。透過系統性的理論探討與實作練習,學生將學習如何從公共行政與相關社會議題出發,設計並執行具學術深度與現實關懷的質性研究。
課程強調「做中學」(learning by doing)的學習取徑,學生將透過核心文獻導讀、課堂對話、研究設計演練與田野實作,逐步建構質性研究的觀察力、詮釋力與批判性思維。課程鼓勵學生在方法訓練的過程中,反思自身作為研究者的定位,並培養進行獨立研究的能力。
本課程以公共行政為核心場域,聚焦於以下三大學習面向:
1. 研究典範與知識論的比較
回顧公共行政領域的研究傳統,並從社會科學的知識論出發,探討量化與質性研究的理論基礎與實踐差異。學生將理解不同質性研究類型(如個案研究、民族誌、敘事研究、詮釋現象學等)的邏輯與特徵。
2. 研究設計與實作練習
學生將學習如何擬定研究問題、選擇適切的質性取徑,進行資料蒐集與分析規劃。課程將引導學生從自身關心的公共議題出發,逐步發展出可執行的質性研究設計。
3. 資料分析與研究創作
介紹多元的質性資料分析策略,包括主題分析、紮根理論編碼、詮釋學分析等,並結合實務演練與個別指導,引導學生撰寫具深度與反思性的研究報告。課程最終目標是協助學生完成一份具初步完整度的質性研究作品,作為未來碩士論文或研究發展的基礎。
objectives:
本課程著重於培養學生的批判性閱讀能力與研究素養,透過質性研究經典文獻與當代表現的導讀與討論,建立對質性研究邏輯與哲學基礎的理解。同時,課程鼓勵學生從自身的生活經驗與所處場域出發,反思社會現象與制度實踐,並轉化為具體的研究問題。
學生將學習如何運用質性方法探索公共行政中具有複雜性、價值爭議或制度變遷的議題,掌握資料蒐集、分析與詮釋的實務技巧,進而能夠進行具深度的田野觀察與社會詮釋。透過課程訓練,學生將奠定進行獨立研究的基礎,並拓展其在政策分析、組織研究、公民參與等實務場域中的應用能力。
grading:
分組活動與參與討論 (20%)
導讀(20%)
作業(20%)
期中專題提案說明(10%)
期末專題報告 (30%)
課程要求
本學期課程會根據選課人數進行分組,每組需認領兩週的導讀
課堂參與與導讀 (30%)
課堂參與 :評量項目包括上課出席及討論發言的參與度。學生必須在學習過程中扮演主動及積極的角色,需要在課堂上投入討論與分享看法,並學習對同儕的發表提供建議。
課堂導讀:第二週到第十四週間安排同學進行分組導讀(共有十二個主題),帶領全班同學進行篇章的理解。每篇書的篇章和文章以單獨導讀為主。導讀小組必須準備PPT,並提供課堂討論的提問。
個人作業(30%)
作業一:提出研究背景與問題意識。報告的頁數以1-3頁為主。包括:問題的背景(如:為什麼會對這個問題感興趣?這個問題的背景介紹)、你對這個問題的想法、你的研究提問方向,以及你期待研究可以帶來的貢獻。
作業二:延續作業一之研究問題,進行文獻回顧,並詳細說明研究方法。文獻回顧至少3-5篇以上,報告頁數以8-12頁為主。
作業三:訪談大綱。針對研究問題以及文獻的整理,擬定適當的半結構式訪綱。
作業四:逐字稿初步分析。請至少針對一位受訪者之錄音檔,完成謄寫並進行分析,至少完成第一頁至第四頁的編碼,並且附上對於編碼的反思。
作業格式:請用中文APA 第七版格式。(中文請用 12 號新細明體、1.5 倍行距、繁體中文,英文請用 Times New Roman 12pt。用A4直式紙,橫向書寫,每頁上下邊界2.4公分及左右邊界2.5公分,且每頁都要排頁碼。)
論文研究方法評論(10%)。針對課堂所介紹的質性研究方法,找出論文中有採用此種質性研究方式,特別針對其研究方法的部分進行評論。可以介紹論文的研究重點,主要評論內容至少8百字。完成七篇運用不同的質性研究類型論文評論。
研究報告(30%)
口頭報告:分別於期中及期末進行口頭報告,報告時間每人以10分鐘為限,包括10分鐘報告,以及1分鐘的現場提問與回答。此發表將指定組別互相擔任評論人。評分標準會著重於發表學生之研究提問的完整性,以及給予同儕的評論建議。
書面報告:期末報告為延續作業1、2、3、4,資料蒐集告一段落,進行初步資料分析,並依照本課程所探討的各種質性研究典範的論文形式書寫,除包含研究計畫的各部分外,應加入資料分析、資料的詮釋、文獻(理論)對話與結論(包含對研究過程的反思)等部分。學生可以參酌教師針對期末口頭報告的PPT修改建議,整合於此份報告中。請使用中文APA格式(第七版)作為書寫規範。內容以30頁為限。

title: 行政組織與管理理論研究 Seminar in Administrative Organization and Management
description: 本課程最主要的目標,就是讓研究所層級(特別是博士班)的學生可以在一堂課當中將組織理論與行為的相關理論作一次有效的巡禮,組織理論與行為是公部門行政研究與政治學研究最大的區別所在,也就是說,政治學基本上較少研讀相關理論,因此,這也是公共行政研究一個特殊的理論基礎。
objectives:
本課程以兩本分別討論組織理論與組織行為的研究所教科書為基準,配合上中文與英文的相關論文,期待研究所學生可以一方面全面性地了解公共行政這個重要的基礎,另一方面也讓學生在這個基礎上,尋找自己有興趣的研究題目,完成論文。
批判報告(個人)25%、個案報告(小組)55%、上課參與20%
grading:
課堂教材研讀指引
每週的研讀教材都在第參部份「課程教材研讀大綱」當中列明,學生每週來上課最基本的責任就是「必須研讀」以數字編號的教材(1, 2, 3...),教材(“*”)學生可以視自己狀況許可「選擇研讀」,但是卻是課堂報告同學一定要報告的重點。加總起來,學生在本堂課中,最少可以研讀約35篇文獻,如果加上選讀或是課堂報告的文獻,至多學生可以研讀40篇文獻。
研讀論文最重要的就是回答下面五個問題:
作者最重要處理的研究問題是什麼?該問題為何重要?
作者是如何討論這個問題?他切入的角度有哪些?使用了哪些文獻?
作者討論這個問題的時候,使用了些什麼事件、案例、歷史作為佐證?這些經驗案例的背景是什麼?
作者明示或是暗示的研究方法是什麼?
作者所得到主要的結論有哪些?他們與實務的關聯性為何?
如果研讀時希望能夠有批判的眼光,讀者可以問下面的三個問題:
作者的研究問題與學界的研究焦點是否是相關聯的(relevant)?還是有更好的途徑可以彰顯這個問題的重要性?
作者所使用的研究方法是否適當,過程是否有可以改進的地方?業如何改進?
作者所得出的結論,與作者研究問題以及研究方法之間,存在怎麼樣的邏輯關聯性?這關聯性是否有瑕疵?該如何改進?
鼓勵同學組成小的讀書團體,一起研讀教材,最好是大家都讀完了,再一起討論;當然,如果因為時間的關係,大家分工研讀,老師也不反對,但是要注意,每一個人對整篇文獻的架構都必須有完整的認識。
課堂任務的分配
(一) 課堂導讀:研讀文獻與報告(佔總成績30%)
學生每週上帶領上課教材研讀,視修課人數,碩士班學生一人可能帶2-3次,博士班學生可能帶3-4次,其他非當週帶領的同學請按時研讀相關教材,導讀同學以不超過一個小時為限。教師上課會先做一個小時的整體課程導讀,接著由同學開始導讀(第一週由老師示範一次)。報告內容應包括下列事項:
一份3-5頁(3000字左右)的摘要,影印發給同學(請用電腦打字),將所有電子檔(報告本文、摘要、與PPT)放上「教學精進實驗平台」(Moodle; http://moodle.nccu.edu.tw/login/index.php)。
口頭詳述該文獻內容的重點,並舉一些例子說明之(當自己是老師!)。
個人對於該主題的特殊看法與思考。
提出具體問題讓同學討論,並試著回答課堂學生的疑問。
(二) 批判文章撰寫(佔總成績40%)
(40%,博生8篇,碩生6篇) 批判報告:本學期當中,為了確保同學上課的參與,並鼓勵學生對課程內容進行批判性的思索,學生將負責完成數篇批判報告,碩士班學生應完成。其做法為,同學在學期中必須選擇數次自己喜歡的內容,於上課前一週(最晚不晚於當週),繳交批判文章(referee reports),並放上「教學精進實驗平台」。字數不超過1000字(單行間距12號字形約一頁)。內容請包括下列三個項目:
主要討論議題
主要論述內容與結論
您個人的評論與看法 (重要!請務必提出)
(三) 上課到課與參與(佔總成績10%)
不論是到課或是上課參雨,都將列入計分,一次沒來扣兩分直到前一部份10分扣完為止。問問題是思考的開始,能思考才會問問題,有了問題才能夠解決問題,這些就是觀察公共事務的首要修養,因此,本課程十分重視課堂討論,請學生務必參與發問與討論,上課「有意義」的發言將使提高學生參與成績。
(四) 期末報告:研究計畫寫作 (佔總成績20%)
學期末報告,學生(博、碩)應從十六個課程單元當中,挑選一個單元,從上課readings開始切入進行主題定位,蒐集相關的中英文文獻。
碩士班學生應完成一篇5000~8000字的文獻回顧,將該單元中的文獻作一個整理,做法類似期刊中的review article,只不過篇幅較少。
博士班學生應完成一篇8000~10000字的研究案計畫書,有些像申請國科會的研究案計畫書,其中包括完整的文獻回顧,研究方法設計,以及預期的成果等部份。
第六週請繳交300~500的寫作大綱,目的乃是事先讓老師知道學生寫作的方向,也歡迎學生與老師討論。延遲的同學將酌扣期末論文成績。
總結來說,本課程成績計算的方式如下表所列:
三、寫作倫理遵守

title: 科技法律與資料治理 Technology Law and Data Governance
description:
I. Course Objectives
This course is designed to help students understand the legal and governance issues arising from the development of digital technologies, with data governance as its central focus. It addresses major emerging topics, including personal data protection, artificial intelligence governance, digital platform accountability, open government data, data sharing, cybersecurity, cross-border data flows, and the European Union(EU)’s data governance framework.
Taught entirely in English, the course introduces students to core concepts in contemporary international technology law. It examines legal issues that arise throughout the data life cycle, from collection, processing, use, retention, and sharing to deletion. The course also considers the legality of artificial intelligence systems in model training and content generation, and analyzes the respective responsibilities and obligations of governments, businesses, digital platforms, and data intermediaries in data governance.
The course further incorporates Taiwan’s legal framework, the EU’s General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), Data Governance Act, Data Act, Artificial Intelligence Act, and other significant legislative developments and international trends. Through this comparative approach, students will develop a stronger interest in technology law and acquire the analytical skills needed to address practical legal issues.
II. Course Description
This course begins with legal issues related to data use as an entry point into technology law. It introduces key legal concepts, including personal data protection, informational self-determination, privacy, and data governance, before moving to issues such as open government data, data sharing, data intermediary services, data altruism, data access for Internet of Things devices and connected products, cloud switching, regulation of artificial intelligence technologies, algorithmic transparency, disclosure obligations, and legal requirements for cross-border data transfers.
The course focuses on recent developments in the EU’s data governance regime and explains how the GDPR, Data Governance Act, Data Act, and Artificial Intelligence Act together shape a technology law framework grounded in trustworthiness, data access, and risk management. In addition to introducing major international technology laws, the course includes weekly case discussions to help students examine the relationship between data governance, personal data protection, public interest, industrial innovation, digital market competition, national data sovereignty, and the protection of fundamental rights.
objectives:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
Understand the foundational theories and regulatory structure of technology law and data governance.
Examine legal issues concerning personal data protection, data sharing, digital platform regulation, risk-based regulation of artificial intelligence, and cybersecurity safeguards.
Compare Taiwan’s digital legal framework with the GDPR, Data Governance Act, Data Act, and other major technology laws of the EU.
Assess, from legal and governance perspectives, personal data protection risks and appropriate levels of regulatory oversight arising from artificial intelligence and other technological applications.
Analyze current disputes and cases involving the application of technology law from an independent perspective and propose appropriate legal or policy reforms.

title: 認識災害管理與風險治理 Introduction of Emergency Management and Risk Governance
description: 邁入風險社會時代,面對氣候變遷帶來的極端氣候影響,防救災已成為我國政府與民眾不可忽視的重要課題。本課程透過閱讀相關文獻以及課堂活動,認識災害管理與風險治理相關議題與研究,課程的進行採教師講課、學生分組導讀、課堂討論活動,以及邀請業師演講或校外參訪等多元方式進行,讓修課學生藉此了解災害管理與風險治理相關領域之研究與實務。此外,修課學生需設計個人/家庭防災計畫書於期末課堂上進行口頭報告。本課程依照修課學生之研究興趣,藉由閱讀相關理論累積專業知識,以及師生之間的互動討論,建立災害管理與風險治理的基本知能,並希望能從社會科學面向幫助修課學生認識災害相關研究,並同步提升個人防災意識。
objectives: 本課程透過社會科學角度來認識災害管理與風險治理,以幫助學生:1) 學習災害管理、風險治理的基本概念;2)了解台灣災防相關歷史、組織、體系、與政策;以及3)思考防救災過程中,政治與領導、組織協力、智慧防災、風險溝通、社區防災、防災教育等議題。修課學生期能藉由研讀資料與文獻、參與課堂討論與活動,建立對災害管理與風險治理概念的初步認識與知能,培養災防研究之興趣,並提升個人防救災意識。
grading:
分組導讀 (30%)、設計個人/家庭防災計畫(40%,包含紙本報告25%、期末口頭報告15%)、演講心得(15%)、課堂參與討論與出席 (15%)
一、課堂分組導讀(30%):針對課程的主題內容,修課學生分組進行導讀,每組成員約2-3位,整學期各組約導讀2次,導讀內容須包含文獻摘要與問題討論兩大部分,以簡報方式呈現,並鼓勵結合時事進行相關個案或新聞的介紹。當周負責導讀小組,導讀時間以60分鐘為原則,針對每篇導讀文章至少須提出2項問題,並在上課前三天,先將討論問題上傳Moodle供其他同學閱讀。 其中教材若設為參考用,則不列入導讀範圍。若組員當中無大學部學生,則需額外找一篇與該週主題相關的中英文期刊文章進行導讀介紹。
評分標準參考:
二、個人/家庭防災計畫(40%,包含紙本報告25%、期末口頭報告15%):修課學生每人期末時需繳交個人/家庭防災計畫書,並於期末時透過口頭報告與同學們分享。個人/家庭防災計畫書須包含以下幾大部分:
詳細介紹個人/家庭居住地主要的災害潛勢 [20%]
回顧當地災害史 [20%]
規劃居家逃生路線、介紹鄰近避難處所以及規劃會合地點[20%]
建立緊急連絡方式[10%][個資部分請隱匿呈現]

建立緊急食物、飲水、醫藥、工具裝備確認表 [10%]
建立重要證件、文件、緊急避難金確認表 [10%][個資部分請隱匿呈現]
口頭報告以時間控制、報告內容清楚與熟悉程度、計劃書依個人狀況詳細設計程度、報告的是否準時繳交PPT等項目來評分。
三、演講心得(15%)
演講心得撰寫需繳交至少1000字心得感想,繳交方式為上傳至Moodle;心得內容須結合課程主題,並於最後提出一至兩個討論問題做為反思與回饋,並請依規定時間繳交電子檔與紙本。
四、課堂出席與參與(15%)
將參照事前課堂提問內容、課堂上發言次數,與出席情況計分。
A(90分以上) | 優良,導讀文獻內容完整且正確清楚呈現重點,口頭報告PPT具有內容且活潑有創意,報告人口條清楚且在表定時間內完成報告。
B(89-80分) | 佳,導讀文獻內容完整,內容符合所有要求外,口頭報告PPT具有內容,報告人口條清楚且在表定時間內完成報告。
C(79-70分) | 尚可,大致交代導讀文獻內容,內容大致符合要求,口頭報告PPT有基本架構,報告人在表定時間內完成報告,但報告人口條待加強。
D(69-60分) | 及格,內容勉強符合要求,口頭報告PPT內容架構鬆散,報告人口條不清楚,對自己所要報告的內容不熟悉,未能在表定時間內完成報告。
E(59分以下) | 不及格,內容不符合要求,未能準時繳交作業,未上傳導讀提問,口頭報告PPT內容架構鬆散,報告人口條不清楚,對自己所要報告的內容不熟悉,未能在表定時間內完成報告。

title: 思辨:當代社會議題 Contemporary Social Problems and Justice
description:
This course is designed to introduce the benefits and methods of interdisciplinary study and research for exploring complex social problems and justice. Starting with the U.S. and Taiwan contexts as its foundation, this course expands its global context and weekly discussions by featuring several talented guest lecturers specializing in public administration and management. Their diverse international insights and perspectives provide a rich learning environment.
Students will be guided through the process by learning and applying critical thinking, problem identification, and problem-solving skills to discuss and explore creative policy approaches that integrate differing perspectives.
* Course Schedule and Adjustments:
The course topics and schedule may be adjusted based on speaker availability and details, field trips, as well as students' learning progress and needs. Changes such as rescheduling sessions or extending class time until 12:30 PM may occur when necessary. Any modifications will be announced in advance. As the course includes engaging and diverse activities, your cooperation is essential. Please carefully consider the course schedule and commit to full participation.
* Class Time and Attendance:
Classes begin promptly at 9:20 AM. Please arrive on time and follow the teaching assistant’s instructions at the start of class to complete the required activities, which will help facilitate the day’s lesson. There will be one scheduled break during the session, depending on the course progress.
* Attendance Policy:
Students who plan to enroll in or add to the course must attend the first class. Failure to do so will result in a final grade of zero (0) for the semester, and you will be responsible for withdrawing from the course. Only students who are physically present and complete the First-Day class attendance survey and self-introduction will be considered to have fully attended. First-day attendance and Regular Participation are required. Please read the course schedule carefully.
* Absence and Leave Policy:
Students who are absent without a valid reason, as outlined in the university’s leave policies, will not be allowed to participate in in-class activities, group presentations, or any graded assignments for that day. If you are unable to attend, please notify both the instructor and teaching assistant in advance via email (other forms of communication, such as messaging apps, will not be accepted) and obtain approval. Supporting documentation is required, and you must also complete the official leave process through the university’s system.
* This syllabus is a guide for the course and is subject to change with advance notice. Please pay attention to the newest course announcements, email notifications, and Moodle for updated course materials.
*AI tools may be used only when permitted and in strict accordance with assignment instructions; students must clearly disclose their use, take full responsibility for the content, and ensure academic integrity through proper citation.
*This course is highly participatory, integrative, and collaborative. All assignments are designed to guide students in building critical thinking, problem identification, and problem-solving skills.
objectives:
This course is highly participatory, integrative, and collaborative. Please note that this course is designed as a project-based learning approach with relevant tasks at different phases to help you develop your project and respond to feedback. All assignments are designed to guide students in completing their final project, developing critical thinking, problem identification, and problem-solving skills.
At the completion of this course, students will be able to:
Understand the process and language of interdisciplinary study and research.
Build tolerance for dissonance in conducting interdisciplinary study and research.
Build a deeper understanding of diversity, inclusion, and social justice embedded in the context of interdisciplinary social problems.
Analyze and apply perspectives of multiple disciplines to shape your understanding of complex social problems and social justice.
Critically examine, interpret, and explain the multiple perspectives from disciplines of social science that apply to complex social problems and creative policy solutions/resources.
Practice collaborative, interdisciplinary approaches to problem identification and disciplinary integration.

title: 公共領導與民主創新 Public Leadership and Democratic Innovation
description:
——當代民主失靈的解方?從參與實驗到制度創新
民主政府不一定等同於創新政府。雖然政府是民主理論的核心構成,但當代的代議政治卻日益充斥著民眾的不滿與不信任,對民主制度的滿意度持續下滑,「民主赤字」因而逐漸浮現。在自由民主的環境中,公民對公共服務與治理品質的期待日益提升,然而傳統的政府體制卻難以有效回應,導致治理供需失衡。此時,政府亟需具備公共領導力與引進民主創新,以彌合制度落差。
民主創新強調讓公民能更直接地參與公共行政與治理過程,特別是在政策的設計、執行與監督等關鍵階段。透過這類制度安排,公民不必再倚賴政黨或民選代表作為中介,即可表達自身偏好並參與決策。參與式治理成為深化民主實踐的重要方式。
然而,參與模式的制度化面臨波動與反覆,審議民主雖被寄予厚望,亦無法免除理論與實務層面的挑戰與限制。在這樣的情境下,民主創新展現出作為選舉與代議制度可行補充乃至替代方案的潛力,為當代治理提供嶄新的想像與實踐可能。本課程聚焦於兩大核心議題:「公共領導力」如何在治理轉型中扮演關鍵角色?「民主創新」如何突破代議政治的侷限,實現更具回應性、包容性與正當性的治理?
課程分為四大單元:
民主創新的理論基礎與模式探索
從參與式民主、審議式民主出發,分析其作為現有民主制度補充與修正的潛力,同時探討其內部矛盾與制度極限。
國際與在地案例研究:制度創新的實驗場
深入解析全球各地的創新實踐,包括巴西的參與式預算、加拿大的公民大會、韓國的社區治理,以及台灣自2000年以來的各式民主參與嘗試。課程亦涵蓋電子民主與數位參與的最新發展,探討科技如何重塑公民協作的可能性。
評估民主創新的效能:民主素質的提升可能嗎?
學生將學習如何辨識與評估民主創新的成效與限制,思考參與是否真的讓民主「更好」、更有正當性,還是僅流於象徵。
公共領導力與在地治理的交織:從社區到地方創生
聚焦「公共領導」如何在地方公共議題中實踐,結合近期「地方創生」浪潮,探索在地群體如何透過協作與制度翻新實現共善。
本課程適合對公共治理、民主轉型、數位參與、非營利行動與地方實驗感興趣的同學。透過理論、案例、討論與實作,期望與學生一同思考:當代民主如何再被想像?誰能領導這場轉變?
objectives:
本課程融合民主理論與比較政治的觀點,透過參與式民主與審議民主的規範性討論,結合各國城市層級民主創新實踐的比較分析,引導學生系統性理解當代民主轉型與治理創新的多樣樣態。課程目標如下:
能夠辨識與理解參與式民主與審議民主的主要理論論點與規範基礎。
掌握各類創新參與模式的制度邏輯與操作方式,並能分析其實施條件與潛在限制。
深入探討不同參與模式的制度設計特性與其對政策制定、治理品質與民主正當性的影響。
建立對「群體智慧」與「公共領導力」的初步理解,並透過地方創生相關案例,反思公民如何透過協作參與推動地方治理創新。
grading:
課堂出席與參與討論 25%
課堂導讀 30%
民主創新參與模式的個案介紹15%
期末專題報告 30%
課程要求
小組課堂導讀 (30%)
為每週上課指定的內容詳細閱讀,製作ppt,並且針對每周的文章每一篇設計2-3題討論題目,以供同學課堂進行討論,加深對主題的了解。
小組期末專題報告 (30%)
運用個案研究,可透過訪談或者二手資料蒐集,書面內容須包含下列各項:
前言
a. 簡述個案背景與問題意識。
b. 解釋為何選擇此個案?以及此個案的特色或價值為何?
c. 希望藉由此個案獲得甚麼?想要回答甚麼問題?
(2)個案介紹
a. 需介紹個案完整的人、事、時、地、物,即為相關的利害關係人或團體是誰?
所發生的創新內容是甚麼?何時發生?為何發生?影響的範圍或地區?
b. 個案內容介紹應具體依照時間順序進行闡述,包括個案發生的背景、發生的
過程以及最後的結果。
c. 個案內容皆須標注資料來源,資料內容的引用可從報章雜誌、期刊論文或是政府相關文件與檔案(法條)等中蒐集獲取;
(3)與理論結合
a. 將個案結合相關理論,例如此個案與參與式治理、公民參與中哪個理論有關?個案與理論所預期的有何異同?以及其可能的解釋因素。
(4)結語:
a. 總結個案發展過程中的價值內涵,並提出對於此個案或是理論的建議。
於課堂上進行簡報,並給予其他同學評論與回饋。
創新的公民參與模式個案介紹 ( 15%) (個人)
根據本學期每周主題,尋找自己有興趣城市或組織所舉辦的公民參與模式,並在指定的周次,在課堂上進行介紹。

title: 地理資訊系統與社會科學 GIS for Social Science
description: This course focuses on the principles of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) as a way of analyzing and understanding society. GIS is a tool to provide geospatial information analysis and display results. Industry-standard GIS software will be used in this course. Students learn the concepts of spatial analysis with GIS; use techniques in importing and creating spatial and attribute data; recognize critical components of cartography to design maps, and build attribute and spatial queries for problem-solving based on spatial relationships. Laboratory exercises incorporate the use of GIS software (ArcGIS) in the analysis of social issues.
objectives: The objectives of the course are to acquaint graduate students with methods to analyze spatially-referenced data with the procedures appropriate for a social science’s theoretical base. The course contact hours are organized into three major foci: (a) essential theoretical concepts and the constituent reference to social science GIS applications; (b) the visualization of social data facilitated by Geographic Information Systems software; and (c) techniques to construct or analyze social point, line, and polygon data using exploratory and confirmatory spatially centered procedures to actual social theories and data using a pedagogical analytical approaches. Weekly readings and homework will emphasize applications of these procedures to actual social theories and data using a pedagogical model of application, interpretation, and presentation of empirical analyses by students. The semester-length project is a key instrument by which students will demonstrate competence in spatial analysis methods covered in the course.
grading:
The final semester grade will be computed as:
10% for the oral presentation of the final project
40% for the final project (3000-5000 words)
15% for the take-home final exam
15% for the assignment (Presentation of the assigned article and the output of the Lab practice)
10% for the classroom discussion
10% for the participation

Identifying Statistical Clusters and Exploratory Spatial Data Analysis (ESDA) of Social Data
Final Project Presentation and Final Exam

title: 行政組織實地研究 Field Research in Administrative Organization
description:
目標:本課程主要提供學生親身參與公部門、私部門、第三部門等組織運作的機會,培養對前述組織相關議題的敏感度,將本系所學理論與組織實務運作進行對話,藉此開拓學生視野。並透過質性研究方法,具系統性地蒐集與分析實證資料,完成學術性研究報告,以增進對公共行政理論與實務的理解與反思。
對象:本課程適合以下各種不同類型的學生選修
對特定議題的研究或特定實務運作有興趣,但無機會透過組織生活實際接觸者。
已在特定組織服務,對於所服務組織的特定問題有興趣進行深入研究者。
對特定組織的實務運作有興趣,並想深入了解及探索者。
內容:針對以上不同類型同學,本課程可協助
提供相關組織實習之機會,或協助安排至合作單位,以完成同學研究議題所需之實地研究機會。
提供研究方法上的協助,以進行特定議題的系統性分析。
機關:實地研究組織之安排由下列方式進行:
同學請自行聯繫機關,並於經授課教師同意後進行。(建議採用!!)
由授課教師在學期初提供機關名額,由同學依興趣及研究需要選擇。
在職同學得利用非上班時間,於「就任職之組織」或選擇「其他組織」進行等同時間之參與觀察,同學可就其任職之組織需求或待解決問題與主管討論後,徵求教師同意,選擇所服務組織之主題進行實地觀察及研究。
時間:進行實地研究時間至少10個工作天,依組織需要及同學選擇,以每週一天(一個全天或兩個半天)為原則,或依機關計畫需要連續10天到機關進行研究。本課程亦可於徵得授課教師書面同意後,利用非學期期間(如:寒、暑假期間等)進行實地研究。實地研究期間教師將至研究機關進行訪視,提供必要之協助與諮詢。
objectives: 目標:本課程主要提供學生親身參與公、私及第三部門組織運作的機會,培養對行政組織相關議題的敏感度,將學習之理論與組織的實務運作進行對話,藉此開拓學生的視野,並透過質性研究方法,系統地蒐集與分析實證資料,完成一學術性研究報告,對公共行政理論與實務進行深入的理解與反思。
grading:
一、機關考核 (20%)
由實習組織輔導員評估同學參與組織業務運作情形,就工作表現、積極主動精神、人際互動等項目情形予以評分。
二、實地日誌(30%)
依研究需要,按照學術格式,撰寫六篇實地研究或參與觀察日誌,於每次實習後一週內以上傳至moodle教學平台指定區域。
三、學期報告(40%)
(一) 報告內容:學期報告介於6,000字與8,000字之間,且應包括但不限於以下各部分:
研究問題的界定:說明你的研究所試圖解答的問題是哪些?對這些問題研究的動機?產生這些問題的背景?以及該等問題為何值得研究(完成後對相關學門具有什麼樣的學術價值?或者在政策上帶來什麼樣的實際貢獻)?研究的範圍是什麼?
文獻回顧:蒐集並回顧前此與預擬研究問題相關之研究,有系統地呈現其發展脈絡,檢閱其優劣或不足之處,並描述當前相關領域研究的缺口,藉此凸顯本研究的重要性。
理論架構或假設(optional):由進行文獻回顧時所接觸到的理論或研究成果,導出本研究之分析方向或初步架構,明確說明架構的主要面向或者假設。
研究設計:根據前此提出的初步方向、架構或假設,設計研究策略或模式,並說明其與前述這些研究方向之關連何在。說明你所選用資料蒐集方法(如次級資料分析、訪談、參與觀察等)的適當性或必要性;並詳述你的資料蒐集步驟:如何選取個案、如何進行選樣、預定分析資料方法、研究者角色的界定、以及研究倫理的處理等。
資料分析與討論:依照本課程所探討的各種質化研究傳統以及不同分析方法,針對參與觀察過程所蒐集之次級資料及原始資料進行分析(必要時得使用電腦軟體),此部分應佔 報告的一半以上。
結論:結論應根據前面的資料分析,包含研究發現、理論或學術意涵(與理論或文獻對話)、實務建議、研究限制與未來研究建議。
(二) 寫作進行方式與時程
於實習之組織進行實地研究起,實習3個工作天或至預計實習期間的四分之一時。需繳交600字研究問題敘述,詳述所選定的研究問題與背景,並附上6篇以上參考文獻出處,並上傳至moodle教學平台指定區域。
於實習之組織進行實地研究起,實習5個工作天或至預計實習期間的二分之一時。需依課程大綱所定時間,繳交所完成之文獻回顧和研究命題(或假設),提交完整實習成果報告計畫初稿,並上傳至moodle教學平台指定區域。
依所定時間於課堂報告實習成果報告內容,報告同學必須於上課前三日之23:59之前,將完整報告送交評論同學及老師。內容應符合學術論文格式,並包括封面頁、目錄、本文、附註、參考書目、附錄等。口頭報告時應準備輔助資料(如:製作簡報),使參與同學能充分了解報告內容。擔任評論的同學亦應於事先完成500字的評論稿,並於報告人完成報告後負責評論。
四、教師考核(10%)
授課教師將依據同學實習日誌登錄情形、課程出席情形、實習出缺勤情形以及上課參與討論情形予以評定成績。

title: 政府公關與政策行銷專題研究 Seminar on Government Public Relations and Public Policy Making
description: 本課程目的為使學生對公共政策形成過程中傳播所扮演的角色,有更深的認識,藉此奠定推動實務上政府公關與行銷的基礎。在理論方面,本課程將由民主理論的規範性觀點開始,探討民主社會公共政策制定過程的現象,再從傳播學、政治學與政策科學中關於議程設定的理論。
objectives: 本課程上半學期理論討論之後,下半學期最重要的學習成效,就是個案報告。本課程將分十個主題探討傳播與公共管理的議題,其中五個政策行銷議題,五個政府公關議題,以學生分組製作「個案報告」(case report)的方式,讓同學可以認識相關理論在實務當中的應用。
grading:
批判報告 (共25%,博生8篇,碩生4篇)
本學期當中,為了確保同學上課的參與,並鼓勵學生對課程內容進行批判性的思索,學生將負責完成一份批判報告。其做法為,在學期中必須選擇四次(碩士生)或八次(博士生)自己喜歡的內容,同時包括理論部份與實務部份,於上課當週,繳交批判文章(referee report),字數1000-2000字(單行間距12號字形約1-2頁)。內容請包括下列三個項目:
主要討論議題
主要論述內容與結論
您個人的評論與看法 (重要!請務必提出)
個案報告(大綱10%; 文本- 期中與期末25%,口頭20%; 共55%)
本學期當中,學生將分組(共分為十組)輪流負責實務單元上課帶領的工作,這工作包括,:

個案報告:請小組依照老師所指定或是學生選定的個案,進行2000字的個案寫作,個案寫作注意事項:

至少訪談一位相關人士,逐字稿整理與應用。
以公部門案例為主,第三部門案例可以接受。
相關資料寫作,作為紙本報告其中主要的個案部分。
理論到實務:連結上課研讀資料與個案報告資料,請小組同學從中萃取上課值得討論的問題三到五題,以1000字左右的篇幅,進行書面討論。

title: 基礎統計學 Introduction to Statistics
description: 本課程分為兩大部分,循序漸進地帶領同學了解統計學的內涵。學期前半將著重在介紹統計學的整體概念,並逐一深入相關主題,包括資料整理、機率論、抽樣分配、估計與信心區間等主題;學期後半段,將著重在提出研究假設之能力培養,同時訓練學生運用各種方法進行假設檢定,包括卡方檢定、t-test、變異數分析、簡單迴歸分析等等。過程中,將配合上機實作與練習等方式,讓同學們具備運用統計軟體達成分析目標之能力。
objectives:
本課程分為兩大部分,循序漸進地帶領同學了解統計學的內涵。學期前半將著重在介紹統計學的整體概念,並逐一深入相關主題,包括資料整理、機率論、抽樣分配、估計與信心區間等主題;學期後半段,將著重在提出研究假設之能力培養,同時訓練學生運用各種方法進行假設檢定,包括卡方檢定、t-test、變異數分析、簡單迴歸分析等等。過程中,將配合上機實作與練習等 方式,讓同學們具備運用統計軟體達成分析目標之能力。
透過本課程之學習,學生將具備運用Excel以及SPSS進行統計分析的能力;除此之外,課程中也將訓練學生閱讀學術文獻中統計分析章節的能力,以便進行批判與反思。學期末,本課程將以實際調查研究個案,讓同學了解統計分析的意義,並藉此熟悉以Excel以及SPSS分析問卷的操作程序。本課程為邁向量化研究方法之基礎課程,修畢之後,將可進一步修習「多變量統計分析」、「調查研究」、「高等量化資料分析」等課程。
grading:
一、課堂參與&導讀:30%
本課程為統計學基礎知識與能力培養之重要課程,課前預習以及積極的課堂參與,將能夠幫助概念的理解與實際運用。
參與 (15%):老師將於學期末綜合評量同學的參與討論程度給分。於課堂中發言、提問及討論,老師將給予加分鼓勵,加分無上限。
導讀 (15%):每位同學將負責一週之主題,向其他同學摘要報告該週之內容。導讀週次及主題,將於開學第一週進行分配。
二、作業:30%
共六次作業,每次作業佔總成績5%,於發佈作業後兩週上課時繳交,遲交以零分計算。
三、期中考:20%
缺考沒有補考。如遇特殊情況無法考試,經老師同意後,期末考佔40%。
四、期末考:20%
如遇特殊情況無法考試,須與老師討論補救辦法,透過補救辦法獲得之成績以八折計算。
本課程授課老師將安排6小時自主學習課程進度,進行方式將於學期課堂說明

title: 多變量統計分析 Multivariate Statistical Analysis
description:
以量化研究與基礎統計學為基礎,如本系「碩博班統計課程進階」與「統計基礎概念自評問卷」(請於首堂課前自評),本課程在使同學具備公共行政與政策專業中多變量(multivariate,亦即至少三個變項)統計分析知識與技能,包括(含類別資料的邏輯斯 logistic)多元迴歸分析(multiple regression)分析、因素分析(factor analysis)與集群分析(cluster analysis),最後以資料探勘(data mining)作為資料科學(data science,如圖)進階準備。
學習過程將以統計分析軟體/程式語言(JASP 與 Python,皆為開源軟體)實作以上的多變量方法,其中 JASP(如同 SPSS 政大雲端版)有較為友善的使用介面;而作為機器學習時代的主流程式語言之一,Python 則具備豐富的網路自學資源與客製彈性的優勢。本課程將搭配採用以使同學更能具備學術與實務的發展潛力,尤其運算思維(computational thinking)與程式設計能力已逐漸成為跨領域學習的必備素養與技能(公行系碩班114-1學期課程表)。
另外,鑑於生成式人工智慧(generative artificial intelligence, GenAI)工具的普及(如 ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini、Perplexity 等),本課程也將盡力善用,例如自主學習特定多變量方法、產出或偵錯 Python 程式碼,包括新興的程式設計理念與工具介面(例如 vibe coding)。
最後,搭配這些多變量統計分析方法,同學也將研讀量化研究論文以瞭解如何實際應用於公共行政與政策研究議題,並以原始或次級量化資料(如中研院學術調查研究資料庫、數位治理研究中心等)撰寫學期報告,藉以培養同學評論及撰寫量化論文的品味與能力(氣質),也同步連結本系碩博班要求的學術發表與學位論文。
grading:
預習或複習作業 40 %
學期報告 40%
學期考試 10%
缺曠、自主學習參與(課堂或數位平台的提問、回應與主動分享)10%

title: 土地開發法制專題討論 Special Topics in Land Development Law
description: 本課程主要在協助碩博士班同學了解土地資源之利用與管理法制,包括土地開發各個階段行政程序的相關法律規範,包括環境資源的合理利用、土地利用計畫,到包括土地開發的用地取得手段,主要集中在土地重劃及土地徵收等工具。並針對台灣既有行政實務及司法實務的現況,輔以不同國家立法例,就土地開發之個案與土地開發法制做討論與分析。
objectives:
本課程主要訓練修課同學具有以下能力,並透過以下評量工具進行檢核教學及學習成效:
1.了解及適用土地開發法規之能力:透過閱讀文獻的報告、透過專題研究報告、課堂討論進行評量
2.可得出解決土地開發專業問題方案之能力:透過透過專題研究報告、課堂討論進行評量
3.個案操作時知悉土地規劃及用地取得與應用能力:透過閱讀文獻的報告、透過專題研究報告、課堂討論進行評量
4.具備邏輯思考及推理之能力:透過透過專題研究報告、課堂討論進行評量
grading:
本學期評量主要針對「文獻整理及引導討論」、「學期專題報告」及「討論與論述」三項,分別依下列項目進行評分。
項目 | 題目設定與執行方案之規劃 30% | 文獻與數據佐證 30% | 結果討論 20% | 簡報呈現 20%
優 | 議題設定能引起迴響 題目與報告內容契合 行動方案具體可行 | 提出相關支持論述 佐證文獻引用具體適當,並有大量引用 佐證案例引用適當,說明及論理得宜 | 資料蒐集完整.分析精確.討論深入層次分明. | 文字圖表大小顯示效果優良,呈現效果吸引聽眾注意 報告口條可有效吸引聽眾目光
佳 | 議題設定有趣 行動方案規劃得宜 | 提出相關支持論述,並未有充分論理 佐證文獻引用適當,但未有充分說明及論理 | 資料蒐集與分析尚可,討論大致都有提到 | 文字圖表大小顯示效果良好,呈現效果佳 報告口條讓聽眾可以了解
普通 | 議題設定引不起興趣 行動方案規劃不夠完 整 | 提出相關支持論述 佐證文獻引用具體 | 資料蒐集缺漏,分析稍有錯誤,討論深度不足 | 文字圖表大小顯示效果差,呈現效果普通 報告口條無法吸引聽眾
待改進 | 議題設定無趣行動方案規劃不可行 | 相關支持論述 有佐證文獻引用 案例援用不當 | 資料蒐集缺漏分析錯誤,幾乎沒有延伸討論 | 文意不明 論述沒重點、不符合邏輯 報告看稿照唸

title: 環境數值模擬與災害潛勢分析 Environmental Numerical Modeling and Hazard Potential Assessment
description: 極端降雨與複合型災害日益頻繁的背景下,水災、坡地崩塌與土砂運移等環境現象已成為國土環境風險的重要來源。本課程以「環境數值模擬」為核心,帶領土地資訊與測量組學生建立從物理機制到空間化成果的完整能力鏈:理解水文與土砂運移等基本過程、掌握模型所需之輸入資料(如 DEM、土地覆蓋、土壤/地質、降雨歷線等)與前處理方法、學習模型參數與邊界條件設定,並透過校驗、敏感度分析與不確定性表達,判讀模擬結果的可信度與適用範圍。課程將以淹水範圍、水深/流速、沖刷與堆積熱區、土石流可能路徑與影響範圍等為主要輸出,進一步轉換為可在 GIS 中整合之災害潛勢圖資與指標,並示範其在都市與國土相關工作中的支援角色,例如:潛在熱區辨識、基礎設施與聚落暴露度盤點、不同情境下風險差異比較,以及跨領域溝通所需的技術性說明。整體目標在於培養學生具備「理解模型—產出圖資—解讀限制」的專業素養,使其能以一致且可檢核的量化方法支撐環境風險之空間分析與應用。
objectives:
本課程將介紹都會與山區天災類型與風險評估、數值地形於災害判釋原則與防災韌性與國土調適策略。課程將學習以遙測圖資及GIS工具產製災害潛勢圖之基本原則、圖資來源與分析方法等,支援都市與國土防災相關應用之技術溝通:能以技術語言清楚說明潛勢成果、資料需求與限制,並示範與土地利用、建物、基礎設施等資料的疊合與暴露度盤點方法。
課程中亦將教授災害數值模擬核心概念,包含理解環境數值模擬之基本概念、控制方程與主要假設,說明模型適用尺度與限制條件。同時學習掌握輸入資料與前處理流程,具備整備 DEM圖資分析、土地使用、降雨歷線、土壤/地質等關鍵資料之能力,理解資料品質對模擬結果的影響。完成基本建模與情境設定建立可重複之模擬流程,並進行多情境(現況/極端/假設情境)比較。透過判讀結果可信度:能執行校驗與敏感度分析,辨識誤差來源,並以合理方式呈現不確定性與結果解讀界線。最終產製不同災害類型之潛勢圖資與指標:將模擬輸出轉換為 GIS 可用的潛勢圖層與空間指標(如土砂災害範圍、沖刷堆積熱區、影響熱區等),建構國土防災與空間分析基礎情資之能力。
grading:
每周實作作業與練習:20%(DEM處理、資料整備、模擬操作、GIS圖資產製等分項作業)。
期中報告(個人書面):30%(RAMMS數值模擬與分析資料報告)
期末專題報告(分組書面與發表):50%(災害議題選定與災害潛勢圖資評估成果)

title: 土地法專題研究 Case Study of Land Law
description: 以專題講授、課堂報告與討論之方式,使履修者瞭解土地法相關理論、研究課題及研究方法,強化法學基礎,並思考、分析、探索我國現行土地法相關議題之論點、問題及其立法論上應有之取向。
objectives: 使履修者瞭解土地法相關理論、研究課題及研究方法,並分析、探索我國現行土地法制於解釋論或立法論上之議題,藉此以培養學生對於土地法律議題之思考與研究分析能力。

title: 毀滅與新生—二次大戰後德國都市、鄉村及其建築的重構 Destruction and Reborn – the New Developments of German Urbanplan and Architecture after WWII
description:
本課程為短期國外移地教學,預計於115年8月中下旬辦理。
鑒於德國是第二次世界大戰期間被摧毀最嚴重地區,且歷經冷戰時期之分裂,在二戰後重建迄於統一後,表現出極度多元的都市規劃與建築設計思維,往往在極小空間範圍中,高度集中典範等級之規劃與設計案例。固本次教學行程規劃,精選由都市到鄉村、由古蹟維護到新建綠建築的典範及案例,分別位於柏林、呂布腦、德勒斯登、林茲、雷根斯堡與加米許-帕登基爾許的都市規劃與建築案例。藉此希望同學可以由其中了解現代都市、鄉村規劃與建築間整體思考的重要性與創意。
objectives:
1. 參訪、觀察樣區及個案在空間規劃與建築上的特殊考量之處,並練習結合地圖做成觀察紀錄。思考城鎮規劃如何與建築管理互相結合。
2. 拜訪相關機關,了解德國、奧地利在制度面向與台灣不同之處。思考這導致台灣與德奧在執行土地使用管制與建築管理時,所形成的差異。
3. 學習辨識歐洲不同時期建築風格及其時代背景,並觀察如何在發展現代都市機能之同時,維護大量文物古蹟以及自古流傳的街道布局。
4. 觀察農村生活模式與經濟產業間的關聯,以及歐盟主導下歐洲山村的治理邏輯。反思在台灣如何處理山村所面臨各種課題。
grading:
教師於出國前開列應觀察、學習之重點,回國後由參與同學針對所列出應觀察、學習重點繳交學習報告。
1. 樣區地圖記錄
2. 觀察分析

title: 住宅研究與資料科學 Data Science for Housing Research
description: 本課程為學士班高年級與碩士班合開課程,將從住宅供、需、價、量不同層面,探討現今住宅問題與相關研究,並特別著重在當前社會住宅政策與過去較少關注的租賃市場,課程亦將安排實地參訪社會住宅或老人住宅。且因應循證研究需求,將在課程中帶領同學運用程式語言及統計分析工具,建立資料分析思維與初階分析能力。
objectives:
希望同學修習之後,能達到以下學習成效:
能學會基本的統計分析工具及資料庫查詢語言,撰寫以「描述統計」為基礎之住宅政策分析報告,包含背景說明、重要發現、重要發現彙整等。
使學生對住宅相關研究有初階理解,能辨識問題,運用循證政策分析,解讀資料數據意涵。
grading:
1.出席及課堂討論 30%
同學應出席課堂與參訪活動,以確保良好學習狀況。(不定期點名3次)
2.書面作業 20%
給分標準(分成A+、A、B、C、D等級)
A+:優良(問題回答完整、清晰、有條理,有充分資料支持結論,心得或個人觀點言之有理且豐富)
A:佳(問題回答完整,內容大致正確,有心得或個人觀點)
B:普通(問題回答雖完整,但缺乏結論、心得或個人觀點)
C:待改進(問題回答過於簡略)
D:抄襲
3.分組報告 50%
一、口語表達與台風:(40%)
報告同學台風是否穩健? 報告流程是否順暢? 時間掌握是否妥適?
二、報告內容正確性:(40%)
報告內容與主題連結度?報告內容邏輯嚴謹度?資料引用?實例分析(是否能提出貼切豐富實例,協助聽眾理解)?
三、創意呈現:(20%)
進行小組報告不要僅呈現文字或唸稿,希望多用圖表、短片,報告時甚至可納入短劇、辯論等創意呈現方式。

title: 國際間財產利用 International Property Use
description:
本課程以老師於中央與地方、地政與財政工作經歷,將學術融合於法令實務,就以下課題授課:土地法、國有財產法及土地政策下公部門財產管理、地方與中央政府公產管理及案例研究、公有財產租約及使用管理、國有及北市地上權制度及案例探討、國內外促參案例、公有財產宿舍管理及案例研究、世大運場館利用。並就老師公務拜訪美國、荷蘭、英國、日本、澳洲、德國、義大利、中國等國家心得分享,整理有趣的議題與同學討論。不動產估價師考試土地利用與本課程之關聯,亦將觸及以利同學考用合一。
Based on practical experience working for central and local government covering land and finance administration, academic ideas will blend into the regulation and practice, share the following topics:
Public sector property asset management based on the Land Act and Land policy
Central/Local government public property management with case study
Public property dormitory management with case study
National non-public property lease and use management
National and Taipei city non-public property superficies management with case study
Public and Private Participation in Infrastructure Projects in Taiwan
Taipei Summer Universiade venues use
Besides, some countries including US, Netherlands, UK, Japan, Australia, Germany, China etc, which lecturer once visited for official purposes before, will come up interesting issues and discuss with participants. Land use application in Real estate appraiser exam will be touched as well.

2. 教導同學國內外財產利用規範Provide students with knowledge about property Use in terms of regulatory perspective both domestically and internationally.
3. 灌輸財產利用學術研究文章Instill students with ideas about property use policy in terms of academic perspective.
4. 指導同學發表國際財產利用論文Guide participants to do research and write paper potentially for publication.
5.輔導同學如何考上不動產估價師並將土地利用導入估價作業Guide participants how to become eligible for real estate appraiser and application of land use into appraisal practice

title: 不動產市場計量經濟分析 Applied Econometric Analysis of Real Estate Market
description: This course applies statistical methods and economic theory to identify, estimate, and test economic models within the real estate market. This course covers concepts and techniques relevant to the empirical analysis of the real estate market. Emphasizing practical applications, the course includes topics such as the classical single-equation regression model, multiple regression models, and models with discrete or categorical dependent variables. Throughout the lectures, we will explore numerous empirical examples using diverse datasets, focusing on real-world data and appropriate models. The course integrates theory with practical exercises, encouraging students to participate actively and complete readings in advance. We will also use the SAS software to tackle empirical exercises and assignments.
objectives:
Students will learn to conduct econometric analysis and critically evaluate empirical studies on the real estate market. This course aims to build your confidence in estimating and interpreting econometric models. Upon successful completion, students will be able to:
1. Gather and process real estate data.
2. Specify an appropriate economic model for real estate.
3. Utilize econometric software to estimate the economic model.
4. Evaluate the estimated results of the model.
5. Interpret the estimation output and make inferences.
6. Generate forecasts based on the estimated model.
grading:

1. Class Participation: 20%
2. In-Class Exercises & Homework: 30%
3. Empirical Research Project (Group Report): 50%

(1) If it is determined that AI was used without proper disclosure in the report, the instructor reserves the right to re-evaluate and re-grade the submission.
(2) The APA citation format could be followed.
(3) Please adhere to the university’s principles regarding the use of generative AI: “National Chengchi University Brief Principles for Generative AI”, https://sites.google.com/g.nccu.edu.tw/nccubasicprincipleforai
4. When writing your report, it is essential to showcase your own ideas and creativity. The content should reflect your ability to think critically, analyze information, and make informed judgments. In the age of AI, students should develop the skills to evaluate, construct, reorganize, and critically assess knowledge.

title: 空間決策 Spatial Decision Making
description:
TL;DR. Learn how to make smarter, evidence‐based decisions about real‐world spatial problems.
We start with core decision‐making tools, then dive into GIS, spatial analysis, and machine learning to tackle challenges like planning infrastructure, mapping hazards, and shaping land‐use policy. By the end, we will be able to design, run, and evaluate powerful spatial decision workflows from the ground up.
Long Version.
How can we make better decisions about places, spaces, and the world around us?
This course explores the tools and approaches that help answer that question.
It begins with the basics of decision-making — breaking down complex choices into manageable steps and comparing options in a structured way. Core methods such as multi‐criteria analysis, weighting techniques, and simple statistical models provide a foundation for understanding robust decision processes.
During the second half of the semester, the focus then shifts to spatial problems — those that involve geography and location. Using Geographic Information Systems (GIS), the class works through real-world challenges including site selection, infrastructure planning, hazard zone mapping, and land-use policy evaluation. Hands-on labs demonstrate how Spatial Decision Support Systems (SDSS) are designed, adapted, and assessed for different decision contexts.
The course introduces machine learning approaches — including decision trees, logistic regression, and clustering — to identify patterns in decision-making. Spatial machine learning models and feature ranking strategies add a leading‐edge complement to traditional analysis.
By the end of the semester, we will have the skills to:
Apply GIS and integrated tools to address spatial decision problems,
Design and implement complete decision‐making workflows,
Evaluate the robustness and reliability of decision processes.
Relevant to fields such as urban planning, environmental analysis, disaster management, and policy design, the course equips students with a practical toolkit for evidence‐based spatial decision making.
objectives:
Course Goals
This course aims to:
Explore key theories, methods, and tools for spatial decision making.
Examine case studies from the literature to highlight successful applications and common challenges.
Provide hands‐on experience in the design, implementation, and evaluation of spatial decision workflows.
Integrate Geographic Information Systems (GIS), statistical methods, and machine learning techniques to support evidence‐based decisions.
Learning Outcomes
By the end of the course, we will be able to:
Identify and critically assess existing spatial decision-making projects from academic and applied contexts.
Select and adapt appropriate approaches for a given decision problem.
Collect, prepare, and model spatial and non‐spatial data for analysis.
Design and implement a complete spatial decision workflow, from problem definition to outcome evaluation.
Apply GIS software and integrated modelling tools to create a targeted decision-making system from scratch.
Incorporate statistical and machine learning methods to analyse patterns and improve decision outcomes.
Evaluate the robustness and reliability of conclusions based on multiple criteria, variables, and uncertainty considerations.
grading:
This course has a midterm and a final exam.
Homework assignments and bonus exercises will help to consolidate the obtained knowledge.
The midterm examination will be a portfolio of online questions and/or a project covering the theoretical foundations.
The final exam will be a project. In order to complete the final project successfully, students will set up a spatial decision-making project, and produce a workflow with evaluation criteria.

description:

objectives:
本課程的主要目標為教授學生如何進行符合邏輯的學術研究。修課學生將各自選定與空間資訊(Geomatics)領域相關之研究主題,透過授課教師個別指導與建議,期望能完成空間資訊領域研究,並參與相關國內外研討會發表。

title: 測量平差法特論 Special Topics in Adjustment Computation
description: 本課程除回顧慣用的間接觀測平差之外,亦深入介紹條件觀測平差與混合模式平差,並介紹可靠度與偵測的理論以及若干平差模式之拓展,藉由理論介紹與軟體操作和程式撰寫讓學生更深入了解測量平差之理論。
objectives:
使學生了解
(1) 誤差基本理論:包括測量誤差及其分類、偶然誤差的統計特性、精度及表示方法、權的定義及定權的方法、方差-協方差誤差傳播規律與應用。
(2) 測量平差函數模型和隨機模型的概念及建立,參數估計理論及最小二乘原理。
(3) 測量平差基本方法:使用的函數模型主要為直接觀測平差、間接觀測平差、條件觀測平差和併存型平差。測量平差中必要的誤差橢圓、統計檢定、粗差偵測等。
(4) 測量平差的實務應用:主要為坐標轉換、水準網平差、角邊的控制網平差、電子測距儀的檢定、GPS網形平差及其他如在數值攝影測量、影像處理的應用。
(5) 近代測量平差理論和方法:如自由網平差、最小二乘配置平差、序慣平差、大型平差系統的分割解法等。
讓學生可以學到可以以測量平差方式解決、分析、評估測量上所遭遇之解算問題,進而啟發其創意發展新方法解決未來所遭遇之任何測量所遭遇之解算問題,達到研究生獨立研究的能力。

title: 經濟計量學 Econometrics
description:
This first-year economics course aims to teach econometric principles and methods. It begins with matrix algebra as a fundamental tool for handling economic data, followed by least squares and normal regression to establish the basis for regression analysis.
The course then explores heteroskedasticity, time series, and panel data. Additionally, this course aims to cover maximum likelihood estimation and quantile regression, depending on time availability. The course emphasizes real-world applications to prepare students for empirical research.

title: 進階個體經濟分析 Advanced Microeconomics Analysis
description:
本課程為經濟學系博士班第一學年之核心必修課程《進階個體經濟分析》。本課程旨在為博士生奠定嚴謹、紮實且具前沿研究視野的個體經濟理論基礎,訓練學生具備高級個體理論之數學推導能力與經濟直覺,為後續之學術研究與資格考試(Qualifying Examination)做準備。
本課程以全球博士班通用之權威教材 Mas-Colell, Whinston, and Green (MWG) Microeconomic Theory 為主要授課架構,全學期分為三大核心模組:
個體決策與對偶理論(Individual Decision Theory & Duality):從偏好公理與效用表徵出發,系統化建立效用極大化問題(UMP)與支出極小化問題(EMP)之對偶關係(Duality),導出包絡線定理(Envelope Theorem)、Slutsky 方程式、顯示偏好理論,以及不確定性下的期望效用與風險趨避(vNM Expected Utility & Risk Aversion)。
非合作賽局理論(Non-Cooperative Game Theory):涵蓋完整資訊靜態賽局(純策略與混合策略 Nash 均衡)、動態展開型賽局(子賽局精鍊 Nash 均衡, SPE)及其在市場競爭模型中的應用。
一般均衡與福利經濟學(General Equilibrium Theory & Welfare Economics):從 2×2 經濟體(Edgeworth Box)與生產經濟切入,探討市場結清機制與帕累托最適(Pareto Optimality);嚴謹推導福利經濟學第一與第二定理(FWT & SWT),並透過 Kakutani 不動點定理簡介競爭均衡解的存在性(Existence of Competitive Equilibrium)。
本課程重視數學邏輯之嚴密性,每週均設有需進行嚴謹數學證明之作業(Problem Sets),引導學生將理論模型內化為自身的研究工具。
objectives:
本課程為經濟學系博士班核心必修課,以權威教材 Mas-Colell, Whinston, and Green (MWG) 為主軸,旨在培育學生具備嚴謹的個體經濟理論推導、數學建模技巧與經濟直覺,為後續獨立研究奠定堅實基礎。
修畢本課程後,學生將全面掌握個體經濟學的三大理論核心:首先是「個體決策與對偶分析」,能熟練處理消費者與生產者之最適化問題及不確定性下的經濟行為;其次為「非合作賽局理論」,具備靜態與動態賽局之建模與求解能力;最後是「一般均衡與福利經濟學」,能嚴謹證明市場效率定理並理解競爭均衡之數學基礎。最終,學生將具備獨立撰寫嚴密數學證明(Formal Proofs)與研讀當代頂尖經濟學期刊論文之核心實力。
grading:
課後作業 (30%):全學期 6 次作業,評估數學推導與模型求解之嚴謹度。
期中考試 (35%):第 8 週隨堂筆試(範圍:第 1–7 週),評估個體基礎觀念與推導能力。
期末考試 (35%):第 16 週隨堂筆試(全學期綜合測驗),評估理論整合與高級證明能力。

title: 進階總體經濟分析 Advanced Macroeconomics Analysis
description:
Course Introduction: Macroeconomics from the Bottom Up — Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) and Generative ABM (G-ABM) in the Age of Big Data, LLMs, and Agentic AI
1. Why Agent-Based Modeling in Macroeconomics?
In today’s interconnected and data-rich world, understanding the macroeconomy requires more than aggregate equations and representative agents. Agent-based modeling (ABM) offers a complementary, bottom-up perspective, treating the economy as a complex, evolving system of heterogeneous, interacting agents—each endowed with rules, learning capabilities, and adaptive behaviors. In this sense, ABM is not only a method for studying the economy; it is itself a form of artificial intelligence in action—a laboratory where autonomous agents sense, decide, learn, and adapt within dynamic environments. By making AI an inherent part of the model rather than a detached analytical tool, ABM allows us to explore how intelligence—human or artificial—shapes macroeconomic outcomes. This approach equips students with computational tools and conceptual insights to navigate the complexity, uncertainty, and adaptive nature of real-world economies, preparing them for a future in which AI and macroeconomics are increasingly inseparable.
2. Macroeconomics in the Context of the Science of Complexity
It is in this spirit that I invite you to join me on a journey I have personally taken—into the world of complexity science, and with it, a new way of rethinking macroeconomic phenomena from the bottom up. In the late 20th century, a fresh paradigm took root in the study of complex systems: agent-based modeling. This method constructs macro patterns from the ground up, through the interactions of diverse, autonomous agents. Over the course of fourteen lectures, we will examine ABM not only as a powerful tool for economic and financial simulation, but also as a vessel for deeply interdisciplinary ideas, drawing inspiration from physics, biology, sociology, and computer science. These concepts will be set against the backdrop of the history of economic thought and the evolution of the modern economy (Week One).
3. EBM versus ABM: From Equationization to Agentization
Building on this foundation, the second half of the course (Weeks Eleven–Sixteen) will focus on agentization—the process of transforming traditional Equation-Based Models (EBMs) into Agent-Based Models (ABMs). As discussed in my recent work (Chen, 2025), EBMs, rooted in the Newtonian tradition of equation-based mathematics, portray economies through aggregated, often centralized, relationships. ABMs, by contrast, replace these aggregates with populations of heterogeneous, interacting agents, allowing micro-level diversity, adaptation, and social interaction to drive emergent macro patterns. While ABMs can be inspired by EBM prototypes—such as asset pricing models (Weeks Fifteen–Sixteen), overlapping generations models (Week Fourteen), or epidemic equations (Week Eleven)—they are not merely numerical approximations of those equations. Instead, they open an independent window into dynamics that EBMs cannot capture: path dependence, out-of-equilibrium processes, network effects, and behavioral diversity. In the current AI era, this shift is more than methodological; it represents a change in the very language of modeling—from solving fixed equations to simulating evolving intelligences. By “agentizing” macroeconomic models, we integrate the logic of artificial intelligence directly into our economic representations, making the study of macroeconomics more attuned to a world where economies themselves are increasingly shaped by adaptive, algorithmic agents.
4. ABM as a Tool for Policy and Market Design
From a practical standpoint, one of the most distinctive strengths of ABM lies in its application to policy and mechanism (market) design—particularly in environments where data are scarce and uncertainty is high, including the realm of unknown unknowns. ABM allows us to experiment with institutional rules, incentive structures, and policy interventions in silico, observing how different designs play out in complex, adaptive systems before they are implemented in reality. We will return to this theme in Week Twelve, where a concrete case study will illustrate how ABM can serve as a decision-making compass when conventional analytical tools falter.
5. Two Canonical Forms of ABM
You will also be introduced to two canonical forms of ABM: Cellular Automata (CA) – Models where the focus is on simulating local interactions on a grid or network, often producing striking macro patterns from simple rules. Evolutionary Computation (EC) – Models that embed variation, selection, and adaptation, often applied to optimization and evolving systems. Historically, the ABM literature began with CA-ABM, but came into full bloom with EC-ABM. In Week Eight, we will trace this evolution and formally introduce social networks as a bridge between micro-level rules and macro-level patterns. These two kinds of ABM differ in their original scientific ambitions: CA-ABM arose from the quest to simulate the very essence of life—pioneered by John von Neumann (1903–1957) in his work on self-reproducing automata (von Neumann, 1966). We will study this in Weeks Two and Three. EC-ABM grew from the ambition to simulate evolution—not just biological evolution, but adaptation across the entire universe. This allows us to view economies as evolving systems, a topic we will explore in Weeks Eleven and Twelve.
6. Evolution, Co-Evolution, and Multi-Level Dynamics
While CA-ABM can simulate evolution, it tends to do so at a single, macro level. EC-ABM, by contrast, can model co-evolution across multiple levels—a hallmark of complex adaptive systems. This multi-level perspective is central to Neo-Darwinism and has influenced both complexity theory and evolutionary economics (Simon, 1962; op Akkerhuis, 2016; Foster & Metcalfe, 2001). Modeling such intertwined processes would be daunting, if not impossible, without ABM.
7. ABM and the Economics of Social Epidemics
Together, CA-ABM and EC-ABM provide foundational lenses for interpreting macroeconomic dynamics as social epidemics—the spread of ideas, behaviors, and expectations through populations. This framing, popularized by Robert Shiller in Narrative Economics (2019), will be introduced in Weeks Seven and Nine, and revisited repeatedly thereafter to link micro-level agent interactions with macro-level shifts in beliefs and markets.
8. Rules as the True Building Blocks
Beneath the agents themselves lie the rules—codes, genes, neurons, and programs—that drive behavior. Rules can be: Ascribed – fixed from the start; Acquired – learned and adapted through experience. The latter connects directly to bounded rationality, but ABM broadens the scope beyond traditional economics by drawing on biology, psychology, computer science, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. This convergence—covered in Weeks Seven, Ten, Twelve, Thirteen and beyond—allows us to model agents who are not only reactive, but adaptive, innovative, and capable of altering the very rules by which they operate.
9. ABM as a Foundation for Big Data and AI-Era Macroeconomics
In one station of the journey, we will turn to the interplay between big data and agent-based modeling (Week Four), drawing on the perspective of Chen and Venkatachalam (2017). Their work frames ABM not merely as a beneficiary of big data, but as its methodological foundation—a way to structure, interpret, and simulate the vast, high-dimensional, and often unstructured information that modern economies generate. In macroeconomics, this connection is especially powerful: big data offers unprecedented real-time signals about consumption, production, employment, and sentiment, yet without a coherent framework, such signals can be overwhelming or even misleading. ABM provides that framework by embedding data into dynamic, micro-founded simulations, allowing us to test how observed patterns might evolve under alternative policies or shocks. This approach is particularly valuable in the AI era, when machine learning algorithms can extract patterns from massive datasets but often lack an explicit causal or structural economic interpretation. ABM bridges that gap: it can integrate AI’s predictive strengths with an explicit, behavior-based model of the economy, enabling us to run what-if scenarios, explore counterfactuals, and design policies with an understanding of underlying mechanisms—not just correlations. In this way, learning macroeconomics through ABM prepares students to work fluently at the intersection of data-rich AI analytics and structural economic reasoning, a skill set increasingly essential for economists in research, policy, and industry.
References
Chen, S. H. (2025). Economic Simulations in Swarm: 20 Years On. New Mathematics and Natural Computation, forthcoming. https://doi.org/10.1142/S1793005726500572
Chen, S. H., & Venkatachalam, R. (2017). Agent-based modelling as a foundation for big data. Journal of Economic Methodology, 24(4), 362-383.
Foster, John, and J. Stanley Metcalfe, eds. Frontiers of evolutionary economics: competition, self-organization, and innovation policy. Edward Elgar Publishing, 2001.
op Akkerhuis, Gerard AJM Jagers, ed. Evolution and transitions in complexity: the science of hierarchical organization in nature. Springer, 2016.
Shiller, Robert J. Narrative economics: How stories go viral and drive major economic events. Princeton University Press, 2019.
Simon, Herbert. "The Architecture of Complexity." Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society 106, no. 6 (1962): 467-482.
Von Neumann, John. Theory of self-reproducing automata. Urbana: University of Illinois Press, 1966.
objectives:
Course Objectives
This course invites students to see macroeconomics from the bottom up—through the lens of complexity science, agent-based modeling (ABM), and the new realities of the AI era. ABM will be presented not merely as a simulation technique, but as a modeling language in which the economy is represented as a population of adaptive, heterogeneous, and interacting agents. In contrast to traditional Equation-Based Models (EBMs), ABM allows for emergent macro patterns shaped by micro-level diversity, network structures, and dynamic adaptation. By the end of the course, students will understand how ABM can serve as both an analytical tool and a conceptual bridge between economics, artificial intelligence, and the broader sciences of complexity.
Learning Outcomes
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Explain the fundamental concepts, historical roots, and interdisciplinary scope of ABM within complexity science.
2. 3Develop a decentralized mindset—in contrast to the traditional centralized approach—enabling them to think and model macro phenomena from the bottom up, as exemplified in agent-based analyses of markets.
3. Distinguish clearly between the logic and limitations of EBMs and the flexibility of ABMs, and recognize their complementary rather than competitive nature.
4. Creatively integrate ABM and EBM within unified research frameworks to address macroeconomic issues, drawing on examples from asset pricing, overlapping generations, and epidemic models.
5. Use two canonical forms of ABM—cellular automata and evolutionary computation—to simulate social interactions, evolutionary processes, and macroeconomic dynamics.
6. Apply ABM to represent adaptive, learning, and algorithmic agents, linking economic modeling to the core principles of AI, including machine learning, evolutionary search, and distributed intelligence.
7. Investigate how ABM enables the study of out-of-equilibrium processes, path dependence, and network effects that are difficult or impossible to capture with EBMs.
8. Evaluate the role of ABM in policy simulation and mechanism design, particularly in contexts with limited data, high uncertainty, or the need to anticipate adaptive agent responses.
9. Integrate skills from econometrics, big data analytics, and experimental economics (laboratory with human subjects) into ABM–EBM hybrid approaches for richer macroeconomic insights.
10. Communicate ABM design, results, and policy implications effectively, demonstrating both technical proficiency and critical, interdisciplinary thinking.
grading:
The course will be taught in English. The course will proceed in lectures. All lectures are prepared in power points, and the students can get these power points before or after the classes. Students are encouraged to interact with the instructor outside the classes. The students have to read the materials in advance. The lecture will only highlight the ppt. During the class, the students are invited to ask questions based on their readings of the preparatory materials and are also required to answer questions posed to them by the instructor. 40% of the score will be based on the in-class interacting performance of the student. The evaluation of the student performance will be based on the final exam (60%), and in-class interactions (40%).
In this course, your final grade will be determined through an oral examination. You will first make an appointment with me to arrange the exam time. The length of the oral exam will depend on how our exchange unfolds. If, during the conversation, it becomes clear that you are performing very well, I may challenge you with more advanced questions to see if you can reach an even higher level—like climbing to a higher peak. On the other hand, if it becomes apparent that you are struggling, we will not prolong the session unnecessarily, and the exam may end sooner. In either case, the goal is to assess your true potential in a fair and efficient way. Your performance in this exam will determine your final grade. If you are not satisfied with your result after the first attempt, you are welcome to schedule a second oral exam, following the same format.

title: 管理經濟學(一) Managerial Economics(I)
description: 管理是ㄧ門真正的博雅藝術( Management is a truly liberal art. );在公共部門,它被稱之為『公共行政管理』;在私人企業,它被稱之為『企業管理』。在互動(Interdependence)關係越來越密切的數位經濟裡,管理經濟學(Managerial Economics)是介紹與探討家計(含個人)、廠商(企業)、政府決策官員及非營利組織執行長如何利用經濟理論與分析方法來有效地做好決策、指揮及監督管理(或管制)的一門社會科學;本質上,它是一門應用經濟學或決策行為科學(Decision Science)。
objectives:
課程主要內容與目標包含:
1.介紹各主題的既有經濟理論;
2.應用既有理論到日常生活與企業各類決策行為個案;
3.透過近期時事的觀察尋找或探討具學術價值的研究主題;
4.針對上述研究主題,嘗試引導學生具備能力建立理論與/或實證模型,進而透過數學與/或統計軟體演繹推導與/或歸納、驗証,並能有效詮釋(解讀)上述推演/或歸納結果。
PS.
傳統完美的管理經濟學研究方法論:
●1.根據研究主題的背景及行爲特性,設定假設後,建立理論(數學)模型。
○2.透過數學軟體推導(演藝)得出推論(結果)。
●3.針對推論(結果)進行詮釋,再檢視合理性或是否合乎直覺(常理)?若為否定,則再修改1.,重複2.⋯⋯,直至滿意爲止。
●4.根據上述滿意推導結果,参考既有文獻與/或實務共識,建立實證模型。
◎5.蒐集實證模型所需資料,反覆進行迴歸估計,直至滿意為止;針對迴歸估計結果進行詮釋 (解讀)。
6.根據上述詮釋結果,先歸納研究結論;再做策略與/或政策性及未來研究建議。
☆隨著科技進步,數學推導與迴歸估計軟體越來越普及、精緻,上述步驟2與5就比較節省時間及人力。
grading:
原則上,期中與期末考試佔80%;課堂討論表現佔20%;
期末考成績若較期中考的顯著進步,會依進步幅度將期末成績比重拉高。

title: 應用個體計量與R語言 Applied Microeconometrics with R
description:
The purpose of this course is to provide an introduction to modern econometric methods commonly used in applied economics, with an emphasis on microeconometric issues based on cross-sectional and panel data.
We will discuss linear regression, instrumental variables, robust and resampling-based inference, discrete choice analysis, panel data models, and causal inference methods.
Rigor and understanding of empirical methods and techniques are emphasized as opposed to learning cookbook methods. Often our focus is on hand-coding the econometric methods to understandard how they work.
We will use a computer program R to gain hands-on experience with working with real data and statistical/econometric programming.
The prerequisite for the course is introductory econometrics and statistics. Having elementary programming skills is assumed.
grading:
Class participation (10%)
Problem sets (20%)
Empirical research proposal (20%)
Midterm presentation (20%)
Empirical research paper (30%)
weeklyText:

Expected hours of study are 8 hours per week (including 3-hour lectures).

Problem sets
The problem sets will include both problem solving and computer tasks. The assignments will be reviewed in class if necessary.
You are encouraged to form a study group with your classmates, but you must write up your own answers. Problem sets with identical answers will NOT be accepted.
Group empirical research project (with 3-4 students per group)
There will be a group project on empirical research, aiming to provide students with experience in applying the statistical and econometric methods examined in the course.
The task is to take a published article of interest, replicate its numerical results, and then extend the analysis in some way. Possible extensions include different data and modifications of model specification.
The empirical research paper will be evaluated with respect to clarity of exposition, thoroughness of description of the data and methods, competence in using the methods, and thoughtfulness in interpreting results. Complexity of economic theory and econometric methods does not carry weight in the evaluation.
